docs.title: Phase 8: deep-time genome structure (requested 2026-10-24)
docs.text:
Same rules as Phases 6-7 (clean-room from the papers, cited, never copied or named after the tools; tests with a known answer; validation on real genomes; docs page), plus: robust, fast (vectorised, linear or near-linear in genomes where the method allows) and benchmarked against the tools that inspired them.

# Feature Commands (planned) Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 8.1 Macrosynteny of distant genomes: chromosome-pair ortholog enrichment (one-sided Fisher, FDR), Oxford dot plots ordered by enrichment, ancestral linkage groups (given, or found de novo from co-occurrence across genomes), fusions, fissions and fusion-with-mixing per genome, mapped on the species tree macro test, macro algs, macro fusions, macro plot Simakov et al. 2020 Nat Ecol Evol; Simakov et al. 2022 Sci Adv; Schultz et al. 2023 Nature; CephChromosomes (Schmidbaur et al. 2022 Nat Commun) 8.2 Multi-genome microsynteny blocks (ortholog-anchored gene neighbourhoods), blocks dated as ancestral or novel at each node of the species tree, syntenic gene density against random blocks, density transitions along the tree Done 2026-10-25 (Leiden family groups, E-values, shuffle null; 98% of planted blocks recovered exactly, no false blocks, over 20 seeds). micro blocks, micro nodes, micro density Simakov et al. 2013 Nature; Zimmermann et al. 2019 Nat Ecol Evol; Robert et al. 2022 BMC Genomics 8.3 Conserved non-coding elements (CNEs) from genome alignments inside syntenic blocks (I/C window scan, exon and repeat masking, two-way merge, repeat filter), CNE density and genomic regulatory blocks (GRBs) with their target genes Done 2026-10-24 (one LAST run per genome pair inside syntenic blocks; Arabidopsis vs Brassica rapa in about 2 minutes). cne find, cne grb, cne plot Kikuta et al. 2007 Genome Res; Tan et al. 2019 PLoS Comput Biol (CNEr); Harmston et al. 2017 Nat Commun 8.4 Hierarchical orthologous groups (HOGs) at every node of the species tree, bottom-up from gene families by species overlap; ancestral gene adjacencies propagated over HOGs (bottom-up, top-down parsimony, linearisation, edge dating), feeding ancestral genomes Done 2026-10-24 (simulation with a WGD: HOG orthologs F1 0.998 with synteny vs 0.976 for OrthoFinder, 1.3 s vs 104 s; ancestral adjacencies precision ≥0.99 and recall ≥0.97 at every node). ortholog hogs, ancestral adjacencies Majidian et al. 2025 Nat Methods (FastOMA); Bernard et al. 2025 Nat Ecol Evol (EdgeHOG); Muffato et al. 2023 (AGORA) 8.5 Karyotype comparison: a known ancestral karyotype painted on genomes through synteny blocks (optionally the blocks of one Ks event), with copies; trajectories from the ancestor (EEJ, NCF, RCT, TRA, FIS, WGD) mapped onto the tree by Dollo, giving each ancestor's karyotype; the ancestral karyotype written as a genome. Done 2026-10-24. karyotype map, events, genome WGDI (Sun et al. 2022 Mol Plant); AKRUP; Wang et al. 2015 Plant Cell; Murat et al. 2017 Genome Biol

Done in the same session (2026-10-24): align many (one search for all pairs, CPU or MMseqs2-GPU), pipeline run --search/--gpu/--jobs, faster network build/cluster/tree, Leiden and Infomap, network stats/gainloss/compare (covers 7.4 and most of 7.19).

docs.title: Phase 9: whole-genome alignment, structural variation, introgression and pangenome views (requested 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
The owner asked for: the miscellaneous JCVI visualisation tools; SyRI- and DEEPSPACE-like analyses (DEEPSPACE by J. T. Lovell); whole-genome alignment tools; introgression tools such as KCFtools; similar whole-genome and pangenome comparison tools; a pipeline to see large structural variation and other pangenome features; and visualisation tools for comparing genomes and haplotypes. Supersedes Phase 7 items 7.7, 7.12 and the plotsr/pansyn part of 7.16. Clean-room, own command names, validated on real genomes.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 9.1 Whole-genome alignment wrapper and chaining (minimap2/LAST/AnchorWave-style anchors), PAF/MAF/SAM in, colinear chains out; annotation-free (DNA-level) synteny across many genomes Done 2026-10-25 (wga align, wga chain; Col-0 vs Ler-0 aligned in 51 s, 111 blocks). minimap2, LAST, AnchorWave, DEEPSPACE 9.2 Structural rearrangements between two assemblies: syntenic regions, inversions, translocations, duplications, not-aligned regions, plus SNPs/indels within syntenic regions (VCF + table) Done 2026-10-25 (sv call, sv plot; 90/90 planted SVs over 10 simulations, no false calls, SNP recall 99.1% with none wrong; Col-0 vs Ler-0 in 3 s: the known 1.17 Mb chr4 inversion recovered, 575k SNPs). SyRI (Goel et al. 2019) 9.3 Multi-genome/haplotype SV pipeline: chained pairwise calls along a genome order, pan-SV table (presence per genome), SV size spectra, core/variable genome in bp Done 2026-10-25 (sv pan, sv merge; six Arabidopsis assemblies in 10 min: 29,535 pan-SVs, 92.8 Mb core / 23.4 Mb variable; the chr4 inversion shared by all non-Col accessions and Sha's chr3 inversion recovered). SyRI, plotsr, pansyn, PGGB 9.4 Introgression scans: k-mer containment/identity of a query genome or reads in windows against donor references, introgressed blocks called by HMM-like segmentation, per-sample haplotype painting Done 2026-10-25 (introgress scan, introgress plot; FracMinHash k-mers, Viterbi segmentation, breakpoints refined to the sampled k-mer: simulated blocks recovered within 114 bp; Kyo painted by five accessions in 25 s and 1.9 GB). KCFtools, IBSpy, k-mer IBS methods 9.5 Genome and haplotype comparison viewers: stacked-chromosome rearrangement plot, haplotype painting along chromosomes, pairwise identity heatmaps in windows, interactive HTML browser of alignments and SVs Done 2026-10-25 (stacked plot sv plot, painting introgress plot, view identity (exact per-window identity from CIGAR, or k-mer estimate; five accessions vs Col-0 in 3.5 s), view matrix (containment ANI of six genomes in 15 s), view browse (self-contained canvas browser of alignments, SVs, pan-SVs, paintings, identity)). plotsr, NGenomeSyn, GENESPACE riparian, JCVI 9.6 Remaining JCVI miscellaneous graphics (graphics.* and misc plots not yet ported) JCVI graphics.* 9.7 Genetic-map-based rescaffolding (requested 2026-10-25): place, order and orient scaffolds by markers of one or more linkage maps, split chimeric scaffolds where markers of different linkage groups meet, report conflicts, write AGP and the new FASTA; fast (vectorised) and robust to marker errors (longest consistent marker chain per scaffold) Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold map: Ler-0 contigs with planted misjoins and two simulated maps (one reversed, renamed): all linkage groups and orders right, Spearman rho 1.00; pieces with under two markers cannot be oriented by maps and are reported) Chromonomer (Catchen J et al.), ALLMAPS (Tang H et al. 2015, Genome Biol 16:3) 9.8 Reference-guided scaffolding and correction (requested 2026-10-25): order and orient contigs by whole-genome alignment to one or more related references, break misjoins supported by the alignments, gap sizes from the reference, merge evidence of several references, AGP out; faster and more reliable than single-reference tools via the 9.1 chains and synteny-aware placement Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold ref: Ler-0 cut into 110 contigs with 6 planted misjoins, scaffolded on Col-0 in 5.5 s: exactly the 6 cuts, 109/109 joins right; RagTag 2.1.1 on the same input: 122 cuts, 128/153 joins right, 16 s) RagTag (Alonge M et al. 2022, Genome Biol 23:258) 9.9 Hi-C scaffolding, haplotype- and allele-aware (requested 2026-10-25): Hi-C pairs from SAM/BAM/.pairs (or reads mapped with bwa), binned contact counts, allele table from contig self-alignment or a monoploid reference, pruning of allelic and weak cross-allelic links, partition into chromosomes x ploidy groups with cannot-link constraints (autopolyploids up to octoploid, e.g. sugarcane), rescue of unplaced contigs, order and orientation by a distance-decay likelihood (greedy joins then local search), AGP and FASTA; reference-guided mode (contigs to chromosomes by alignment, Hi-C to separate haplotypes and order them); Hi-C misjoin correction; contact map figures (whole genome and per chromosome); Juicebox-like review (requested 2026-10-25): interactive contact map in the browser with scaffold/contig outlines, zoom, and manual curation (select, move, invert, cut, mark debris, undo) exporting the edited AGP and a Juicebox .assembly file; reading .assembly back to rebuild the FASTA Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold contacts, hic, hicmap, review, apply: simulated octoploid (4 chromosomes x 8 haplotypes) with half the cis contacts mis-mapped to alleles: all 32 haplotypes pure and correctly ordered with the allele table, purity 0.22 without; reference-guided polyploid mode; all planted misjoins found within 1 kb, no false cuts; homologs named and co-oriented; Juicebox-like review page with curation and .assembly export) ALLHiC (Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833), HapHiC (Zeng X et al. 2024, Nat Plants), YaHS (Zhou C et al. 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btac808), 3D-DNA (Dudchenko O et al. 2017, Science 356:92) 9.10 One scaffolding pipeline combining evidence: reference(s), genetic map(s) and Hi-C, with conflicts reported and the contact map / map-vs-assembly / synteny figures of the result Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold run: references, maps and Hi-C in one graph; Ler-0 with Col-0 and two maps: 6 cuts, 109/109 joins; simulated Hi-C + reference: 95/95 joins) ALLMAPS, RagTag, ALLHiC 9.11 Gene Ontology (requested 2026-10-25): OBO parser (is_a/part_of, alt ids, obsolete terms), annotations from GAF/GPAD/tables with true-path propagation, enrichment and depletion with Fisher exact tests and Bonferroni/Holm/Sidak/BH/BY corrections, GO-slim mapping, semantic similarity (Resnik/Lin), DAG and bubble plots; wired into MCscan3 gene sets: retained WGD duplicates and duplication modes, lineage-specific and core/dispensable pan-genes, HOGs gained or lost on a branch, genes in SVs, introgressed blocks, CNE/GRB targets, subgenome-dominant genes Done 2026-10-25 (go enrich, go sets, go slim, go similarity, pipeline step go; same counts and significant terms as GOATOOLS 1.6.7 on 37,573 Arabidopsis genes, 16x faster) GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872) 9.12 Chain-based liftover between assembly versions (requested 2026-10-25): base-level UCSC chains from wga align PAFs, lifting of BED, GFF3/GTF (whole gene models kept on one chain and strand, CDS frame checked on the new genome) and VCF (REF checked, minus-strand indels re-anchored, REF/ALT swapped with genotypes when the new reference carries the old ALT), unlifted records with reasons Done 2026-10-25 (annotate chain, annotate lift) transanno (Okada Y, Tang H), UCSC liftOver/CrossMap 9.13 Annotation-free synteny views (requested 2026-10-25): one genome cut into windows (1-5 kb) aligned to another, window hits chained into synteny blocks like gene anchors (distant/fast presets), per-pair dotplots of the windowed hits with block outlines, and a multi-genome riparian plot phased by a reference (blocks as braids, inversions highlighted, chromosomes ordered by synteny, daisy-chained genomes), with density tracks above Done 2026-10-25 (wga windows, wga riparian; Col-0/Ler-0/Cvi-0/Sha in about a minute per pair) DEEPSPACE (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/DEEPSPACE), GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526) 9.14 GFF3/GTF toolkit (requested 2026-10-25): format checking and repair (missing parents, IDs, phases, UTRs, gene/mRNA spans), GFF3/GTF/BED conversion, statistics (genes, transcripts, exons, introns, lengths, isoforms), longest isoform, filtering by type/attribute/length/ORF, sequence extraction (CDS, protein, exons, introns, UTRs, upstream/downstream), merging and deduplicating annotations, renaming IDs, intron/intergenic features, comparison of two annotations Done: gff fix/convert/stats/longest/filter/extract/merge/rename/add/compare; Arabidopsis TAIR10 GFF3 -> GTF -> GFF3 identical at every level, rice fix in 11 s AGAT (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3552717) 9.15 Gene ages (requested 2026-10-25; supersedes 7.13): proteome searched against a taxonomically wide database (DIAMOND/MMseqs2), hits mapped to taxonomy (NCBI taxdump), phylostrata as the oldest node with a homolog, taxonomic representativeness per stratum, homology-detection-failure test (expected bit-score decay with distance, abSENSE-like), synteny support from MCscan3 blocks to rescue or confirm young genes, gene-family ages, age per subgenome/duplicate class, figures GenEra (Barrera-Redondo J et al. 2023, Genome Biol 24:54), abSENSE (Weisman CM et al. 2020, PLoS Biol 18:e3000862), phylostratr (Arendsee Z et al. 2019, Bioinformatics 35:3617) 9.16 Synteny output formats chosen by the user (requested 2026-10-25): every block/anchor output writable as MCscan/JCVI .anchors (default), MCScanX .collinearity (+ .gff), WGDI collinearity/blockinfo, i-ADHoRe multiplicons, SynVisio input, GENESPACE-like syntenic hits and BED/BEDPE, via --out-format on the synteny commands and synteny convert between them. Done: synteny convert (anchors, mcscanx, wgdi, genespace (synHits and syntenicBlock_coordinates, checked with GENESPACE's read_synHits), iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv), --out-format on synteny scan/anchor and ortholog run, pipeline run --synteny-format; WGDI files checked against WGDI 0.75's readers MCScanX (Wang Y et al. 2012, NAR 40:e49), WGDI (Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841), i-ADHoRe 3.0 (Proost S et al. 2012, NAR 40:e11), SynVisio (Bandi V & Gutwin C 2020) 9.17 Phylotranscriptomics (requested 2026-10-25; needs 9.15 gene ages): transcriptome age index (TAI) and divergence index (TDI, from Ka/Ks of orthologues) across stages/tissues/conditions, flat-line, reductive hourglass, early- and late-conservation tests by permutation, contribution of each stratum, relative expression per stratum, gene-level age-expression profiles, with GO of the driving genes myTAI (Drost HG et al. 2018, Bioinformatics 34:1589; github.com/josuebarrera/myTAI), Domazet-Loso T & Tautz D 2010 (Nature 468:815) 9.18 Project files (requested 2026-10-25): every run writes <prefix>.mcscan3 (gzip tar: command, version, input checksums, outputs and compressed copies of them) and indexes it in the user cache; mcscan3 --cache restores an identical earlier run; project show/fetch/rerun/history. Done MCscan3 9.19 Expression (requested 2026-10-25): expr counts (featureCounts/htseq/Salmon/kallisto/RSEM to counts, TPM, CPM), expr de (genes ranked by Bayes factors with replicate consistency, reference-vs-reference controls and consistently inconsistent genes; values identical to the authors' bayexpress functions), expr homoeolog (homoeolog bias, subgenome dominance, bias changes between conditions; reads subgenome fractionation tables), expr pairs (expression correlation of duplicate/syntenic/ortholog pairs, tau); DE calls and bias categories feed go sets. Done Hoerbst F et al. 2025 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902; 10.1101/2025.01.20.633909), Ramírez-González RH et al. 2018 (Science 361:eaar6089), Yanai I et al. 2005 (Bioinformatics 21:650) 9.20 Genome track figures (requested 2026-10-25): view tracks --tracks FILE.ini --region chr:start-end -o result.pdf, pyGenomeTracks-style INI (genes, BED, bedGraph/bigWig, links, synteny between genome rows, x-axis, spacers) for microsynteny figures. Done: view tracks (genes from BED/GFF/GTF, BED, bedGraph, bigWig with pyBigWig, links, vlines, x-axis, spacers, per-track regions, synteny ribbons from anchors/BEDPE; --BED for many regions) pyGenomeTracks (Lopez-Delisle L et al. 2021, Bioinformatics 37:422)

docs.title: Phase 10: centromeres and telomeres (requested 2026-10-25; after Phase 9)
docs.text:
The owner asked to integrate centromere and telomere mining like quarTeT's CentroMiner (and TeloExplorer) once all earlier phases are finished. Clean-room, own command names, validated on telomere-to-telomere assemblies (e.g. Arabidopsis Col-CC, rice T2T).

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 10.1 Telomere detection: telomeric repeat arrays (known motif per clade or found de novo) at chromosome ends, length and completeness per end, T2T status of each chromosome quarTeT TeloExplorer (Lin Y et al. 2023, Hortic Res 10:uhad127) 10.2 Centromere candidates: tandem-repeat monomers (period finding, monomer clustering), satellite arrays along chromosomes, scored with TE density and gene density into a predicted centromere per chromosome quarTeT CentroMiner (Lin Y et al. 2023) 10.3 Integration: centromere/telomere tracks in karyotype, synteny and SV figures; centromere positions to classify fusions (EEJ vs NCF) and to mark pericentromeric SVs — 10.4 Genome landscapes (requested 2026-10-25): contigs, gaps and telomeres (present, incomplete or absent per end; interstitial arrays) from assemblies; sliding-window feature content (genes as CDS and introns, Ty3, Copia, other repeats, centromeric satellites, unknown) as stacked area plots along linearised chromosomes; classification of windows into arm, pericentromere and subtelomere by a classifier trained on the most centromere-like region of each chromosome, with probabilities; overlays on riparian plots geeViz (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/geeViz)

docs.title: Phase 11: transposable elements and subgenome phasing (requested 2026-10-25; started 2026-10-26, ahead of Phase 10)
docs.text: The owner asked for "a newer, more enhanced version of EDTA with a faster implementation, more sub-tools and more in-depth annotation, with TEsorter-like subclassification and insertion-time dating", followed by "SubPhaser-like" subgenome phasing with its figures. Native reimplementations (external tools optional), validated on Arabidopsis, rice and a polyploid (e.g. wheat or Brassica napus) against curated libraries.

docs.title: What goes wrong with EDTA, and what MCscan3 does instead (owner request 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
Moved ahead of Phase 10 on 2026-10-26 ("take EDTA, see what's wrong with it and not fast, integrate new tools and features, make it a world-class detailed repeat annotation, with TEsorter-like things"). From the EDTA README and issue tracker (about 600 closed issues):

Problem with EDTA MCscan3 te About 20 external programs (TIR-Learner with a deep-learning model, HelitronScanner in Java, RepeatModeler, AnnoSINE, LTR_FINDER, LTRharvest, LTR_retriever, RepeatMasker, cd-hit, mdust...); versions break each other (pandas 2, TIR-Learner 4, containers) native discovery of every order (C kernels with pure-Python fallbacks); only HMMER and BLAST/minimap2 needed; external finders optional, as extra evidence Slow steps: TIR-Learner and RepeatModeler run for days on large genomes; whole-genome RepeatMasker k-mer seeded search per chromosome in parallel; library masking split by chromosome; every step cached and resumable Fragile input: sequence names of 13-15 characters at most, failures on large single chromosomes, empty-file and "not found" crashes, silent "no SINE found" stops names mapped internally; any size; every step writes its result (even empty) and the run report says what each step found Inconsistent outputs (intact FASTA, GFF3 and library disagree; superfamily labels lost on reruns) one table of elements from which GFF3, FASTA, library and figures are all written Many "unknown" LTR elements; classification only to superfamily (TEsorter optional) REXdb domain classification to clade built in (Ty1/copia and Ty3/gypsy clades, LINE clades, TIR transposases), with domain order and completeness Helitron false positives; gene fragments in the library hairpin and end-motif scoring for Helitrons; protein-domain and CDS filters for gene fragments; tandem-repeat filter Little analysis after annotation insertion times (K2P, per clade), solo:intact ratios, LAI along chromosomes, Kimura landscapes, density along chromosomes, TE-gene distances, TEs near SVs and in synteny gaps, benchmark against curated libraries

Commands (mcscan3 te ...): ltr, tir, helitron, nonltr (LINE/SINE), tandem, classify, library, annotate (homology masking, fragments, Kimura divergence), age, lai, landscape (figures), bench (against a curated library: sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 per superfamily and a confusion matrix), and run (all of them, resumable).

Build order: 11.1 LTR (kernel, intact elements, TSD/motif/PBS/PPT, identity and age) -> 11.3 REXdb classification -> 11.1 TIR/MITE, Helitron, LINE/SINE, tandem -> 11.2 library and genome annotation -> 11.4 ages, LAI, landscapes -> te run and te bench -> 11.5 phasing.

First head-to-head (2026-10-26, simulated 3.9 Mb genome with 80 intact LTR elements, 8 nested, solo LTRs, truncated copies, tandem duplications and satellites): te ltr found 80/80 with exact boundaries and no false calls in 3 s (4 CPUs); EDTA's LTR module (LTRharvest + LTR_FINDER_parallel + LTR_retriever, 4 CPUs, osx-64 build) found 45/80, no false calls, in 441 s. It missed all 11 elements below 92% LTR identity, 9 of 12 hosts broken by later insertions and 4 of 8 nested ones.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 11.1 Structural TE discovery, natively and fast: LTR retrotransposons (paired LTRs with TSDs, PBS/PPT; candidate pairs from k-mer seeds), TIR elements (terminal inverted repeats with superfamily TSD lengths), Helitrons (5'TC/3'CTRR ends and hairpin), non-LTR LINE/SINE (poly-A tails, target-site duplications), MITEs; optional wrappers of LTR_FINDER/LTRharvest/TIR-Learner/HelitronScanner EDTA (Ou S et al. 2019, Genome Biol 20:275), LTR_retriever, LTRharvest, TIR-Learner, HelitronScanner 11.2 Library curation: filtering of false positives (gene fragments, tandem repeats, nested elements), clustering to families (80-80-80 rule), whole-genome masking with the library, homology-based annotation of fragments; LTR Assembly Index EDTA, LTR_retriever LAI (Ou S et al. 2018, NAR 46:e126) 11.3 Domain-based classification to clade (TEsorter-like): REXdb protein domain profiles (GAG, PROT, RT, RH, INT, CHD...), domain order, clade calls (Ty1/copia: Ale, Angela, Bianca, Ikeros, Ivana, SIRE, Tork...; Ty3/gypsy: Athila, CRM, Galadriel, Reina, Tekay, Retand...), plus TIR superfamilies and Helitrons TEsorter (Zhang RG et al. 2022, Hortic Res 9:uhac017), REXdb (Neumann P et al. 2019, Mob DNA 10:1) 11.3b te classify as an evidence ensemble (owner request 2026-10-26, "something like Terrier, or a better way"): (1) structure from the finders (LTR motif/TSD/PBS/PPT; TIR terminal motifs and TSD length per superfamily: DTA 8 bp, DTC CACTA and 3 bp, DTH TWA and 3 bp, DTM 9-11 bp, DTT TA; Helitron TC...CTRR and hairpin; LINE/SINE poly-A, Pol III boxes), (2) protein domains (REXdb clades, Pfam/transposase families) with domain order, (3) homology to curated open families (Dfam curated, CC0; user libraries), (4) a hierarchical k-mer/convolutional classifier trained on open curated families (Dfam curated; Repbase only when the user has it), with the class tree and a confidence threshold per level that falls back to the parent (order instead of superfamily) when unsure; optional Terrier or TEsorter runs as extra votes. The calls are combined per level with their evidence and a calibrated probability; disagreements are reported. Benchmarked on held-out families (rice, fruit fly, human, mouse; the Terrier/TEclass2 test sets) against Terrier, TEsorter, DeepTE and the RepeatModeler classifier Terrier (Turnbull R et al. 2025, Brief Bioinform 26:bbaf442), TEsorter, TEclass2, DeepTE, Dfam (Storer J et al. 2021 Mob DNA 12:2) 11.4 Insertion-time dating of intact LTR elements (5'/3' LTR divergence, K2P, substitution rate per clade/species), age distributions per clade, solo-LTR to intact ratios, TE landscapes (Kimura divergence) LTR_retriever, RepeatMasker landscapes 11.5 Subgenome phasing of polyploids from differential k-mers (subgenome-specific k-mers enriched on homoeologous chromosome sets), k-means/hierarchical assignment with bootstrap support, LTR insertions carrying the k-mers dated to time the divergence of progenitors and the polyploidisation, combined with MCscan3 synteny and subgenome dominance; figures: k-mer heatmap and clustering, chromosome painting by subgenome, insertion-time histograms per subgenome, circos SubPhaser (Jia KH et al. 2022, New Phytol 235:801) 11.7 Insertion history (owner request 2026-10-26: "when and where they were inserted, nested insertion"): ages of intact LTR elements (K2P of the two LTRs, rate per species), nested insertions (elements inside other elements, inside their LTRs or internal region) resolved into nesting trees and a relative chronology (an inner element is younger than its host; checks the molecular ages), insertion sites (chromosome region: arm, pericentromere, centromere; distance to genes, intron/promoter/intergenic; target-site duplication motifs and hotspots), and dating against the species tree with MCscan3 synteny: an insertion present at the orthologous position in a related genome is older than their split, absent means younger (insertions placed on branches); figures: age histograms per clade, nesting trees, insertion maps along chromosomes, insertions on the species tree LTR_retriever (dating), TE-nest/TEnest (SanMiguel P et al. 1996 Science 274:765 for nested LTR dating), MCscan3 synteny 11.8 Speed, plots and browsers (owner request 2026-10-26): every step parallel over chromosome chunks (processes; C kernels release the GIL) and cached; GPU when available for the neural classifier and k-mer counting (CUDA or Apple MPS through PyTorch/CuPy when installed, CPU otherwise, same results); a plotting suite (genome composition by order and superfamily, length and age distributions per clade, Kimura landscapes, density along chromosomes and ideograms, nesting trees, LAI along chromosomes, element structure diagrams with domains, insertion maps on the species tree); genome browser output for everything MCscan3 writes: JBrowse 2 configuration (bgzipped and indexed GFF3/BED, BigWig densities, synteny tracks), IGV sessions, UCSC track hubs, and the MCscan3 viewer JBrowse 2 (Diesh C et al. 2023 Genome Biol 24:74), IGV, UCSC track hubs 11.6 Integration: TE tracks in karyotype, synteny, SV, centromere (Phase 10) and browser views; TE-mediated SVs; GO of TE-associated genes —

docs.title: Phase 12: block expression, phylogenomics, orthogroup QC and biosynthetic gene clusters (requested 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
The owner asked for: the useful parts of the metazoan synteny/expression code (Zimmermann et al.); "busco_phylogenomics integrated, better, faster and optimised, with tree plotting modules"; cogeqc-like quality checks and orthobrowser-like views of OrthoFinder results; and "a plantiSMASH-like package that uses hmmscan/pfamscan and synteny to find biosynthetic gene clusters", integrated with RNA-seq co-expression and comparative genomics. Native implementations (HMMER/MAFFT/trimming/tree builders optional), clean-room from the papers and docs.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 12.1 pan run: gene-based and sequence-based (FracMinHash) pan-genome, classes, curves, Heaps' law, similarity (done 2026-10-26) GENESPACE, Mash, FracMinHash, Tettelin 2008 12.2 (done 2026-10-26) micro coexpr: co-expression of the genes of microsynteny blocks across tissues/cell types against shuffled, sampled and sampled-ortholog random blocks (Fisher-z mean correlation, empirical P), tau specificity and cell-type bias per block, paralog content of blocks, intervening-gene gaps with a negative binomial fit Zimmermann B et al. (2019) Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289 (metazoan_synteny code) 12.3 (done 2026-10-26) phylo busco: BUSCO (or compleasm/MCscan3 single-copy) results of many genomes -> shared single-copy sets with occupancy threshold -> parallel alignment (MAFFT or native), trimming, supermatrix with partitions and gene trees -> concatenated ML (IQ-TREE/FastTree optional) and coalescent summary (native ASTRAL-like quartet support), concordance factors; cached and parallel BUSCO_phylogenomics (McGowan J), ASTRAL, gCF/sCF 12.4 (done 2026-10-26) plot phylo tree figures (ete3-like features natively in matplotlib): rectangular/circular/unrooted layouts, support and concordance pie charts, clade highlight, aligned heatmaps/bars (BUSCO completeness, genome size, gene counts, pan classes), tanglegrams of two trees ete3 (Huerta-Cepas J et al. 2016 Mol Biol Evol 33:1635) 12.5 (done 2026-10-26) ortholog qc: orthogroup statistics and figures from OrthoFinder or MCscan3 groups (per-species assignment, species overlap, size distributions, duplications per node), domain-aware homogeneity and dispersal scores with Pfam, BUSCO summary and assembly/annotation statistics comparison cogeqc (Almeida-Silva F & Van de Peer Y, Bioconductor) 12.6 ortholog browse: interactive HTML browser of an orthogroup: gene tree, domain architecture, the synteny neighbourhood of every member, expression orthobrowser (Salk TM, GitLab) 12.7 bgc find: biosynthetic gene clusters: Pfam domains (hmmscan/pyhmmer or native) -> signature enzyme rules per class (terpene, triterpene/saponin, alkaloid, polyketide, saccharide, lignan, cyanogenic glycoside, NRPS/PKS for fungi and bacteria...) -> clusters of co-located signature and tailoring enzymes with gap rules, scored against random genomic windows; plant, fungal and bacterial rule sets plantiSMASH (Kautsar SA et al. 2017 NAR 45:W55), antiSMASH (Blin K et al. 2023 NAR 51:W46) 12.8 BGC evidence integration: co-expression of cluster genes from RNA-seq (expr), conservation of clusters across genomes from MCscan3 synteny (present, partial, rearranged, absent), tandem duplication and pan-genome class of cluster genes, cluster families across genomes (domain-content and synteny similarity), figures (cluster maps with domains, comparative cluster ribbons, co-expression heatmaps, presence on a species tree) and an HTML report per cluster plantiSMASH CoExpress, BiG-SCAPE (Navarro-Muñoz JC et al. 2020 Nat Chem Biol 16:60) 12.9 expr coexp: genes co-expressed with bait genes (Spearman/Pearson, r and P cutoffs, BH, minimum expression, number of baits each gene is co-expressed with), bait network and heatmap; expr qc: sample filtering (share of expression on the top 100 genes, read counts, sample-correlation outliers, block list) CoExp (Pucker B, GitHub bpucker/CoExp) 12.10 expr conserved: co-expression conserved across species: baits per species, co-expressed genes grouped by MCscan3 orthogroups or synteny (or protein clustering), gene trees with co-expressed tips highlighted (MCscan3 tree figures), clusters where co-expressed genes of several species fall together CoExpPhylo (Pucker B et al., GitHub bpucker/CoExpPhylo) 12.11 Read coverage: genome-wide coverage plots of resequencing data (binned, saturated, normalised to the genome average, region zoom) from samtools depth/mosdepth/bedGraph; coverage-based gene presence/absence and zero-coverage regions between samples GKseq2, PAV_finder (Pucker B, GitHub bpucker/GKseq2, PBBtools) 12.12 Utilities: masking monophyletic same-species tips in gene trees; tblastn check for genes missing from an annotation; expression plots of gene sets with outlier filtering PBBtools (Pucker B)

docs.title: Phase 13: regions, local copy number and haplotypes in the pan-genome (requested 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
The owner asked for what GENESPACE gives for a region (QTL intervals traced through the riparian plot, presence/absence and copy number of the pan-genes in a syntenic region) and more: local copy-number variation, structural and haplotype variation in the same view, and a pan-genome that has not been studied this way as the case study. GENESPACE has query_pangenes/query_cnv with a BED of positional bounds and highlightBed (whole chromosomes) in plot_riparian.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 13.1 plot riparian --highlight regions.bed: intervals on any genome (QTL, loci) traced through the anchors into every genome and drawn as coloured braids over grey synteny; --region genome:chr:start-end draws only the syntenic region (with flanks) in every genome, on gene ranks or base pairs GENESPACE plot_riparian (Lovell JT et al. 2022 eLife 11:e78526) 13.2 pan region: regions on one genome -> syntenic intervals in every genome (anchors and flanking-anchor interpolation) -> pan-gene matrix of the region: presence/absence, copy number, tandem arrays, order and orientation per genome; table, copy-number heatmap along the reference, locus figure GENESPACE query_pangenes / query_cnv 13.3 pan cnv: genome-wide windows of pan-genes: presence/absence and copy-number variability per window, hotspots against permuted windows, tracks along chromosomes for every genome, overlap with QTL — 13.4 pan haplotype: per region, genomes grouped into haplotypes by gene content, copy number, gene order (inversions) and SVs (sv merge); haplotype map (dendrogram, matrix, ribbons) and, with a phenotype table, association of haplotypes with traits — 13.5 QTL candidate ranking: genes of a QTL scored by presence/absence, copy number, SV overlap, haplotype-trait association, expression and GO; HTML report per QTL — 13.6 Case study: a taxon with public chromosome-level annotated assemblies but no published joint pan-genome, analysed end to end with 13.1-13.5 —

docs.title: Phase 14: graph pan-genomes and the distinct features of pangenome and genome-visualisation tools (requested 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
The owner asked that every distinct feature of the tools in the awesome-pangenomes list (github.com/colindaven/awesome-pangenomes) and useful plots of the awesome-genome-visualization list (cmdcolin.github.io/awesome-genome-visualization, e.g. BUSCO synteny plots) be captured, using the established tools as engines where they are more robust than a reimplementation (wrapped when installed, with MCscan3 turning their output into tables, variants and figures). Each row below is one tool's distinct feature and how MCscan3 covers it.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 14.1 pan graph: graph built and genotyped by minigraph (PanSN renaming so same-named contigs stay apart), bubbles typed INS/DEL/INV/CPX, each assembly written as walks (paths.gfa, readable by odgi, panacus, vg, Bandage), core/softcore/shell/private segments, exact growth curves, multi-sample VCF with allele traversals, diversity windows Done 2026-11-05 (simulated insertion, deletion, inversion and private insertion all recovered with correct genotypes; growth identical to panacus) minigraph, gfatools bubble, mgutils merge2vcf, panacus, Pansel 14.2 Graph analysis of any GFA with paths (PGGB, Minigraph-Cactus): classes, growth, similarity; vg deconstruct VCF and gfatools stat when installed; GFA validation (steps on unknown segments, steps without a link) Done 2026-11-05 PGGB, Minigraph-Cactus, vg deconstruct, gfatools, gretl, odgi validate 14.3 Association markers from bubble alleles (--plink) Done 2026-11-05 gfa2bin 14.4 Genome similarity on the graph (bp-weighted Jaccard) Done 2026-11-05 odgi similarity 14.5 Linear pan-reference: reference plus non-reference segments (--pan-reference) Done 2026-11-05 PSVCP 14.6 Region subgraph, sequences of every path and a tube map (--region) Done 2026-11-05; odgi viz of all paths when installed impg, odgi extract/viz, SequenceTubeMap, ggtubemap 14.7 Reference genes traced through the graph: share of each gene present in every genome (--gff) Done 2026-11-05 GrAnnoT, APAV 14.8 te tips: TE insertion polymorphisms from bubble alleles: gained sequence masked with the library, family, carriers, frequency, divergence Done 2026-11-05 (5/5 simulated sites, correct families and carriers) GraffeTE, Pantera 14.9 pan kmer: k-mer conservation along each genome (how many genomes share each k-mer), conserved and private blocks, tracks Panagram, PanKmer, MEMO 14.10 Gene graph: pan-genes as nodes and adjacencies as edges, exported as GFA from pan genes; regions of genomic plasticity (runs of non-core genes) pangene, PPanGGOLiN, Panaroo 14.11 Graph quality: share of each assembly's unique k-mers spelled by its walks PG-SCunK 14.12 Short-read genotyping against the graph when vg or PanGenie is installed (genotypes of the bubbles per sample) vg giraffe/call, PanGenie, Varigraph 14.13 Comparison of two graphs of the same genomes (segmentation boundaries along each path) rs-pancat-compare, junctions 14.14 Multi-genome maximal unique matches and their colinear blocks drawn across genomes Mumemto, Chromatiblock 14.15 plot busco: synteny of BUSCO genes between genomes (dot plots, chromosome painting across many genomes) from BUSCO tables alone ChromSyn, BUSCO-based Oxford plots — Done 14.16 view selfid: self-identity heatmap of a region (satellites, centromeres) from k-mer identity of windows, linked to centromere find ModDotPlot, StainedGlass 14.17 sv plot data tracks: gene, TE, SV density, bedGraph signals and highlighted regions under the genome rows plotsr, SVbyEye

Out of scope (reads to graph for RNA-seq or methylation, metagenome binning, microbial-only HGT graphs, TB-scale indexes): pantas, rpvg, PanGraphRNA, methylGrapher, Pantax, Kente, ropebwt3, TeraTools. Already covered elsewhere: dot plots, Oxford plots, riparian and multi-genome synteny, circos, gene-cluster comparison (plot locus), identity heatmaps (view identity/matrix).

Promoter analysis (requested 2026-11-05 after the PlantPAN 5 stand-alone release, which has no licence: it is run as the user's own Docker image, never copied):

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 14.18 promoter scan: promoters around the transcription start, clipped at neighbouring genes; binding sites from JASPAR (any taxon), own libraries (MEME, JASPAR, TRANSFAC, HOMER) or PlantPAN 5; FIMO when installed or a native scanner with exact p-values (same sites as FIMO on the tests, 10x faster), CUDA through CuPy Done 2026-11-06 FIMO, JASPAR, PlantPAN 14.19 promoter compare: promoter divergence of syntenic orthologs, duplicates (by mode) and homoeologs against random pairs, with Ks, and asymmetric retention of families between the two copies Done 2026-11-06 — 14.20 promoter enrich: families enriched or depleted in gene sets (Fisher, BH) Done 2026-11-06 — 14.21 macro ancestors: ancestral karyotypes at every node of a species tree from BUSCO tables, fissions/fusions/reciprocal translocations per branch; karyotype tree, branch flows, linkage-group fate matrix and rate figures; plot busco --algs; phylo busco --synteny Done 2026-11-06 syngraph

docs.title: Phase 15 — a new genome to publication figures (genome group)
docs.text:
Requested 2026-11-06: an automated path from a newly sequenced genome to publication figures, after the JCVI wiki pages Miscellaneous plotting, Genome diversity and Genome build, improved, plus circos and other figure types.

# Command What Status 15.1 genome stats contiguity (N50, auN, NG50, Nx curves of scaffolds and contigs), gaps, GC, soft-masking, telomeres (motif detected), T2T chromosomes; several assemblies compared Done 2026-11-06 15.2 genome landscape windows of genes, exons, repeats by class, GC, tandem repeats; stack plots of the genome and heatmap ideograms per chromosome Done 2026-11-06 15.3 genome circos one genome as a circos: chromosomes with centromeres and telomeres, density tracks, paralogous synteny links Done 2026-11-06 15.4 genome survey k-mer histogram model: genome size, heterozygosity, repeats, ploidy Done 2026-11-06 15.5 genome depth read-depth (mosdepth) copy-number panels of several samples, segments Done 2026-11-06 15.6 genome pedigree pedigree drawing, founder contributions, inbreeding coefficients (any ploidy) Done 2026-11-06 15.7 genome ldmap genetic-map LD heatmap; discontinuities flag misassemblies Done 2026-11-06 15.8 genome report everything above from a FASTA (+ optional GFF, repeats, reads, Hi-C, reference), composed figures and HTML report Done 2026-11-06 15.9 go treemap multi-dataset GO treemaps: GOGO clusters named by their lowest common ancestor, colour-blind families Done 2026-11-06 15.10 network cluster --device MCL on the GPU (PyTorch cuda/mps or CuPy): components batched into dense matrix products Done 2026-11-06 15.11 wgd ploidy copies made by the last WGD from syntenic depth: logistic regression trained on simulated polyploids Done 2026-11-06

docs.title: Phase 16: biosynthetic gene clusters, figure export, AI agents and clusters (requested 2026-11-06)
docs.text:
The owner asked for a biosynthetic gene cluster pipeline in the spirit of BiG-MAP (Pascal Andreu V et al. 2021, mSystems 6:e00937-21) coupled with multi-species microsynteny; dark, transparent and high-resolution export of every figure; MCscan3 usable by AI agents (Claude, Codex...) that run the commands, interpret the results and tailor figures; batch-cluster scripts and an interactive mode.

# Feature Status 16.1 Global figure export: --plot-theme dark, --background, --transparent, --formats, --plot-dpi, --plot-font, --font-scale, --palette, editable vector text (every figure) Done 2026-11-06 16.2 bgc find: Pfam domains -> enzyme functions and class signatures -> co-located clusters, shuffled-genome chance, co-expression Done 2026-11-06 16.3 bgc synteny: every cluster traced through the anchors to other genomes (conserved, partial, remnant, region only, no synteny), origin on the species tree, microsynteny figure by enzyme function Done 2026-11-06 16.4 bgc family: cluster families across genomes (domain content and order + DIAMOND identity, average linkage, representatives), syntenic (positional) or not Done 16.5 bgc map: reads mapped to the clusters (minimap2) or a count matrix, RPKM and coverage per sample, family representatives, hurdle / Kruskal-Wallis tests with BH q, heatmap + volcano Done 16.6 bgc run: find, families, synteny and map from a directory of genomes, with an HTML report queued 16.7 subgenome circos: subgenome painting, specific k-mer and LTR densities and homoeolog links in one circos queued 16.8 AI agents: machine-readable command catalogue, MCP server, agent guide (AGENTS.md / skills), result summaries for interpretation, figure specs agents can edit and redraw queued 16.9 Clusters and sessions: --sbatch job scripts (SLURM, PBS), interactive mode queued 16.10 wgd rates: ksrates-style rate adjustment of every speciation against the focal genome from the species tree (all trios, mean over outgroups), adjustment table, rate-adjusted mixed paralog-ortholog Ks plot and a Ks-unit phylogram (after Sensalari, Maere & Lohaus, ksrates; GPL-3, clean-room) queued 16.11 wgd hdr: credible Ks ranges of WGD components for dating (lognormal CI and highest density region per mixture component of segment-guided anchor Ks, k-medoids alternative) and the anchor pairs inside them (after wgd v2 peak, Chen, Zwaenepoel & Van de Peer 2024 Bioinformatics btae272) queued 16.12 wgd date: absolute dating of a WGD: orthogroups of the anchor pairs inside the HDR with single-copy genes of other species, MAFFT alignment, concatenation, MCMCtree/BEAST/r8s inputs with fossil calibrations (run when installed), and a quick rate-based date (Ks / 2r) with intervals (after wgd v2 focus --dating) Partly done 2026-11-14: wgd date with bracketing, calibrated-rate dates, gene quartets and concordance; MCMCtree/LSD2 phylogenomic dating still queued 16.13 wgd retention: retention and loss between consecutive WGDs from reconciled gene trees, P(R R) and P(L 16.14 bench genetrees: gene trees simulated on a species tree with WGDs, small-scale duplications and losses (after wgdtree sim), to benchmark wgd tree-map and wgd retention queued

docs.title: JCVI source version
docs.text:
MCscan3 is derived from the following JCVI release. Every derived file carries a # Derived from JCVI <path> (BSD license), commit <hash> header that refers to this commit.

Item Value Repository https://github.com/tanghaibao/jcvi Release tag v1.6.7 Commit e10b8844a7539bad0a9de31f2bfe93b3c4fbd29c Commit date 2026-09-02 License BSD-3-Clause (see LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY) Local reference copy vendor/jcvi (gitignored, never imported by mcscan3) Golden-output environment .venv-jcvi (Python 3.12, Biopython 1.88, pip install ./vendor/jcvi, compiled cblast, pygraphviz 2.0.2) Legacy golden environment .venv-jcvi-legacy (Python 3.10, Biopython 1.78) for ks calc and apps.phylo, which call Biopython APIs removed in 1.79+

The main branch was at a44fa61b52639a54b5ecc096d1407d2eca8fcc8f (2026-09-18) when cloned; we deliberately use the latest release tag instead.

docs.title: External tools used for golden outputs
docs.text:
Installed in a project-local bioconda environment .tools/ (gitignored), not system-wide.

Tool Version Used by LAST (lastdb, lastal) 1654 (bioconda) align last, ortholog run DIAMOND 2.2.8 (bioconda) align diamond BLAST+ 2.17.0+ (Homebrew, pre-installed) align blast GLPK (glpsol) 5.0 (bioconda) quota align fallback solver OR-Tools (SCIP backend) 9.15.6755 (PyPI, in .venv-jcvi) quota align default solver ClustalW2 2.1, MUSCLE 3.8.1551, pal2nal 14.1, PAML 4.10.10 (yn00) bioconda ks calc, phylo prepare PhyML 3.3.20260528, RAxML 8.2.12, Gblocks 0.91b bioconda phylo build R + ggplot2 Homebrew (pre-installed) JCVI graphics.histogram (golden only) bedtools 2.31.1 (bioconda) fractionation validate/gaps/gff-select (intersectBed) Graphviz 14.1.2 (conda-forge) pygraphviz for ancestral adjgraph CLUSTER 3.0 (command line) C Clustering Library 1.59, built from source into .tools/cluster3/ (graphviz also ships a cluster binary) pad cluster EMBOSS PHYLIP (fdnadist/fneighbor), TreeFix not available for osx-arm64 phylo build (NJ tree, TreeFix steps) gmm-bic not packaged anywhere ks report --fit

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Every plot command takes the same image options: --figsize, --dpi, --format (pdf, png, svg, ...), --font, --style (axes background), --cmap, --diverge, --seed (random colours) and --theme.

  • --theme mcscan3 (the default) is the MCscan3 house style. It uses white panels without a grid and a restrained frame. Colours named by letter in the plots (b, g, r, m, y, c, k) are drawn from the colour-blind-safe Okabe–Ito palette, the default colour map is viridis, and figures drawn on a blank canvas are cropped to their content.
  • --theme classic reproduces the original figures. PNGs are pixel-identical to the originals, and SVG and PDF are identical apart from their metadata. Set MCSCAN3_THEME=classic to make it the default for every command.
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --theme mcscan3 --format png

Every saved figure records Creator: MCscan3 <version> in its metadata (PNG, PDF and SVG). Nothing is added to the visible image.

docs.title: Dark, transparent and high-resolution export (every figure)
docs.text:
Options given before the command apply to every figure the command writes: the figures that are new in MCscan3, the ported ones and the figures of the pipelines and reports. They can also be set in the environment, which works for the Python API and the desktop app too.

option environment effect --plot-theme dark MCSCAN3_PLOT_THEME black background: text, rules and grey fills inverted, data colours kept (dark ones lifted for contrast), greyscale heatmaps flipped --background COLOUR MCSCAN3_BACKGROUND background of the dark theme (#111827, navy...; default black) --transparent MCSCAN3_TRANSPARENT=1 no background in PNG, PDF, SVG, TIFF and WebP (EPS and JPEG have no transparency) --formats png,svg,tiff MCSCAN3_FORMATS more formats written beside every figure: png, pdf, svg, eps, ps, tiff (LZW), jpg, webp --plot-dpi 600 MCSCAN3_DPI resolution of raster formats, over each command's --dpi --plot-font Arial MCSCAN3_FONT font of every text in the figure --font-scale 1.3 MCSCAN3_FONT_SCALE every text 30% larger (posters, slides) --palette tol MCSCAN3_PALETTE categorical colours of the MCscan3 figures: okabe (default), tol, bright, dark2 (all colour-blind aware), grey

Text stays editable in vector formats: fonts are embedded as TrueType in PDF and EPS, and SVG keeps text as text, so figures can be finished in Illustrator or Inkscape.

# slides: black background, PNG at 300 dpi and SVG
mcscan3 --plot-theme dark --formats svg --plot-dpi 300 genome report asm.fa -o report

# a journal: 600 dpi TIFF and editable PDF of every figure of a run
mcscan3 --formats tiff,pdf --plot-dpi 600 --plot-font Arial pipeline run genomes/ -o run

# overlays: transparent background, light text for dark slides
mcscan3 --plot-theme dark --transparent wgd ploidy grape.poplar.anchors --ref-bed grape.bed --bed poplar.bed -o poplar

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot gallery renders every plot from the test data into one HTML page for review. Each figure is shown in both themes, next to the reference image of the original tool:

mcscan3 plot gallery --tests-dir=tests -o gallery     # then open gallery/index.html
mcscan3 plot gallery --only dotplot --only karyotype  # a subset

The command needs a source checkout (it reads tests/golden and tests/data). It exits with status 1 if any figure fails to render; the error is shown on the page.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: Every figure on this page comes from one run of mcscan3 pipeline run on six flowering-plant genomes: Amborella trichopoda, Arabidopsis thaliana, grape, peach, poplar and soybean (209,882 genes in all). They were regenerated with python tools/make_docs_gallery.py <run>. Click a figure to open it full size.

docs.title: Interactive dot plot
docs.text:
Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a chromosome name to zoom to it, and hover over a dot to see its two genes. Dots are coloured by Orthology Index: blue and orange blocks are orthologous synteny (forward and inverted), and grey blocks come from older duplications. Open it on its own page.

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.lifted.anchors --oi grape.peach.oi -o grape.peach.html

docs.title: Synteny
docs.text: Dot plot of grape vs peach: peach chromosomes are ordered and flipped along grape, and older duplications are grey. plot dotplot --theme mcscan3 --oi Soybean against itself: the two recent WGDs make every region appear about four times. 125 unplaced scaffolds are hidden. plot dotplot --theme mcscan3 Riparian plot: syntenic orthologous blocks between neighbouring genomes, coloured by the grape chromosome they descend from. plot riparian, pan genes

docs.title: Flexible layouts
docs.text:
Every macrosynteny figure can be reshaped from the command line: chromosomes chosen, ordered, flipped and zoomed by hand, blocks merged into a macrosynteny view, genomes drawn to one base-pair scale, and microsynteny genes, links, names and alignment styled freely. See plotting and themes for every option.

Microsynteny, styled: two genes coloured with a legend, their links in the same colour, tracks renamed and every track shifted so the red gene lines up. plot microsynteny --gene-colors genes.tsv --track-labels Grape,Peach,"Poplar copy 1","Poplar copy 2" --align-gene Vitis05g00810.t01 --link-alpha 0.6

Microsynteny, left-aligned: tracks start on one line, one gene highlighted, pale links. plot microsynteny --align left --highlight Vitis05g00810.t01 --link-color "#cfd8e3"

Zoom on chromosomes: grape 14 against the poplar chromosomes it shares blocks with, poplar 5 reversed. plot dotplot --qorder 14 --sorder 2,14,5-

Chromosome painting: poplar chromosomes to base-pair scale, each block painted by the grape chromosome it comes from. plot painting

Riparian plot on one base-pair scale, rows centred, nearby blocks of the same chromosome pair merged into one braid; reversed chromosomes carry a minus. plot riparian --basepair --merge-gap 25 --min-block 20

Karyotype tracks to scale: grape and poplar drawn with one base-pair scale and centred, so chromosome lengths compare between the genomes. plot karyotype --genomes grape,poplar --basepair (--fill: full width)

docs.title: Whole-genome duplications
docs.text: Ks of duplicated blocks in soybean, with a log-normal mixture: the peaks at Ks 0.15 and 0.65 are the two soybean WGDs. wgd blocks, wgd mix --plot Ks of several genomes as ridges, fitted peaks labelled once where they agree. wgd compare WGDs on the species tree: the γ triplication, Arabidopsis α and β, two soybean WGDs and the salicoid WGD, each placed where block ratio, quota ratio, Ks peaks and the gene trees of its syntenic paralogs agree. Circles are shaded by the number of agreeing lines of evidence; the table gives each one. wgd consensus --label grape="Vitis vinifera"

docs.title: Ancestral genomes
docs.text: Karyotype evolution on the species tree, ancestor at the top: ancestral chromosomes (colours) traced through every reconstructed ancestor to the extant genomes, clades on pastel regions, WGDs as red circles, and each branch's rearrangements drawn as inputs → outputs (end-end joins EEJ, nested fusions NCF, reciprocal translocations RCT, fissions FIS). ancestral tree-karyotype --clade Rosids=ath,poplar,peach,soybean --label ath="Arabidopsis thaliana" One ancestor painted on every genome. ancestral karyotype Fusions, fissions, translocations and duplications on each branch. ancestral tree-karyotype

docs.title: Many genomes
docs.text: Synteny similarity between genomes, raw (lower) and corrected for phylogenetic distance (upper). network plot Phylogenomic profile: presence of the largest syntenic clusters in each genome. network plot

docs.title: The pipeline report
docs.text:
The report of pipeline run: an interactive dot plot of every pair of genomes, plus pan-genes, ancestral karyotypes, duplicate classes and WGDs. See the report.

Two styles

Every figure on this page uses the MCscan3 house style, the default. Pass --theme classic to draw the commands ported from JCVI in the original style, pixel for pixel. See plotting and themes.

docs.title: Quick start: grape vs peach
docs.text:
This tutorial reproduces the classic MCscan tutorial (grape vs peach) with MCscan3 commands. Starting from genome annotations, you find syntenic blocks and draw them as a dot plot, a karyotype and a local synteny view.

The commands below run as written on the small test data in the MCscan3 repository (tests/data: grape chromosomes 6 and 8, peach chromosome 6, from Ensembl Plants). The test suite runs them (tests/test_tutorial.py), so they stay correct. With your own genomes, use your file names.

docs.title: 0. Install
docs.text:
pip install mcscan3              # add [phylo] for tree drawing
mamba install -c bioconda last   # the default aligner (lastal/lastdb)

docs.title: 1. Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Each genome needs a BED file of genes (one representative transcript per gene) and the matching CDS sequences, named <species>.bed and <species>.cds.

mcscan3 prep gff2bed grape.gff3.gz --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only -o grape.bed
mcscan3 prep gff2bed peach.gff3.gz --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only -o peach.bed
mcscan3 prep fasta-format grape.cds.fa.gz grape.cds
mcscan3 prep fasta-format peach.cds.fa.gz peach.cds

--key names the GFF attribute that matches the FASTA headers. For Ensembl this is transcript_id; for Phytozome it is Name. --primary-only keeps the first transcript of each gene; use --longest to keep the one with the longest CDS instead.

docs.title: 2. Find syntenic blocks
docs.text:
mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --no-strip-names --cpus=1

This aligns the CDS sets with LAST, filters the hits, finds syntenic anchors, and extends them by liftover. It writes grape.peach.anchors (the blocks, separated by ###), the lifted anchors and a dot plot, grape.peach.pdf.

docs.title: 3. Look at the blocks
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors
mcscan3 synteny depth grape.peach.anchors --histogram

The depth histogram (grape.peach.depth.pdf) shows how many peach regions match each grape region, and the reverse. The pattern it reports (for example 1:1) is what you pass as --quota to keep that many blocks per region.

docs.title: 4. Macrosynteny: a karyotype plot
docs.text:
Keep the larger blocks and write them in the compact .simple format:

mcscan3 synteny screen grape.peach.anchors grape.peach.anchors.new --minspan=30 --simple

Then describe the tracks. seqids lists the chromosomes of each genome:

Vv06,Vv08
Pp06

layout places the tracks and says which blocks join them:

# y, xstart, xend, rotation, color, label, va,  bed
 .6,     .1,    .8,       0,      m, Grape, top, grape.bed
 .4,     .1,    .8,       0,      c, Peach, bottom, peach.bed
# edges
e, 0, 1, grape.peach.anchors.simple

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout

docs.title: 5. Microsynteny: a local view
docs.text:
Stack the peach matches along the grape genome (one column per track):

mcscan3 synteny mcscan grape.bed grape.peach.lifted.anchors --iter=1 -o grape.peach.i1.blocks

Pick a region of grape.peach.i1.blocks (a few dozen consecutive lines), and draw it with mcscan3 plot microsynteny using a layout with one line per track. See plot microsynteny.

docs.title: 6. Figures in the MCscan3 style
docs.text:
Every plot command draws in the MCscan3 theme (white panels, colour-blind-safe colours) unless given --theme classic, and all accept --format png|svg|pdf. When an output name with an extension is given, that extension wins, and plot karyotype writes karyotype.pdf unless told otherwise:

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout --theme mcscan3 -o karyotype.png

docs.title: Coming from JCVI?
docs.text:
The same steps written as JCVI command lines run unchanged after mcscan3 legacy:

mcscan3 legacy compara.catalog ortholog grape peach --no_strip_names

See Migrating from JCVI.

docs.title: mcscan3 ks kaks
docs.text:
Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks of gene pairs with MCscan3's own estimators (no PAML)

Ks10.4 minreal data Reference →

Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks (Goldman-Yang maximum likelihood and Nei-Gojobori) of the syntenic pairs, with MCscan3's own estimators; also written as Ks tables.

cd core && cat grape.cds peach.cds poplar.cds > all.cds  && for p in grape.peach.lifted.1x1 grape.poplar.lifted.1x2 peach.poplar grape.grape; do
   mcscan3 ks kaks $p.anchors --cds all.cds --method gy94,ng86 --cpus $CPU -o ${p%%.lifted*}.kaks.tsv; done  && for p in grape.peach grape.poplar peach.poplar grape.grape; do awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)c[$i]=i; print "name,yn_ks,yn_ka,ng_ks,ng_ka"; next} $c["gy94_ks"]!=""{print $1";"$2","$c["gy94_ks"]","$c["gy94_ka"]","$c["ng86_ks"]","$c["ng86_ka"]}' $p.kaks.tsv > $p.ks; done && wc -l *.ks && head -3 grape.peach.kaks.tsv

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo busco
docs.text:
Phylogenomics from single-copy BUSCO genes: markers, alignments, supermatrix, ML, gene and ASTRAL trees, gCF

Phylogenomics4.1 minreal data3 figures Reference →

A tree of fungi, insects and plants from single-copy BUSCO genes: the lineage (eukaryota_odb10) is chosen from NCBI Taxonomy, proteomes are searched directly, and the concatenated, gene and coalescent trees are compared with gene concordance. Duplicated BUSCOs show the whole-genome duplications of soybean and poplar.

docs.title: Parity
docs.text:
Every analysis feature (all groups except plot, and phylo draw, which is a figure) is parity-verified: its outputs are byte-identical to the JCVI v1.6.7 golden outputs, and its report text matches the original's.

Group Features Status prep 4 all parity-verified align 3 all parity-verified filter 4 all parity-verified synteny 19 all parity-verified quota 1 parity-verified ortholog 8 all parity-verified ks 8 all parity-verified (multireport and the report --pdf figure are verified by image comparison) fractionation 7 + 4 7 parity-verified; napus, merge, segment, offdiag are legacy-only (hard-coded B. napus study code) ancestral 5 all parity-verified pad 2 all parity-verified synfind 1 parity-verified (both scoring modes) phylo 2 of 3 prepare, build parity-verified; draw is ported with the graphics (Phase 4)

Ten features crash on every run in JCVI v1.6.7. For these, the reference is JCVI plus the minimal fixes in tools/jcvi_fixes.patch (the golden cases ending in -fixed, decided at Checkpoint 0). All other outputs come from unmodified JCVI.

What the parity tests do not cover byte-for-byte, and why:

  • phylo build: PhyML seeds its random generator from the clock, so two JCVI runs may root the same tree differently. Trees are compared as unrooted splits with branch lengths. The NJ step needs EMBOSS PHYLIP, which is not packaged for osx-arm64; its failure path matches the golden, but its success path is untested.
  • align blast/align diamond stdout (tool chatter with timestamps) and the report of ortholog run with BLAST/DIAMOND.
  • phylo prepare gene order within each family file (hash-seed dependent in the original).

docs.title: Deviations
docs.text:
See DEVIATIONS.md. In summary:

  • 20 JCVI defects are catalogued (section A). Crashes are fixed by default; silent result changes keep the original behaviour, with an opt-in fix.
  • Platform and representation notes are in section C. These include C printf and Cython BlastLine emulation, the Unix sort emulation, sorted outputs where the original order depended on the hash seed, and the dropped seaborn/palettable/R dependencies.

docs.title: Runtime versus JCVI
docs.text:
tools/bench.py runs each golden case with JCVI (golden environment) and MCscan3 (fresh processes, same inputs). Times are wall-clock seconds, from one run on an Apple-silicon laptop.

Area JCVI MCscan3 Ratio prep (gff2bed, fasta-format, bed) 0.5–3.1 s 0.4–3.1 s 0.69–1.07 align last / blast (aligner-bound) 7–50 s 6–57 s 0.89–1.14 filter blastfilter / cscore / rbbh 0.6–1.1 s 0.6–1.2 s 0.80–1.05 filter best 0.6–0.7 s 0.7–0.8 s 0.97–1.22 synteny (19 features) 0.5–4.5 s 0.2–1.1 s 0.09–1.00 quota align 1.0–1.3 s 0.6–0.8 s 0.58–0.61 ortholog run (end to end, incl. LAST/BLAST/DIAMOND) 14–79 s 9–73 s 0.66–0.98 other ortholog, ks, fractionation, ancestral, pad, synfind, phylo 0.4–7 s 0.2–3.2 s 0.06–0.97

The BLAST-line question from Phase 2: the pure-Python BlastLine is 3.8x slower than the compiled original per line. End to end, it is not a bottleneck. filter blastfilter runs at 0.80–1.02x JCVI, synteny scan at 0.63–0.73x, and ortholog run at 0.66–0.98x, because MCscan3 starts faster and avoids subprocess round trips. No compiled accelerator is needed.

The only case above 1x beyond measurement noise was filter best, which sorts the BLAST file like Unix sort. The emulation now uses stable key passes instead of a comparison function (7x faster, identical order), which brought it from 2.3–3.3x down to 0.97–1.22x.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: graphics ported (2026-09-29)
docs.text: All 13 plot features, ks multireport, phylo draw and the dot plot of ortholog run are ported and parity-verified. The original look is the default (--theme classic), and --theme mcscan3 gives the house style. mcscan3 plot gallery renders every figure in both themes next to the original's reference (see Figures and gallery).

docs.text:
The goldens were drawn by JCVI with matplotlib 3.11.2, the same version MCscan3 uses. Comparisons are exact unless a tolerance is shown. PNG is compared pixel by pixel. SVG and PDF are compared byte for byte after removing the metadata block, because MCscan3 records itself as the Creator.

docs.title: What made exact parity possible
docs.text:
• The seaborn theme values that JCVI applies (rcParams and remapped colour codes, for example "k" drawn as #1a1a1a) are recorded as data, as are the ColorBrewer tables. Neither seaborn nor palettable is a dependency.
  • Each figure starts from a clean matplotlib state, as a fresh JCVI process did.

docs.title: Phase 6: new analyses (2026-09-29)
docs.text:
These are the features requested after the extraction (see ROADMAP.md). Each reimplements a published method from its paper, with no code taken from those tools, and cites it on its documentation page. Their registry status is new.

Command Method How it is tested prep genome longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced from the genome and translated synthetic genome (minus strand, phase, isoforms, non-coding); same transcripts as prep gff2bed --longest on the peach annotation dup classify DupGen_finder classes, from the paper synthetic genome with a known class for every pair; grape run looks plausible ortholog soi Orthology Index filtering (SOI) constructed blocks with known OI; pairs, OrthoFinder and BLAST RBH inputs wgd ksd paranome (MCL + node weighting) or anchor Ks; yn00 or codeml (pairwise ML) anchor Ks equals JCVI ks calc (golden) to 1e-3; node weights on a known family wgd peaks, wgd mix, wgd blocks KDE peaks; GMM, ELMM (exponential background + log-normal peaks) and Bayesian GMM, chosen by BIC/AIC, multi-start EM, warm-start bootstrap intervals, saturation warning; per-block median Ks ELMM recovers background + peak and picks the no-WGD null on exponential data; weights equal repeated data; grape: the paranome ELMM and the block-level GMM both put γ at Ks 1.36 wgd correct relative rate correction with an outgroup (ksrates) exact numbers; bootstrap on synthetic distributions wgd tree-map Tree2GD-style LCA reconciliation duplications at known nodes; rooting, support and coverage filters pan genes, plot riparian GENESPACE-style pan-genes and braids three synthetic genomes with transitive synteny and neighbour placement; colour propagation network build, cluster, profile, tree synteny networks (Zhao & Schranz) four synthetic species: clusters, profiles and the tree ((A,B),(C,D))

The full suite has 386 tests, plus 22 slow tests that run external aligners. mypy and ruff are clean.

docs.title: Figures, report and documentation site (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
The figures, the pipeline and the documentation were made into one consistent system.

  • House style (mcscan3.plot.style). Every figure that is new in MCscan3 shares its colours, fonts, layout, title and subtitle, and output settings. The mcscan3 theme lists only fonts that are installed, which ends a flood of findfont warnings. Ported figures keep --theme classic byte for byte.
  • Modern dot plot. Chromosome names are shortened and non-overlapping, unplaced scaffolds are hidden (with a note), and the heading is measured to sit above the labels.
  • Interactive dot plots (plot dotplot -o x.html, and every pair in the report). The page draws on a canvas: zoom, pan, click a chromosome to zoom to it, see the genes on hover, and colour by orientation, block or Orthology Index. It needs no network access.
  • Pipeline. run.json records the status, time and notes of every step, plus the report's results. --steps re-runs only the steps given; pipeline report <outdir> rebuilds the report. A table of the steps is printed at the end of each run.
  • Report. Sidebar, summary cards, interactive dot plots, stacked bars, lightbox, sortable tables, dark mode and a table of the run.
  • Documentation site. Material for MkDocs with tabs, a landing page, a gallery made from a six-eudicot run (tools/make_docs_gallery.py) and an embedded interactive dot plot. GitHub Pages deploys it (.github/workflows/docs.yml), and the build fails if the command pages are out of date.
  • Fixes. network plot --kind profile crashed with a RecursionError: with few genomes, scipy's dendrogram recursed through a chain-like tree. The dot plot's orientation palette crashed when some anchors were on hidden scaffolds.

Validated by re-running the six-eudicot pipeline (all steps done), and by checking the report and the site in headless Chromium (no script errors; hover, zoom and pair switching all work).

docs.title: WGDs placed by syntenic paralogs in gene trees (2026-10-22)
docs.text:
• Anchored placement (wgd tree-map --paralogs pairs.tsv --outgroup X). This reimplements PUG (McKain et al. 2016) from the paper:
  • gene trees are rooted on the outgroup's genes when they form a clade, else on the fewest duplications;
  • each paralog pair's last common ancestor is mapped to the species tree, and kept when both child clades hold at least half the species below it;
  • each gene tree gives one vote per event and node;
  • supports, when present, are filtered, and votes at ≥80% support are counted separately.

It writes <prefix>.events.tsv. * wgd consensus, gene-tree line. * The noisy count of duplication bursts is replaced. Each genome's self-synteny anchors are labelled by the Ks mixture component of their block, then placed in the gene trees (consensus.events.tsv). * A Ks peak with fewer than --min-tree-rate (0.05) gene trees per pair is rejected, and it loses its Ks vote too. Such pairs come from tandem arrays or a few large families. * A placement split between two adjacent branches is flagged as possible allopolyploidy. * Bursts remain the fallback when there are no syntenic paralogs. * Counting. Ks peaks less than 1.35 times apart count as one event. Ks and gene-tree counts are capped by the copy ratios when those saw events on the branch. * Fixes. * wgd consensus computed ortholog Ks with PAML yn00, so without PAML the Ks line silently gave nothing. It now uses the native LPB93 estimator, like pipeline run --ks. * pipeline run --steps lost the reference, tree and orthology of the earlier run and reran the all-vs-all orthology search. _previous now restores them, and run.json also records the orthologues directory.

Validated on the six-eudicot run (OrthoFinder gene trees, 12,112 used) with the OrthoFinder species tree and with the accepted one. The calls:

branch before now core-eudicot stem γ triplication γ triplication (4/4) Arabidopsis missed α and β (2/4; 4/4 on the accepted tree) soybean 2 WGDs 2 WGDs poplar 1 WGD 1 WGD grape false 1 WGD none

The false grape call came from a Ks component at 0.35: 7,594 pairs in only 60 gene trees, now rejected. Grape's γ peak (Ks 1.45) and peach's (1.64) are placed on the core-eudicot stem by the gene trees, even where Ks alone placed peach's deeper.

docs.title: 2026-10-22: benchmark framework, synteny-constrained anchoring, MMseqs2, annotation transfer
docs.text:
Work for the NAR paper (docs/development/PAPER_PLAN.md).

  • bench simulate / bench score. A genome-evolution simulator that writes a known answer:
  • codon-level divergence with a per-gene ω, so Ks matches the branch length;
  • rearrangements, tandem and dispersed duplications, and losses;
  • WGDs, triplications and allopolyploidy, with biased fractionation;
  • a genealogy-based truth: orthologs, ohnologs, positional pairs, events and ancestral orders.

bench score gives the precision and recall of anchors against that truth. * synteny anchor. Synteny-constrained anchoring, reimplemented from the GENESPACE paper: * collapses tandem arrays; * chains on condensed gene ranks; * rescues hits within a buffer; * finds secondary blocks.

New in MCscan3 is block-local best-hit extension with a C-score filter. The new defaults are --hits 2 (4 for a genome against itself), --secondary 3 and --mask-buffer 100. They were tuned on the simulated polyploids, where F1 is at least 0.998 in every case. * align mmseqs, and ortholog run --align-soft mmseqs. * annotate transfer. Annotation transfer from one or more references: * splice alignment with minimap2; * each gene's copy chosen by synteny with its flanking anchors; * ORF check and repair; * a union across references. * benchmarks/. A synteny benchmark with these methods, all run on shared DIAMOND hits: MCscan3 anchor, MCscan3 classic, MCScanX and GENESPACE 1.3.1. Peak memory comes from /usr/bin/time. * CLI help. [default: …] text was being stripped by rich markup; it now reads (default: …).

docs.title: MCscan3 extraction plan
docs.text: Source: JCVI v1.6.7 (e10b884), see SOURCE_VERSION.md. Generated with tools/inventory.py (actions) and tools/import_graph.py (imports).

docs.title: 1. Inventory vs. Feature Map
docs.text:
tools/inventory.py confirms every action in the Feature Map exists in JCVI v1.6.7, and that every action of the fully in-scope modules (compara.*, apps.phylo, graphics.* listed) is mapped. Differences and corrections:

Item Finding Proposed action align diamond Not new. JCVI has apps.align.diamond_blastp_main (a function, not a listed action), used by catalog ortholog --align_soft diamond_blastp. Port it as a normal feature; JCVI source = apps.align diamond_blastp_main. plot dotplot No main(); entry point is dotplot_main() under if __name__ == "__main__". Map to graphics.dotplot dotplot_main. plot blastplot No main(); argument parsing is inline in the __main__ block. Map to graphics.blastplot __main__. prep gff2bed longest isoform JCVI gff bed --primary_only keeps the first transcript seen per --parent_key, not the longest. There is no longest-isoform option in gff bed. Parity: keep first-seen as --primary-only. Proposal: add opt-in --longest (new, documented in DEVIATIONS). Needs confirmation. quota align solvers v1.6.7 solves via OR-Tools pywraplp (bundled SCIP backend) first; external scip / glpsol binaries are only fallbacks. Default: OR-Tools SCIP (parity). Fallbacks: GLPK (glpsol), external SCIP. Add HiGHS (highspy) as opt-in. compara.phylogeny lcn Low-copy-number gene selection from OrthoFinder output. Not MCscan-related. Out of scope. compara.pedigree Pedigree/inbreeding. Not MCscan. Out of scope. graphics.align, graphics.wheel, graphics.landscape, graphics.mummerplot, graphics.coverage, graphics.table, graphics.assembly, graphics.grabseeds Not MCscan-related. Out of scope. fractionation napus/merge/segment Project-specific (B. napus). legacy-only unless Haibao confirms.

Minor JCVI bugs noticed so far (logging only, no output change): formats.bed fix/some call logger.debug("...%s".format(x)), so the value is never interpolated. Will record in DEVIATIONS.md when ported.

docs.title: 2. Import graph summary
docs.text: The JCVI internal graph is densely cyclic (apps.base ↔ formats.base ↔ utils.cbook, formats.sizes ↔ formats.agp, etc.), so the transitive closure of every in-scope module is ~35 modules including assembly, AWS, grid, OBO/GO, SAM, and uclust code. Almost all of that is reached only through module-level imports used by out-of-scope actions. The plan below is therefore driven by the names that in-scope code actually calls (tools/import_graph.py --names).

docs.title: 3. Decision per dependency
docs.text: Legend: core = port into mcscan3.core, io = port into mcscan3.io, plot = port into mcscan3.plot, replace = use a standard library / third-party package, drop = not needed.

docs.title: apps
docs.text: JCVI module Names used by in-scope code Decision apps.base OptionParser, ActionDispatcher drop → Typer CLI (mcscan3.cli). Option names/defaults preserved per feature. logger replace → logging.getLogger("mcscan3") configured in mcscan3.log (rich handler optional). sh, popen, Popen, which, getpath, need_update, mkdir, cleanup, get_abs_path, glob, iglob core → mcscan3.core.shell (subprocess-based, same semantics incl. need_update skip logic). getpath reads tool paths from env vars (MCSCAN3_<TOOL>) instead of ~/.jcvirc. flatten, parse_multi_values, sample_N, datafile core → mcscan3.core.utils; datafile only needed for hg38 files in graphics.chromosome (see below). apps.align last, blast_main, diamond_blastp_main, run_lastdb, run_formatdb, run_diamond_makedb Feature modules features/align/{last,blast,diamond}.py. apps.grid MakeManager (only ks batch in scope) replace → write a Makefile as JCVI does (small port into core.shell), or run sequentially. Output parity is on the generated makefile + results. apps.r RTemplate (only graphics.histogram) drop → matplotlib reimplementation (spec). apps.phylo feature module Feature modules features/phylo/*. apps.fetch, apps.cdhit, apps.uclust, apps.biomart only via out-of-scope code drop
