docs.title: mcscan3 expr de
docs.text:
Differential expression ranked by Bayes factors.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr de [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Hoerbst F, Sidhu GS, Tomkins M & Morris RJ (2025) What is a differentially expressed gene? (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902) and their Bayesian framework (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.20.633909; github.com/Morris-Research-Group/bayexpress). Instead of a yes/no call from p-value and fold-change cut-offs, every gene is ranked by the evidence for a difference in expression between two conditions (log10 Bayes factor BF21, replicates pooled; see mcscan3.features.expr.bayes), with its inferred log2 fold change, its expression probabilities q per condition, and the evidence that its replicates disagree (BFk1 per condition). Calls (up/down) are made only for convenience, at --min-bf (log10 BF, default 1: a Bayes factor of 10, "strong" on Jeffreys' scale) and --min-fc (|log2 fold change|, default 0); the table keeps every gene with its rank.

Checks of the uncertainty, as in the paper:

  • --control N: N random splits of the first condition's replicates into two halves (wild type against wild type): genes called in a split are listed with how often, and the number of calls per split is reported as the expected false calls of the design;
  • --subsets N: consistently inconsistent genes (CIG) of each condition: replicates drawn N times (--subset-size, default half of them, at least 3); a gene is a CIG when BFk1 > 1 in every draw.

Contrasts come from --contrast TREATMENT:REFERENCE (repeatable) or every pair of conditions. Writes per contrast <prefix>.<treatment>_vs_<reference>.tsv (sorted by evidence), a volcano plot (log2 fold change against log10 BF) and an MA-like plot, <prefix>.summary.tsv and, for the first contrast, q-plots of the top genes (q per replicate):

mcscan3 expr de ath.expr.counts.tsv --samples samples.tsv --contrast heat:control \
    --control 50 --subsets 50 -o ath.de

docs.text: Argument Description MATRIX Count matrix (expr counts output, featureCounts or any gene x sample table).

docs.title: Options

(default: []) --min-bf log10 Bayes factor for a call (1 = BF of 10). (default: 1.0) --min-fc --min-count Skip genes with fewer reads in the two conditions. (default: 0) --control Reference-vs-reference splits to estimate false calls. (default: 0) --subsets Replicate draws to find consistently inconsistent genes. (default: 0) --subset-size Replicates per draw (default: half, at least 3). (default: 0) --top Genes in the q-plot. (default: 12) --format Figure format. (default: pdf) --seed Random seed. (default: 1)

docs.title: mcscan3 expr homoeolog
docs.text:
Homoeolog expression bias and subgenome dominance.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr homoeolog [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. --strip REGEX removes a part of the gene names (e.g. transcript suffixes \.\d+$) so they match the expression matrix. Groups of homoeologs (pairs, triads, ...) come from a table with one column per subgenome (the <prefix>.genes.tsv of subgenome fractionation, . for a lost copy), any table with a header of subgenome names (--columns picks some), or 1:1 anchors (--anchors FILE with --names A,B). For each condition (replicates pooled):

  • bias evidence: log10 Bayes factor that the homoeologs' shares of the group's reads differ from the expected shares (equal, or proportional to gene length with --length), flat Dirichlet against a fixed multinomial (see mcscan3.features.expr.bayes), after the Bayesian treatment of read counts of Hoerbst F et al. (2025, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902);
  • shares of TPM (mean of replicates) and the category nearest to them (Euclidean distance): balanced, one homoeolog dominant, or (three or more) one suppressed, after the triad categories of Ramírez-González RH et al. (2018, Science 361:eaar6089); pairs are dominant when one homoeolog has at least --min-fold times (default 2) the other's TPM; groups with less than --min-tpm in total are not expressed. A category other than balanced is kept only with bias evidence of at least --min-bf (log10 BF, default 1), else balanced;
  • changes between conditions (pairs, with --contrast T:R or every pair of conditions): log10 Bayes factor that the first homoeolog's share differs between the two conditions (the two-sample Bayes factor on the pair's reads).

Per condition, a summary counts groups dominated by and suppressed in each subgenome, the median log2 ratio for pairs, and a sign test of dominance (are biased pairs more often towards one subgenome than half?). Writes <prefix>.groups.tsv, <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.changes.tsv (pairs) and a figure (ternary plot for triads, ratio histogram for pairs, category bars):

mcscan3 expr homoeolog ath.expr.counts.tsv --groups bnap.frac.genes.tsv -o bnap.heb

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description MATRIX Count matrix (expr counts output, featureCounts or any gene x sample table).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output prefix. --samples Sample sheet: sample, condition (default: .samples.tsv). --groups Homoeolog table (one column per subgenome). --columns Subgenome columns to use (repeatable). (default: []) --anchors 1:1 anchors as homoeolog pairs (with --names). --names Subgenome names of the --anchors columns. (default: A,B) --length Expected shares proportional to gene length. --min-tpm Least total TPM of a group to classify it. (default: 1.0) --min-bf log10 Bayes factor for a biased category. (default: 1.0) --min-fold Pairs: TPM fold between homoeologs for dominance. (default: 2.0) --strip Regex removed from homoeolog names (e.g. '.\d+$'). --contrast TREATMENT:REFERENCE for bias changes (pairs). (default: []) --format Figure format. (default: pdf)

docs.title: mcscan3 expr pairs
docs.text:
Expression similarity of gene pairs.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr pairs [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Pairs come as named groups (--pairs NAME=FILE, repeatable: .pairs of dup classify, synteny .anchors, ortholog pairs or any two-column table). Each pair's profiles across conditions (mean log2(TPM + 1) of the replicates; CPM when no gene lengths) are compared by Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation and expression divergence (1 - Pearson); the breadth of expression of each gene is its tissue-specificity index tau (Yanai I et al. 2005, Bioinformatics 21:650). Pairs between species use a second matrix (--matrix2, genes of the second column), with conditions matched by name (only shared conditions are used). A baseline of random pairs is added (--strip REGEX removes transcript suffixes from the pair files' gene names) and each group is compared with it (one-sided Mann-Whitney test: are the pairs more similar than random?). Writes <prefix>.pairs.tsv, <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.tau.tsv and a box plot:

mcscan3 expr pairs ath.expr.counts.tsv --pairs wgd=ath.wgd.pairs --pairs tandem=ath.tandem.pairs \
    -o ath.dup.expr

(default: 2000) --strip Regex removed from pair gene names (e.g. '.\d+$'). --format Figure format. (default: pdf)

docs.title: mcscan3 fetch genome
docs.text:
Genomes and annotations by accession, species or URL.

Group fetch · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fetch genome [OPTIONS] SPECS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each argument names a genome in a public database, and the genome sequence and its annotation are downloaded into a folder that mcscan3 pipeline run reads directly (<label>.dna.fa.gz and <label>.gff3.gz; --proteins adds protein and CDS files). Your own genomes can be mixed in as local files. Accepted names (LABEL= in front sets the species label used in file names and figures):

  • GCF_000001735.4, GCA_...: NCBI Assembly (NCBI Datasets, O'Leary NA et al. 2024, Sci Data 11:732). A GenBank assembly without annotation is replaced by its annotated RefSeq pair.
  • ncbi:Sorghum bicolor or just "Sorghum bicolor": that species' NCBI reference genome.
  • nuccore:CAKMNR000000000 (a WGS project), nuccore:OZ403805-OZ403848 (records), nuccore:PRJEB12345 or nuccore:"Species name": genomes deposited only in NCBI Nucleotide, with no Assembly record (whole-genome shotgun projects, chromosome or complete-genome records; gene, clone, locus, EST/TSA and organelle records are filtered out). GenBank annotation becomes GFF3, protein and CDS files. ncbi:<species> falls back to Nucleotide when the species has no annotated Assembly record, and fetch taxon --nucleotide missing adds such species to a taxon.
  • ensembl:zea_mays: Ensembl and Ensembl Genomes, all divisions, current release (Harrison PW et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Res 52:D891; Yates AD et al. 2022, Nucleic Acids Res 50:D996).
  • GWHBPAH01000000: the Genome Warehouse of the China National Center for Bioinformation (Chen M et al. 2021, Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 19:584).
  • CNP0000111 or CNP0000111/CNA0000821: the CNGB Sequence Archive (Guo X et al. 2020, Database baaa055). An assembly accession alone cannot be looked up there; give its project.
  • a URL of a folder (the genome, annotation, protein and CDS files are recognised by name) or comma-separated file URLs; local files or a folder.

Downloads resume after interruptions and are kept in a cache shared by all runs ($MCSCAN3_FETCH_CACHE or ~/.cache/mcscan3/genomes). manifest.tsv records each genome's source, accession, assembly, annotation and URLs, and taxonomy.nwk the NCBI taxonomy tree of the species:

mcscan3 fetch genome ath=GCF_000001735.4 ensembl:vitis_vinifera GWHBPAH01000000 \
    mine=my_genome.fa,my_genes.gff3 -o genomes
mcscan3 pipeline run genomes -o run

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECS Genomes: NCBI accession (GCF_/GCA_), ncbi:SPECIES, ensembl:SPECIES, GWH accession, CNGB project (CNP... or CNA...), NCBI Nucleotide genomes without an Assembly record (nuccore:WGS_MASTER, nuccore:ACC1-ACC2, nuccore:PRJ..., nuccore:SPECIES), URL of a folder or files, or local files; LABEL=SPEC sets the name.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --outdir Folder for the genomes (ready for pipeline run). --proteins Also download protein and CDS files. --jobs Downloads at once. (default: 3) --unannotated Keep genomes without an annotation. --no-cache Download straight into the folder. --dry-run Only list what would be downloaded.

docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). MCscan3: database clients with resumable, cached downloads, ready for the pipeline. Data from NCBI Datasets (O'Leary NA et al. 2024, Sci Data 11:732), Ensembl and Ensembl Genomes (Harrison PW et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Res 52:D891; Yates AD et al. 2022, Nucleic Acids Res 50:D996), Genome Warehouse (Chen M et al. 2021, Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 19:584) and the CNGB Sequence Archive (Guo X et al. 2020, Database baaa055).

docs.title: mcscan3 fetch taxon
docs.text:
The best annotated genome of every species of a taxon.

Group fetch · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fetch taxon [OPTIONS] NAME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Give a taxon name or NCBI taxid (Poaceae, Brassicaceae, Saccharomycetaceae, 4479). The taxon is looked up in NCBI Taxonomy (Schoch CL et al. 2020, Database baaa062); the annotated assemblies of NCBI (reference genomes; --all-assemblies for every one) and of the Ensembl division the taxon belongs to are listed, and the best assembly of each species is kept: annotated, most contiguous (complete > chromosome > scaffold > contig; --level sets the least), RefSeq before GenBank, then the highest BUSCO completeness of the annotation. --per-genus spreads the genomes over genera and --max keeps the best ones; --include and --exclude (regular expressions on species or accessions) and --add (any fetch genome name, e.g. your own genome) adjust the set.

--nucleotide missing also searches NCBI Nucleotide for genomes that have no Assembly record (whole-genome shotgun projects and chromosome or complete-genome records submitted directly; mcscan3.features.fetch.nucleotide) and adds the best one of each species without an Assembly record; --nucleotide all considers them for every species. With the quality options they are ranked and reported like assemblies (read technology unknown; the N50 of the records).

Without -o the genomes are only listed. With -o they are downloaded as by fetch genome, and taxonomy.nwk joins them by their NCBI lineages: a rooted tree with internal nodes named by taxon (unbranched ranks collapsed). Taxonomy leaves polytomies where relationships are unresolved. pipeline run --taxon does all of this and then the whole analysis (orthology, synteny, networks, pan-genes, ancestral genomes, duplications, WGDs, report), comparing the taxonomy tree with the gene-based species trees:

mcscan3 fetch taxon Poaceae --per-genus 1 --max 12            # list
mcscan3 fetch taxon Poaceae --per-genus 1 --max 12 -o grasses  # download
mcscan3 pipeline run -o grasses_run --taxon Poaceae --taxon-max 8 --cpus 16 --ks

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description NAME Taxon name or NCBI taxid (e.g. Poaceae, Brassicaceae, 4479).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --outdir Folder for the genomes (omit to only list them). --source Databases to search: ncbi, ensembl (comma-separated). (default: ncbi,ensembl) --prefer When both have a species: ncbi or ensembl. (default: ncbi) --level Least assembly level: complete genome, chromosome, scaffold or contig. (default: chromosome) --all-assemblies NCBI: consider every assembly, not only reference genomes. --max At most this many genomes, the best first (0: all). (default: 0) --per-genus At most this many genomes per genus (0: any). (default: 0) --include Always keep species/accessions matching (regex, repeatable). (default: []) --exclude Leave out species/accessions matching (regex, repeatable). (default: []) --add Extra genomes (any fetch genome spec, repeatable). (default: []) --reads Quality filter: read technologies to keep (long, hybrid, short, unknown; comma-separated). --min-contig-n50 Quality filter: least contig N50 (bp). (default: 0) --max-contigs Quality filter: most contigs (0: any). (default: 0) --min-busco Quality filter: least BUSCO completeness of the annotation (%; NCBI's). (default: 0.0) --tier Quality filter: worst tier kept (A: long/hybrid reads, contig N50 >= 1 Mb, annotated; B: >= 100 kb; C: annotated, >= 20 kb; D: any). --unannotated Also consider assemblies without annotation (list them; quality filter only). --report Write every assembly considered with its quality metrics (.tsv, or .xlsx). --nucleotide Also genomes deposited only in NCBI Nucleotide (WGS projects, chromosome records): missing (species without an Assembly record) or all. --nuc-min-size Nucleotide genomes: least total size of a record set (Mb). (default: 1.0) --proteins Also download protein and CDS files. --jobs Downloads at once. (default: 3) --no-cache Download straight into the folder.

docs.title: mcscan3 filter best
docs.text:
Best BLAST hit(s) per query or subject (mcscan3 filter best; legacy formats.blast best).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis

docs.title: Description

As in the original, the BLAST file is first sorted in place (sort -k1,1 -k12,12gr: by query, then score descending; -k2,2 with --subject) unless --nosort. Writes <blastfile>.best (<blastfile>.subject.best with --subject):

docs.title: mcscan3 filter blastfilter
docs.text:
Filter a BLAST table for synteny detection (mcscan3 filter blastfilter; legacy compara.blastfilter).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 filter blastfilter [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Keeps one hit per gene pair (highest score first), then applies, in order:

  • --exclude: drop pairs present in an anchors file from a previous run;
  • C-score filter: keep hits whose score is more than --cscore times the best score of either gene;
  • local (tandem) duplicate filter: genes hitting the same partner within --tandem-nmax genes are collapsed onto the largest one.

Writes <blast_file>.filtered. With --tandems-only also writes <bed>.localdups and <bed>.nolocaldups.bed for each genome:

mcscan3 filter blastfilter grape.peach.last --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --no-strip-names

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE BLAST tabular file (e.g. a.b.last).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --tandems-only Also write .localdups and .nolocaldups.bed files. --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within this distance. (default: 10) --cscore Keep hits with C-score above this. (default: 0.7) --exclude Remove anchors from a previous run.

docs.title: mcscan3 filter cscore
docs.text:
C-scores of BLAST hits (mcscan3 filter cscore; legacy formats.blast cscore).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 filter cscore [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
cscore(A, B) = score(A, B) / max(best score of A, best score of B) (sea anemone genome paper). A C-score of 1 is a reciprocal best hit. Reports query subject cscore (optionally percent identity) for pairs above --cutoff, sorted by pair:

mcscan3 filter cscore grape.peach.last --cutoff=0.7 --pct -o grape.peach.cscore

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE BLAST tabular file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --cutoff Minimum C-score to report. (default: 0.9999) --pct Also include percent identity. --writeblast Also write .filtered.blast. --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.text:

mkdir -p filter && mcscan3 filter cscore core/grape.peach.last -o filter/grape.peach.cscore && head -3 filter/grape.peach.cscore

docs.title: mcscan3 fractionation loss
docs.text:
Gene-loss candidates (mcscan3 fractionation loss; legacy compara.fractionation loss).

Group fractionation · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fractionation loss [OPTIONS] BLOCKSFILE GENOMIC

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads a 2-column MCscan blocks file a.b.i1.blocks. For runs of genes of a without a syntenic gene in b (.) flanked by syntenic genes at most --gdist genes apart in b, the expected location in b (flanks extended by --bdist bp) is checked against a genomic alignment of a's CDS to b's genome (BLAST, or BED with --bed):

[S] hit in the syntenic location, [NS] hit elsewhere, [NF] no hit. Prints seqid gene target for every gene of a:

mcscan3 fractionation loss grape.peach.i1.blocks genomic.bed --bed --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLOCKSFILE Two-column blocks file a.b.i1.blocks. GENOMIC Genomic alignment of a's CDS to b's genome (BLAST or BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --bed The genomic alignment is in BED format. --gdist Gene distance. (default: 20) --bdist Base pair distance. (default: 20000) --qbed Query BED. --sbed Subject BED.

docs.title: mcscan3 fractionation validate
docs.text:
Check [S] loss calls against CDS (mcscan3 fractionation validate; legacy compara.fractionation validate).

Group fractionation · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fractionation validate [OPTIONS] FRACTIONATION CDSBED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
[S] rows of a fractionation file (from fractionation loss) mark a lost gene whose region still has a sequence match. Those regions are written to S.bed and intersected with the CDS BED (intersectBed -wao, bedtools); a region overlapping a CDS is replaced by that CDS name. Writes <fractionation>.validated:

mcscan3 fractionation validate grape.peach.fractionation peach.cds.bed

The original crashed on Python 3 (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.4).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FRACTIONATION Fractionation file from fractionation loss. CDSBED CDS BED file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. The overview figure of a genome paper, from the same tracks as genome landscape (genes, repeat classes or the soft-masked share, GC, variants, any BED or bedGraph):

  • the ideogram ring: chromosomes to scale with Mb ticks, centromeres (--centromeres) and detected telomeres;

docs.title: mcscan3 genome depth
docs.text:
Read depth along the genome: copy number of samples, segments and aneuploidy.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome depth [OPTIONS] INPUTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the read-depth copy-number panels of Tang H et al. (2024, iMeta 3:e211). Each sample is a depth file in windows (mosdepth *.regions.bed.gz or any bedGraph: chrom, start, end, mean depth) or a BAM/CRAM, whose depth in --window bp windows is computed with mosdepth when it is installed, else samtools bedcov. Give NAME=path to name a sample (default: the file name).

Depth becomes copy number in four steps:

  1. windows are re-binned to --window (covered-base weighted means);
  2. with --genome, depth is corrected for GC: each window is divided by the median depth of the windows of the same GC percentile (read depth rises and falls with GC on most platforms);
  3. with --normalise panel (the default for five or more samples), each window is divided by its median over the samples, which removes mappability and collapsed-repeat artefacts shared by all samples; otherwise by the genome-wide median (genome);
  4. copy number = --ploidy x depth / the sample's median over the --reference chromosomes (all by default; give the autosomes when sex chromosomes differ).

Segments come from a hidden Markov model over copy states 0..--max-copy (Gaussian emissions whose spread grows with the copy number and is estimated from the sample's window-to-window noise, with a 1% outlier floor; the Viterbi path, switching at probability --switch per window). The median copy number of every chromosome of every sample is the karyotype: trisomies, sex chromosomes and aneuploid lines show at a glance.

Writes <prefix>.depth.tsv (copy number of every window and sample), <prefix>.segments.tsv (every segment with its state; gains and losses are those away from --ploidy), <prefix>.karyotype.tsv and the figures <prefix>.depth (one panel per sample: windows coloured by state and the segments), <prefix>.heatmap (samples by genome, clustered) and <prefix>.karyotype (samples by chromosomes):

mcscan3 genome depth s1.regions.bed.gz s2.regions.bed.gz s3.bam --genome ref.fa --window 100000 -o cnv

docs.text: Argument Description INPUTS Depth per sample: mosdepth regions.bed.gz, bedGraph or BAM/CRAM; NAME=path names a sample.

(default: 100000) --chroms Comma-separated chromosomes (default: the large ones). --min-chrom Chromosomes: sequences of at least this share. (default: 0.01) --ploidy Copies of the genome in a normal sample. (default: 2) --max-copy Highest copy state (0: 2 x ploidy + 2). (default: 0) --normalise panel (per-window median of the samples), genome, or auto (panel with five or more samples). (default: auto) --reference Comma-separated chromosomes that set the median depth (e.g. the autosomes). --switch Probability of a copy change between windows. (default: 0.001) --mapq Lowest mapping quality counted (BAM/CRAM). (default: 0) --cpus Threads for mosdepth. (default: 4) --max-panels Samples drawn as panels (all are in the heatmap). (default: 16) --title Figure title. --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 genome landscape
docs.text:
Genomic landscape: genes, repeats, GC and any track along the chromosomes.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome landscape [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the landscape stack and heatmap plots of Tang H et al. (2024, iMeta 3:e211), made genome-wide and publication-ready. Tracks are computed in sliding windows (--window bp moved by --step; see mcscan3.features.genome.tracks): gene density, gene and exon share, the share of each repeat class or superfamily (the --top-repeats most abundant, the rest pooled), GC, variants per kb (heterozygous sites of --sample), and any BED or bedGraph. Each track keeps one colour in every figure:

  • <prefix>.ideogram: every chromosome drawn to scale with one heatmap strip per track (white to the track's colour over the genome-wide 2nd-98th percentiles), centromeres (--centromeres, e.g. from centromere find) and telomeres (detected, as genome stats);
  • <prefix>.stack: the composition of every chromosome as stacked areas (genes and repeat classes; share of each window), one panel per chromosome;
  • <prefix>.<chrom>: one chromosome in detail (--detail; the longest by default): stacked composition, every track as a line, and the heatmap strips;
  • <prefix>.correlation: Spearman correlation of the tracks across windows (genes and repeats are usually anti-correlated; recombination-poor pericentromeres stand out).

Writes <prefix>.windows.tsv (every track in every window; --from-windows redraws from it) and the figures:

mcscan3 genome landscape --genome ath.fa --gff ath.gff3 --repeats ath.EDTA.TEanno.gff3 \
    --centromeres ath.centromeres.tsv --window 250000 --step 50000 -o ath

docs.title: mcscan3 genome ldmap
docs.text:
Linkage along the assembly: genetic-map r² heatmaps and misassembly flags.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome ldmap [OPTIONS] GENOTYPES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the genetic-map heatmaps of Tang H et al. (2024, iMeta 3:e211). Markers genotyped in a mapping population (F2, RIL, backcross, any cross; a VCF or a table of marker chrom pos then one dosage per individual: 0/1/2, A/H/B or NA) are ordered by their position in the assembly, and the linkage of every pair is the squared correlation of their dosages (r²). In a correct assembly r² is high near the diagonal and fades with distance; a misjoin, an inversion or a translocation breaks that pattern, and a marker linked to another chromosome sits on the wrong one.

Markers pass --min-maf and --max-missing and are thinned to --max-markers per chromosome (evenly by position). Two kinds of flags are written:

  • breaks: positions where the --flank markers on each side are linked to each other at less than --break-ratio of the linkage within the two sides (a misjoin of unrelated sequences), or where every pair of the two markers on each side of the gap is linked at less than --adjacent-ratio of the median r² of neighbouring markers on the chromosome (the physical neighbours are not genetic neighbours: the edge of an inversion, or a join that skips a stretch of the chromosome; one noisy marker lowers only the pairs it is in, so it does not make a break);
  • misplaced markers: markers are clustered into linkage groups (pairs linked at r² >= --min-r2, single linkage); each group belongs to the chromosome holding most of its markers, and markers in the group of another chromosome are misplaced (a translocated block or a chimeric scaffold).

Writes <prefix>.markers.tsv (every kept marker: allele frequency, missing share, linkage to its neighbours, best other chromosome), <prefix>.breaks.tsv and the figures <prefix>.genome (r² of every pair across the genome, chromosomes outlined) and <prefix>.chromosomes (one r² heatmap per chromosome with the breaks marked):

mcscan3 genome ldmap f2.vcf.gz --min-maf 0.2 -o asm

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOTYPES Mapping-population genotypes: VCF, or marker, chrom, pos then 0/1/2 or A/H/B per individual.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --chroms Comma-separated chromosomes (default: those with markers). --min-maf Lowest minor allele frequency. (default: 0.1) --max-missing Highest share of missing calls. (default: 0.2) --max-markers Markers kept per chromosome (thinned evenly). (default: 500) --flank Markers on each side compared at a possible break. (default: 10) --break-ratio A break: linkage across below this share of the linkage within the two sides. (default: 0.35) --adjacent-ratio A break: the markers next to a gap linked below this share of the median neighbour r². (default: 0.8) --min-r2 Linkage to another chromosome that flags a marker. (default: 0.3) --title Figure title. --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 genome pedigree
docs.text:
Pedigrees: founder contributions, inbreeding and kinship at any ploidy.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome pedigree [OPTIONS] TABLE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the pedigree inbreeding calculations of Tang H et al. (2024, iMeta 3:e211). The pedigree is a table of individual sire dam (tab, comma or space separated; 0, -, . or NA for an unknown parent; a header line is skipped; the same parent twice is a self). Parents that are not listed are founders, taken as unrelated and not inbred.

  • Founder contributions are exact: every individual holds half of each parent's.
  • Inbreeding (the probability that two alleles drawn without replacement from an individual are identical by descent) and kinship (the probability for one allele from each of two individuals) are exact for diploids (the tabular method of the numerator relationship matrix) and simulated at any even --ploidy by gene dropping: every founder carries ploidy distinct alleles and every gamete takes ploidy/2 of a parent's alleles at random (chromosome segregation without double reduction), over --replicates pedigrees; diploids get both, the simulation as a check.

Writes <prefix>.pedigree.tsv (generation, parents, inbreeding, the share of the main founders), <prefix>.kinship.tsv (between the --focus individuals, or every individual without offspring) and the figures <prefix>.pedigree (the pedigree drawn by generation; every individual a pie of its founder contributions, labelled with its inbreeding) and <prefix>.inbreeding (inbreeding by generation and the founder make-up of the focus individuals):

mcscan3 genome pedigree crosses.tsv --ploidy 4 -o potato

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TABLE Pedigree: individual, sire, dam (0, -, . or NA unknown).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ploidy Ploidy (even); polyploid inbreeding is simulated. (default: 2) --focus Comma-separated individuals for kinship and the founder bars (default: those without offspring). --replicates Simulated pedigrees (gene dropping). (default: 2000) --top Founders coloured; the rest are pooled. (default: 8) --seed Random seed of the simulation. (default: 1) --title Figure title. --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 genome report
docs.text:
A new genome to publication figures in one command.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome report [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. From an assembly FASTA, and whatever else is at hand, every genome analysis that the inputs allow is run, each figure is drawn, and everything is gathered in a composed genome portrait and a self-contained HTML report with a methods paragraph:

===================== ========================================== ================================ input analysis output folder ===================== ========================================== ================================ --genome assembly statistics, telomeres, T2T stats/ --histo/--reads k-mer survey: size, heterozygosity, ploidy survey/ (always) landscape of GC and soft-masking, and of landscape/ genes (--gff) and repeats (--repeats) (always) circos; paralogous links with --anchors circos/ --busco BUSCO completeness (a full_table.tsv) busco/ --hic, --agp Hi-C contact map hic/ --reference alignment to a reference (minimap2) and dot reference/ plot --depth read-depth copy number of samples depth/ --genotypes genetic-map linkage and misassembly flags ldmap/ --pedigree founders and inbreeding of the lines pedigree/ ===================== ========================================== ================================

A step that fails is reported and the others go on. Figures are written in every --format (PDF for the paper and PNG for the page, by default); <outdir>/<name>.portrait composes the circos, key numbers, Nx curves, k-mer spectrum, BUSCO and genome composition into one figure, and <outdir>/report.html holds every figure, table and the methods text. report.json keeps the numbers and the steps:

mcscan3 genome report --genome asm.fa --gff asm.gff3 --repeats asm.EDTA.TEanno.gff3 \
    --histo reads.k21.histo --busco full_table.tsv --title "Arabidopsis thaliana Col-0" -o ath_report

docs.title: mcscan3 genome stats
docs.text:
Assembly statistics: contiguity, gaps, GC, masking and telomeres.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome stats [OPTIONS] FASTA...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For one or more assemblies (FASTA, gzip ok), compares versions in one table and figure:

  • contiguity of scaffolds and of contigs (scaffolds split at runs of --min-gap Ns or more): N50/L50, N90/L90, auN (the area under the Nx curve, sum(L^2) / total, which unlike N50 does not jump with single sequences), and NG50 with --genome-size;
  • composition: GC of the called bases, Ns, soft-masked (lower-case) share;
  • telomeres at both ends of each sequence: the telomeric repeat is detected among the known motifs (TTTAGGG plants, TTAGGG vertebrates and fungi, TTAGG insects, TTTTAGGG green algae, TTGGGG ciliates) by its density at sequence ends, or given (--motif); an end is telomeric when the motif (either strand) covers --min-cover of its first --end bp, and the telomere length is that of the repeat array at the end. Sequences with telomeres at both ends and no gap are telomere-to-telomere (T2T);
  • figures: Nx curves of scaffolds and contigs of every assembly; the chromosomes (sequences of at least --min-chrom of the assembly) drawn to scale with gaps and telomeres; size of each assembly in chromosomes, other sequences and gaps.

Writes <prefix>.stats.tsv (one column per assembly), <prefix>.sequences.tsv, <prefix>.gaps.bed, <prefix>.telomeres.tsv and <prefix>.stats.<format>:

mcscan3 genome stats v1.fa.gz v2.fa.gz --genome-size 1.1g -o asm

docs.title: mcscan3 genome survey
docs.text:
Genome survey from k-mers of reads: size, heterozygosity, repeats, ploidy.

Group genome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 genome survey [OPTIONS] HISTO

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the k-mer histogram survey of Tang H et al. (2024, iMeta 3:e211) and the model of GenomeScope 2.0 (Ranallo-Benavidez TR, Jaron KS & Schatz MC (2020) Nat Commun 11:1432), implemented from their descriptions. Input is a k-mer count histogram (count<TAB>number of k-mers`: `jellyfish histo`, `kmc_tools ... histogram`, `meryl histogram), or reads (--reads), counted with KMC or Jellyfish when installed.

Model. k-mers seen x times follow a mixture of negative binomials with means i * lambda (lambda: k-mer coverage of one haplotype, 1n) and a shared overdispersion: for ploidy p, component i <= p holds k-mers present in i of the p haplotypes, components p < i <= 2p duplicated k-mers (two copies on some haplotypes), and components at 3p and 4p repeats. The tail of the error k-mers past the valley (the first minimum) is extrapolated as the power law of the last counts before it and taken out. For each lambda and overdispersion the component sizes (numbers of distinct k-mers) are the non-negative least-squares fit to the histogram beyond the valley, and lambda and the overdispersion are optimised from every start that puts the main peak at 1n .. pn. Fits are plausible when single-copy distinct k-mers outnumber repeated ones, k-mers in two copies of the genome are at most half the homozygous single-copy ones, and (p >= 3) the 1n class holds at least half as many distinct k-mers as the (p-1)n class (a k-mer in p-1 haplotypes has its alternative in the remaining one).

Ploidy. With --ploidy auto every ploidy from 1 to --max-ploidy is fitted; the call is diploid (one haplotype and a homozygous diploid give the same spectrum) unless a higher ploidy beats it by --margin in BIC with haplotype classes at coverages the lower one lacks (e.g. k-mers in 3 of 4 haplotypes) that are needed (refitted without them, the BIC worsens by the margin) and seen (a peak or shoulder of the spectrum within 0.3 lambda: a local minimum of its curvature). A higher ploidy at a fraction of the coverage holds every lower model and reshapes the flanks of the main peak, so a better BIC alone is not evidence. An autopolyploid whose lower-dosage peaks are not visible (low coverage, few heterozygous sites) cannot be told from a diploid by k-mers alone; the BIC of each ploidy is reported.

Estimates. Haploid genome size = k-mers counted beyond the valley / (p * lambda); single-copy share = k-mers in components 1..p (counted i * lambda times each) / all; repeats = the rest; heterozygosity r from the share of fully homozygous k-mers, (1 - r)^k = w_p / sum_i (i/p) w_i (i <= p), the per-site rate at which haplotypes differ; error k-mers below the valley.

Writes <prefix>.survey.tsv (estimates), <prefix>.survey.fit.tsv (histogram, model and components), <prefix>.survey.ploidy.tsv (every ploidy tried) and <prefix>.survey.<format>:

mcscan3 genome survey reads.histo -k 21 --ploidy auto -o sp
mcscan3 genome survey --reads r1.fq.gz --reads r2.fq.gz -k 21 --cpus 8 -o sp

docs.text: Argument Description HISTO k-mer histogram (countk-mers), or give --reads.

(default: 0) --cpus Threads for k-mer counting. (default: 4) --memory Memory for KMC (GB). (default: 8) --title Figure title (e.g. the species). --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). docs.title: mcscan3 gff add
docs.text:
Add derived features to an annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff add [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_add_introns, agat_sp_add_intergenic_regions, agat_sp_add_start_and_stop and UTR completion (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT):

  • --introns: intron features between the exons of each transcript;
  • --utrs: five_prime_UTR/three_prime_UTR from exons minus CDS where missing;
  • --intergenic: top-level intergenic_region features between consecutive genes of a sequence (genes on either strand; overlapping genes leave no gap), and from the sequence ends when --genome gives the sequence lengths;
  • --codons: start_codon and stop_codon at the ends of each CDS, split across exons when a codon is spliced, added only where the genome (--genome, required) shows ATG (or the --table start codons) and a stop codon.

Writes GFF3 (or GTF/BED by the extension of -o):

mcscan3 gff add ath.gff3 --introns --intergenic --codons --genome ath.fa -o ath.full.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --introns Introns between exons. --utrs UTRs from exons minus CDS where missing. --intergenic Intergenic regions between genes. --codons Start and stop codons (needs --genome). --genome Genome FASTA (codons; sequence ends for --intergenic). --table Genetic code (NCBI table number). (default: 1)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff compare
docs.text:
Compare two annotations of one genome.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff compare [OPTIONS] REFERENCE QUERY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_compare_two_annotations (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT) and the sensitivity/precision levels of gffcompare (Pertea G & Pertea M 2020, F1000Research 9:304). The first file is the reference. Genes overlapping on the same strand (by CDS when both are coding, else exons) form loci; each locus is identical (a transcript pair with the same CDS, or the same exons when non-coding), overlapping, reference only or query only, with its numbers of genes on each side (1:1, 1:n, n:1, n:m). Sensitivity and precision at the base (CDS or exon bases), exon (exact exon), intron (exact intron), intron chain (transcript) and gene (locus with an identical pair) levels. Writes <prefix>.loci.tsv and <prefix>.summary.tsv:

mcscan3 gff compare reference.gff3 new.gff3 -o ref_vs_new

docs.text: Argument Description REFERENCE Reference annotation. QUERY Annotation to compare.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.text: mcscan3 gff convert [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's converters (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). Reads GFF3 or GTF (detected), writes GFF3, GTF (Ensembl-like with gene and transcript lines, or --gtf-version 2.2), BED12 of transcripts (exons as blocks, CDS as the thick part) or BED6 of genes. (default: 3) --name BED: attribute used as the name. (default: ID) --fix Repair the annotation first (as gff fix).

docs.title: mcscan3 gff extract
docs.text:
Sequences of annotated features.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff extract [OPTIONS] GFF GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_extract_sequences (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). From an annotation and its genome FASTA, one record per transcript (or per piece) of --type:

  • cds (spliced, 5' to 3', first phase trimmed) and protein (translated, --table genetic code, final stop removed; --keep-stop keeps it). A complete CDS (first phase 0) that opens with an alternative start codon of the table (CTG, TTG; GTG with table 11) begins with M, as the ribosome reads it;
  • mrna (spliced exons), gene (genomic span), exon and intron (each piece);
  • five_prime_UTR and three_prime_UTR (spliced per transcript);
  • upstream / downstream: --flank bp before the transcript start or after its end, on the transcript's strand (clipped at sequence ends).

--longest uses one transcript per gene. Headers are >ID gene=GENE seqid:start-end(strand); --name Name uses another attribute as the record name:

mcscan3 gff extract ath.gff3 ath.fa --type protein --longest -o ath.pep

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped). GENOME Genome FASTA.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output FASTA (default: stdout). (default: -) --type cds, protein, mrna, gene, exon, intron, five_prime_UTR, three_prime_UTR, upstream or downstream. (default: cds) --longest One transcript per gene (longest CDS). --flank Upstream/downstream length (bp). (default: 1000) --table Genetic code (NCBI table number). (default: 1) --keep-stop Proteins keep a final stop (*). --name Attribute used as the record name. (default: ID)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff filter
docs.text:
Select genes of a GFF3/GTF annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff filter [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's filters (agat_sp_filter_feature_by_attribute_value, agat_sp_filter_by_ORF_size, agat_sp_filter_gene_by_length, ...; Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). A gene is kept with all its transcripts when it passes every test given:

  • --type: gene type (gene, ncRNA_gene, ...; repeatable);
  • --seqid: on these sequences; --region SEQ:START-END: overlapping the region;
  • --attr KEY=REGEX: an attribute of the gene or one of its transcripts matches (repeatable, all must match); --exclude KEY=REGEX: none matches;
  • --min-length/--max-length: gene span in bp;
  • --min-protein/--max-protein: longest protein (CDS length / 3, stop excluded) in amino acids; genes without CDS fail --min-protein;
  • --coding/--noncoding: with or without CDS;
  • --max-exons/--min-exons: exons of the longest transcript.

Writes the kept genes (-o) and, with --discarded FILE, the others:

mcscan3 gff filter ath.gff3 --min-protein 50 --exclude Note=transposable -o ath.f.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --discarded Also write the genes that fail. --type Gene type to keep (repeatable). (default: []) --seqid Sequence to keep (repeatable). (default: []) --region SEQ:START-END: genes overlapping it. --attr KEY=REGEX that must match (repeatable). (default: []) --exclude KEY=REGEX that must not match (repeatable). (default: []) --min-length Smallest gene span (bp). (default: 0) --max-length Largest gene span (bp). (default: 0) --min-protein Shortest longest protein (aa). (default: 0) --max-protein Longest longest protein (aa). (default: 0) --coding Only genes with (or without) CDS. --min-exons Fewest exons (longest transcript). (default: 0) --max-exons Most exons (longest transcript). (default: 0)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff fix
docs.text:
Check and repair a GFF3/GTF annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff fix [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the checks of AGAT (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3552717). Repairs, each counted in the report:

  • types: GTF and common aliases (5UTR, three_prime_utr, ...) to Sequence Ontology names; a transcript with a CDS becomes mRNA;
  • IDs: every gene and transcript gets one (<type><n>); parts get <transcript>.<type><k>, all CDS lines of a transcript share <transcript>.cds; repeated gene/transcript IDs get a suffix;
  • missing parents: parts whose transcript is missing get a transcript (mRNA when it has a CDS) and a gene; transcripts without a gene get one; parts without any Parent are grouped by transcript_id, Name or gene_id (else one transcript each);
  • exons made from CDS and UTRs when a transcript has none; UTRs made from exons minus CDS;
  • CDS phases recomputed from the lengths of the CDS before them (5' to 3');
  • transcript and gene spans set to their parts and transcripts;
  • duplicated lines and identical isoforms (same exons, same CDS) removed.

Writes the repaired annotation (GFF3, or GTF/BED by the extension of -o) and <output>.report.tsv:

mcscan3 gff fix messy.gff3 -o clean.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --no-utr Do not add missing UTRs. --no-exon Do not add missing exons. --no-phase Keep the CDS phases as they are. --keep-duplicates Keep repeated lines and isoforms.

docs.title: mcscan3 gff merge
docs.text:
Merge annotations into one.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff merge [OPTIONS] GFFS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_merge_annotations (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). Annotations are read in order; a gene of a later file that overlaps a gene already present on the same strand (by CDS when both have one, else by exons; at least --min-overlap bp) joins it: its transcripts become isoforms of the earlier gene, except transcripts identical to one already there (same exons and CDS), which are dropped. Other genes are added; IDs that clash get the file's --tag (default the file name) as a prefix. --separate keeps overlapping genes as separate genes (only identical transcripts are dropped). Writes GFF3 (or GTF/BED by the extension of -o) and a summary:

mcscan3 gff merge braker.gff3 liftoff.gff3 -o merged.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFFS Annotations, in order of priority.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --tag Prefix for clashing IDs, one per file (default: file names). (default: []) --min-overlap Shared CDS/exon bases that join two genes. (default: 1) --separate Keep overlapping genes apart.

docs.title: mcscan3 gff rename
docs.text:
Systematic IDs for genes, transcripts and their parts.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff rename [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_manage_IDs (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). Genes are numbered along each sequence (sequences in natural order) with --template, whose fields are {prefix}, {seqid}, {chrom} (the last number in the sequence name, else the name) and {n} (the gene number, which grows by --step; --per-seqid restarts it on each sequence). Transcripts become <gene>.1, <gene>.2...; exons, UTRs and others <transcript>.<type><k>, and the CDS lines of a transcript share <transcript>.cds. Old IDs are kept as Alias (--no-alias drops them) and listed in <output>.ids.tsv:

mcscan3 gff rename ath.gff3 --prefix ATH --template "{prefix}{chrom}G{n:05d}" --step 10 \
    --per-seqid -o ath.renamed.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --prefix Value of {prefix} in the template. (default: GENE) --template Gene ID: {prefix}, {seqid}, {chrom}, {n}. (default: {prefix}{n:06d}) --step Increment of the gene number. (default: 1) --start First gene number (default: --step). --per-seqid Restart the numbers on each sequence. --no-alias Do not keep old IDs as Alias.

docs.title: mcscan3 go enrich
docs.text:
Gene Ontology enrichment of gene sets.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go enrich [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872), reimplemented. Annotations (GAF, GPAD, gene2go, eggNOG-mapper, InterProScan or a table; see go docs) are propagated up the ontology (true-path rule: a gene annotated to a term is annotated to all its ancestors; --relationships part_of also follows those links). For every term annotated in the population, the study genes in it are compared with the population genes in it:

  • test: Fisher's exact test, two-sided by default (terms both enriched, e, and purified, p, in the study); --test greater tests enrichment only;
  • correction for the number of terms tested, per namespace (BP, MF, CC) or over all (--correct-by all): fdr_bh (default), fdr_by, bonferroni, holm, sidak, holm-sidak; several can be given and the first decides significance (--alpha);
  • the population is the given gene list or BED (--population), or the genes of the MCscan3 output the sets come from, or else every annotated gene; study genes outside it are ignored. --annotated-only restricts both to annotated genes (as many R packages do).

Gene sets come from a gene list (--study), a table of named sets (--sets: set<TAB>gene, as written by go sets), or straight from MCscan3 outputs (--from: duplicate classes, pan-gene categories, subgenome assignments, HOGs, synteny blocks, genes in SVs, introgressed segments, regulatory blocks; see go sets), and every set is tested against the same population.

Writes <prefix>.tsv (set, term, namespace, name, level, depth, e/p, study and population counts and ratios, fold enrichment, raw and corrected p values, study genes in the term), a dot plot of the top terms (<prefix>.dotplot.<format>: one set, terms by fold enrichment; several sets, a grid of sets and terms) and, for each set with significant terms, the significant part of the ontology graph with its ancestors (<prefix>.<set>.dag.<format>):

mcscan3 go enrich --obo go-basic.obo --annotations tair.gaf --study young.txt \
    --population genes.bed -o young
mcscan3 go enrich --obo go-basic.obo --annotations ath.emapper.annotations \
    --from ath.genes --bed ath.bed -o ath.dup

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --obo Gene Ontology (OBO, e.g. go-basic.obo; gzip ok). --annotations, -a GAF, GPAD, gene2go, eggNOG-mapper, InterProScan or gene-GO table. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --study Gene list or BED of a study set (repeatable; set named after the file). (default: []) --sets Named sets: setgene (from go sets). --from MCscan3 outputs to take sets from (see go sets; repeatable). (default: []) --bed Genes (BED) for region outputs (SVs, introgression) and the population. --population Population: gene list or BED (default: from the sets' source). --genome Genome column of pan-gene / microsynteny tables. --species Species of HOG tables. --ann-format auto, gaf, gpad, gpad2, gene2go, emapper, interproscan, table. (default: auto) --id-field GAF gene ids: id, symbol or synonym. (default: id) --evidence Keep only these evidence codes (repeatable). (default: []) --no-evidence Drop these evidence codes, e.g. IEA (repeatable). (default: []) --strip Regular expression removed from gene ids, e.g. '.\d+$'. --relationships Also propagate through these relations (part_of, regulates, all). (default: []) --test two-sided (enriched and purified) or greater. (default: two-sided) --method fdr_bh, fdr_by, bonferroni, holm, sidak, holm-sidak (repeatable; first decides). (default: ['fdr_bh']) --correct-by namespace or all. (default: namespace) --alpha Significance level of the corrected p value. (default: 0.05) --min-term Test terms with at least this many population genes. (default: 2) --max-term Test terms with at most this many population genes (0: any). (default: 0) --annotated-only Count only annotated genes in study and population. --all Write every tested term, not only significant ones. --top Terms in the dot plot. (default: 20) --no-dag Skip the ontology graph figures. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 go kegg
docs.text:
KEGG pathway enrichment of gene sets.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go kegg [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after metaKEGG (github.com/dife-bioinformatics/metaKEGG) and the KEGG mapping of KOBAS and clusterProfiler, reimplemented.

  • Annotations (--annotations): eggNOG-mapper .emapper.annotations (its KEGG_ko and KEGG_Pathway columns), KofamScan mapper output or KAAS query.ko (gene, KO), a KEGG organism link file (link/ko/<org> of the KEGG REST service), or any table of genes and KOs;
  • pathways: KO -> pathway links and pathway names from the KEGG REST service, downloaded once into --kegg-dir (default ~/.cache/mcscan3/kegg) or read from there offline. Global and overview maps (map01100-map01299) are left out unless --overview, and so are the Human Diseases (map05) and Drug Development (map07) categories unless --all-categories: they reuse the genes of core pathways (a disease map holds ribosome and respiratory chain genes), so they repeat those pathways' signal under misleading names, above all outside animals. --org (a KEGG organism code: ath, osa, zma, ...) keeps only the pathways KEGG draws for that organism, which removes maps of other kingdoms that share KOs (e.g. "MAPK signaling pathway - fly" in a plant);
  • test: for every pathway with --min-genes to --max-genes annotated population genes, a one-sided Fisher's exact test of the study genes in it, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (or --correction) over the pathways tested;
  • population: --population (gene list or BED) or every annotated gene; only annotated genes count, in the study and in the population.

Gene sets come from --study (one list) or --sets (set<TAB>gene, e.g. from go sets). Writes <prefix>.tsv (set, pathway, name, counts, fold, p values, KOs and genes), a dot plot of the top pathways and <prefix>.links.tsv: for each significant pathway a KEGG link that opens the map with the study KOs highlighted:

mcscan3 go kegg --annotations ath.emapper.annotations --study retained.txt --population ath.bed -o retained

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --annotations, -a Gene KOs: eggNOG-mapper, KofamScan/KAAS, KEGG link file or a table. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --study Gene list or BED of a study set (repeatable; set named after the file). (default: []) --sets Named sets: setgene (from go sets). --population Population: gene list or BED (default: from the sets' source). --org KEGG organism code (ath, osa, zma, ...): only its pathways are tested. --kegg-dir KEGG tables (downloaded here once; default ~/.cache/mcscan3/kegg). --correction fdr_bh, fdr_by, bonferroni, holm, sidak. (default: fdr_bh) --alpha Significance level of the corrected p value. (default: 0.05) --min-genes Test pathways with at least this many genes. (default: 5) --max-genes Test pathways with at most this many genes (0: any). (default: 500) --overview Also test global and overview maps. --all-categories Also test Human Diseases and Drug Development maps. --all Write every tested pathway. --top Pathways in the dot plot. (default: 20) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 go sets
docs.text:
Named gene sets from MCscan3 outputs, for enrichment.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go sets [OPTIONS] INPUTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each input is recognised by its header or name, and gives sets named <kind>:<value> together with its population (all genes it classifies):

  • dup classify <prefix>.genes: one set per duplication class (dup:wgd, dup:tandem, dup:proximal, dup:transposed, dup:dispersed, dup:singleton);
  • dup classify / synteny pair files (*.pairs, *.anchors): the genes in pairs;
  • pan genes table: pan-gene categories (pan:core, pan:softcore, pan:dispensable, pan:private, ...) of the genes of one genome (--genome, default the first);
  • subgenome assign gene table: one set per subgenome (subgenome:<progenitor>);
  • ortholog hogs gene table: genes by the node of their oldest HOG (hog:origin:<node>; with --bed, genes in no HOG are hog:origin:<species>, the species-specific ones), for one species (--species); the HOG table: genes of HOGs from a duplication at each node (hog:duplicated:<node>);
  • OrthoFinder (or pipeline) Orthogroups.tsv and Orthogroups_UnassignedGenes.tsv, for one species (--species): og:core (orthogroups in every species), og:single-copy (one gene in every species), og:accessory (in some other species, not all), og:specific (only in this species, unassigned genes included), og:expanded / og:contracted (at least twice / at most half the median copy number of the other species that have the orthogroup, and a difference of two or more genes);
  • network clusters (net.clusters.tsv): genes of one species in clusters of that species only (network:specific), of every species (network:all) or of some (network:partial); with the network gainloss origins table, by the node where their cluster arose (network:origin:<node>);
  • synteny .anchors / .pairs with --bed: the genome's anchored genes (<file>:syntenic) and the others (<file>:non-syntenic);
  • micro blocks block table: genes in microsynteny blocks of each genome;
  • cne grb table: genes in regulatory blocks;
  • regions with --bed (genes overlapping them, at least --min-overlap of the gene): sv call tables and VCFs (sv:<type>, reference side unless --side qry) and introgress scan segments (introgress:<state>);
  • expr de contrast tables: genes called up or down (de:<contrast>:up, de:<contrast>:down), all ranked genes as the population;
  • expr homoeolog group tables: per condition, the dominant and suppressed homoeologs (heb:<condition>:dominant:<subgenome>, heb:<condition>:suppressed:<subgenome>) and the genes of balanced groups (heb:<condition>:balanced);
  • a set<TAB>gene table or a plain gene list (one set named after the file).

Writes set<TAB>gene rows, with the population as set _population (go enrich --sets reads it back):

mcscan3 go sets ath.genes ath.pan.tsv sv/col.ler.sv.tsv --bed ath.bed --genome ath -o ath.sets.tsv

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description INPUTS MCscan3 outputs (dup classify, pan genes, subgenome assign, hogs, ...).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --out, -o Output table (setgene). --bed Genes (BED) for region outputs (SVs, introgression) and the population. --genome Genome column of pan-gene / microsynteny tables. --species Species of HOG tables. --side Side of SV tables the genes are on: ref or qry. (default: ref) --min-overlap Least share of a gene inside a region. (default: 0.5)

docs.title: mcscan3 go similarity
docs.text:
Functional similarity of gene pairs from their GO terms.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go similarity [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Semantic similarity of terms by information content (IC = -ln of the share of annotated genes of the namespace annotated to the term, after propagation): Resnik (IC of the most informative common ancestor, MICA), Lin (2 IC(MICA) / (IC(a) + IC(b))) or Jiang-Conrath similarity (1 / (1 + IC(a) + IC(b) - 2 IC(MICA))). Two genes compare by the best-match average of their most specific terms in one namespace (--ns, default BP). After Resnik P (1995, IJCAI), Lin D (1998, ICML), Jiang JJ & Conrath DW (1997, ROCLING) and the semantic similarity of GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872).

Pairs come as groups (--pairs NAME=FILE, repeatable): the .pairs of dup classify (wgd, tandem, ...), synteny .anchors, ortholog pairs, or any two-column table. A baseline of random annotated gene pairs (--random) is added, and each group is compared with it (one-sided Mann-Whitney test: are the pairs more similar than random?). Writes <prefix>.pairs.tsv (group, gene pair, similarity), <prefix>.summary.tsv and a box plot:

mcscan3 go similarity --obo go-basic.obo --annotations ath.gaf \
    --pairs wgd=ath.wgd.pairs --pairs tandem=ath.tandem.pairs -o ath.dup.sim

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --obo Gene Ontology (OBO, e.g. go-basic.obo; gzip ok). --annotations, -a GAF, GPAD, gene2go, eggNOG-mapper, InterProScan or gene-GO table. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --pairs NAME=FILE of gene pairs (repeatable). --ns Namespace: BP, MF or CC. (default: BP) --method lin, resnik or jc. (default: lin) --random Random annotated pairs as a baseline (0: none). (default: 2000) --ann-format auto, gaf, gpad, gpad2, gene2go, emapper, interproscan, table. (default: auto) --id-field GAF gene ids: id, symbol or synonym. (default: id) --evidence Keep only these evidence codes (repeatable). (default: []) --no-evidence Drop these evidence codes, e.g. IEA (repeatable). (default: []) --strip Regular expression removed from gene ids, e.g. '.\d+$'. --relationships Also propagate through these relations (part_of, regulates, all). (default: []) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 go slim
docs.text:
Gene annotations summarised on a GO slim.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go slim [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the slim mapping of GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872) and map2slim (GO Consortium). Each term of a gene maps to its direct slim ancestors: the slim terms among the term and its ancestors that have no other such slim term below them (--all-ancestors: every slim ancestor). The slim is a separate OBO (e.g. goslim_plant.obo, --slim) or a subset of the main ontology (--subset goslim_plant).

With gene sets (as for go enrich: --study, --sets, --from) the genes of each set are counted per slim term, as numbers and as shares of the set's annotated genes, next to the population. The figure is a grouped bar chart of the shares per namespace for up to two sets, and a heatmap of sets by slim terms (shares, coloured by their ratio to the population) for more. Writes <prefix>.genes.tsv (gene, slim terms), <prefix>.counts.tsv (slim term, namespace, name, then genes and share per set) and <prefix>.<format>:

mcscan3 go slim --obo go-basic.obo --slim goslim_plant.obo --annotations ath.gaf \
    --from ath.genes -o ath.dup.slim

(default: []) --sets Named sets: setgene (from go sets). --from MCscan3 outputs to take sets from (see go sets; repeatable). (default: []) --no-evidence Drop these evidence codes, e.g. IEA (repeatable). docs.title: mcscan3 go treemap
docs.text:
Treemaps of enriched GO terms across datasets.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go treemap [OPTIONS] TABLES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after GOGetter (multi-dataset GO treemaps). The enriched terms of one or more enrichment tables (go enrich output, any table with go and a q or p value, or plain GO lists; NAME=FILE names a dataset, and every set of a go enrich table is a dataset of its own) are:

  1. compared by GOGO semantic similarity (Zhao C & Wang Z (2018) Sci Rep 8:15389): every ancestor of a term gets an S-value from the term through its children, each edge weighing 1 / (0.67 + children of the parent) + 0.4 (is_a) or + 0.3 (part_of), and two terms compare by the S-values of their common ancestors;
  2. clustered (average linkage, joined while similarity is at least --cutoff), the same clusters in every dataset;
  3. named by their lowest common ancestor: the most specific term that is an ancestor (or one) of every member; a cluster of one keeps the term's name;
  4. coloured by family: every cluster has one colour-blind-safe hue (Okabe-Ito, then Tol), its terms lighter to darker shades of it by significance.

The treemap of each dataset is squarified (Bruls et al. 2000): clusters are blocks of their terms, sized by --size (-log10 q by default, or genes, or fold enrichment). Writes <prefix>.clusters.tsv, <prefix>.terms.tsv and the figures <prefix>.treemap (one panel per dataset, shared colours) and, with several datasets, <prefix>.compare (clusters by datasets: terms and best significance):

mcscan3 go treemap --obo go-basic.obo leaf=leaf.enrich.tsv root=root.enrich.tsv -o tissues

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TABLES Enrichment tables (go enrich output, or GO and q columns); NAME=FILE names a dataset.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --obo Gene Ontology (OBO, e.g. go-basic.obo; gzip ok). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ns Namespace: BP, MF or CC. (default: BP) --alpha Terms with q below this. (default: 0.05) --cutoff GOGO similarity that joins terms into a cluster. (default: 0.5) --size Area: significance (-log10 q), genes or fold. (default: significance) --max-terms Most significant terms per dataset. (default: 60) --compare-top Clusters in the comparison of several datasets (most significant first). (default: 40) --title Figure title. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 introgress scan
docs.text:
Introgression and haplotype-sharing scans with k-mers.

Group introgress · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 introgress scan [OPTIONS] TARGET

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the k-mer identity-by-state approach of KCFtools and IBSpy (k-mers of a reference window looked up in the k-mers of a sample, with no alignment or variant calling). A target genome (an assembly: its chromosomes give the coordinates) is cut into windows; each source (assemblies or read sets, plain or gzip FASTA/FASTQ) is reduced to its sampled k-mers (introgress k-mer sketches, FracMinHash with --scaled; read k-mers seen fewer than --min-count times are dropped as errors). For every window and source, the containment is the share of the window's k-mers found in the source: ~1 where the two are identical by state, about (1 - d)^k where they differ at a rate d (0.53 at 2% with k = 31).

Two ways to read the windows, both segmented with a Viterbi path (--switch penalises a change of state between neighbouring windows, so single noisy windows do not break blocks); every block boundary is then moved to the sampled k-mer where the k-mers on each side best agree with the two states, so breakpoints are placed to tens of bases rather than to a window:

  • --mode paint (default): every window goes to the source it matches best; with the parents (or candidate donors) as sources and a hybrid or introgression line as target, the blocks are its ancestry mosaic, like haplotype painting;
  • --mode identity: every source separately, windows are identical by state (containment at least --min-identity) or divergent; with a reference as target and samples (reads) as sources, divergent blocks are candidate introgressions from a distant donor, as KCFtools reports them.
mcscan3 introgress scan hybrid.fa --source parentA.fa --source parentB.fa -o hybrid
mcscan3 introgress scan ref.fa --source line1.fq.gz --source line2.fq.gz --mode identity --min-count 3 -o lines

Writes <prefix>.windows.tsv (window, k-mers sampled, containment in each source, state) and <prefix>.blocks.tsv (chromosome, start, end, state, windows, mean containment).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TARGET Target assembly (FASTA): its chromosomes give the windows.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --source Source genome or reads (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip ok), optionally named as NAME=FILE; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --mode paint (best source per window) or identity (IBS per source). (default: paint) --window Window size (bp). (default: 50000) --k k-mer length (up to 31). (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash). (default: 10) --min-count Read k-mers seen fewer times are errors (FASTQ only). (default: 2) --min-identity Identity mode: least containment of an IBS window. (default: 0.8) --switch Penalty of a change of state between windows. (default: 3.0) --min-kmers Windows with fewer sampled k-mers are not scored. (default: 50) --cpus Threads (default: all).

Group introgress · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 introgress view [OPTIONS] SCAN_PREFIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, drawn with genomeview (Spies N et al.; github.com/nspies/genomeview, MIT), an SVG genome-browser engine. introgress plot paints whole chromosomes; introgress view zooms into regions (--region chrom:start-end, repeatable; --chrom for a whole chromosome; default: the longest blocks of the scan) and stacks, for each region:

  • the coordinate axis;
  • the k-mer containment of the target windows in every source (one line per source, the same colours as introgress plot);
  • the painted blocks of the scan, coloured by source;
  • optionally genes (--bed, BED6 or MCscan3 .bed), aligned reads (--bam, repeatable, indexed BAM or CRAM; mismatches shown against --reference) and other window tracks (--track file.tsv:column`, e.g. f_dM of `introgress abba` or the combined score of `sex run).

Writes SVG; PDF and PNG need rsvg-convert (librsvg) or Inkscape on the PATH (else the SVG is kept). Needs the view extra: pip install "mcscan3[view]" (genomeview, pysam).

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype align
docs.text:
Event-related hierarchical alignment of several genomes to one reference.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype align [OPTIONS] REF_BED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Every gene of the reference gets one row; every copy that a duplication or speciation event left in each genome gets one column. The columns are filled from the synteny blocks between the reference and each genome (the reference against itself gives its own duplicated copies):

  1. events: with Ks (the anchor-pair TSV of wgd ksd --anchors) and named Ks ranges (--event rho=0.6,1.4), each block takes the event its median Ks falls in; blocks outside every range are left out. Without ranges every block of a genome belongs to one event, named after the genome (orthologues of a speciation), and self for the reference itself;
  2. copies: within one genome and event, blocks are laid out in columns from the largest down: a block joins the first column where it overlaps no other block on the reference (by at most --overlap of the shorter one's reference genes), else opens a new column, up to --copies columns. A column is one copy of the reference region (subgenome, or homoeologous region);
  3. cells: inside a block, a reference gene with an anchor partner gets the partner; a gene without one gets . (the region is there but the gene is missing: lost, moved, or not anchored); outside every block of the column the cell is - (no syntenic region).

Columns are ordered by event (in the order of --event), then genome, then copy, so the table reads from the oldest duplication to the youngest speciation when the events are given in that order. Retention of each column is the share of the covered reference genes that have a partner: the fractionation of each copy after its event:

mcscan3 karyotype align rice.bed --genome rice=rice.rice.anchors --genome sorghum=rice.sorghum.anchors \
    --ks rice=rice.ks.tsv --ks sorghum=rice.sorghum.ks.tsv --event rho=0.6,1.6 --event speciation=0,0.6 \
    --ancestor rice.labels.tsv -o grass

Writes <prefix>.alignment.tsv (reference chromosome, rank, gene, ancestral chromosome when --ancestor is given, then one column per copy), <prefix>.columns.tsv (per column: genome, event, copy, blocks, covered genes, partners, retention, median Ks) and the figure <prefix>.<format>: one track per column along the reference chromosomes, partners drawn as ticks coloured by ancestral chromosome (or by event).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description REF_BED Genes of the reference genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --genome NAME=ANCHORS of the reference with a genome (the reference's own name: its duplicated copies); repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ks NAME=KS: anchor-pair Ks of that genome (TSV of wgd ksd). (default: []) --event NAME=lo,hi: blocks with median Ks in the range belong to this event; repeat, oldest first. (default: []) --ancestor Ancestral karyotype on the reference, to colour the genes (or chromosomes). --copies Most columns per genome and event. (default: 4) --overlap Blocks of one column overlap by at most this share. (default: 0.2) --min-block Fewest anchors of a block. (default: 5) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype ancestor
docs.text:
The ancestral karyotype that explains the genomes with the fewest events.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype ancestor [OPTIONS] SEGMENTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the telomere-centric model of chromosome evolution (Wang X et al. 2015, Plant Cell 27:1953; Murat F et al. 2017, Genome Biol 18:200): chromosome numbers fall by end-to-end joining (EEJ) and nested chromosome fusion (NCF, one chromosome inserted near the centromere of another) and rise by fission. A candidate ancestor (the ancestral chromosomes of ancestral karyotype or of an outgroup, painted on every genome by karyotype map) may be too fine (two of its chromosomes were one in the true ancestor) or too coarse (one was two). Both are tested as characters on the rooted species tree:

  • join A-B: present in a genome where A and B meet in an EEJ or NCF, absent where both occur on separate chromosomes, unknown where one is missing;
  • split A: present where A is split by a fission (FIS:A), absent where A is whole.

For each character the fewest changes on the tree (Sankoff parsimony, gains and losses costing one each) are computed with the root fixed absent and fixed present. A join or split is accepted when the root carrying it costs less (by at least --min-gain) and at least --min-support genomes show it: the event then predates the root and belongs to the ancestor, not to a lineage. Accepted splits are applied first (at the median breakpoint of the genomes), then joins from the best supported down: an EEJ connects the ancestral ends the genomes join most often, if both are still free; an NCF inserts B into A at the median insertion point. Joins that would need an end already used are reported as conflicts.

With --centromeres (genome, chromosome, start, end in bp, e.g. from centromere find) and the BED files of the genomes (--bed-dir), each NCF is checked for an insertion at the centromere of the host, the signature of the telomere-centric model (column ncf_at_centromere):

mcscan3 karyotype ancestor eudicot.segments.tsv anc.labels.tsv grape.bed --tree species.nwk -o anc2

Writes <prefix>.characters.tsv (every tested join and split: genomes with it, without it, root costs, decision), <prefix>.chromosomes.tsv (the new ancestral chromosomes as ordered pieces of the old ones) and <prefix>.labels.tsv (reference genes with their new ancestral chromosome, in ancestral order), which karyotype map reads as the ancestor of the next round.

docs.text: Argument Description SEGMENTS Segments of karyotype map (.segments.tsv).

(default: 2) --min-gain Changes saved on the tree by an ancestral join or split. (default: 1.0) --end-tol Ancestral positions this close to 0 or 1 are ends. (default: 0.15) --min-genes Smaller segments are ignored (genes). (default: 50) --centromeres genome, chromosome, start, end (bp) per centromere. --bed-dir Folder of .bed (with --centromeres).
