docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype events
docs.text:
Trajectories from the ancestral karyotype to each genome, and shared events on the tree.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype events [OPTIONS] SEGMENTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the chromosome evolution models used with AKRUP and WGDI (Wang X et al. 2015, Plant Cell 27:1953 on grasses; Murat F et al. 2017, Genome Biol 18:200; Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841). Each extant chromosome painted by karyotype map is read as a row of segments of ancestral chromosomes, each with its ancestral span (0 and 1 are the two ends, the telomeres, of the ancestral chromosome) and copy. Neighbouring segments meet at junctions, which are classified:

  • EEJ (end-to-end joining), EEJ:A-B: both segments meet with their ancestral ends (within --end-tol of 0 or 1). One chromosome is lost.
  • NCF (nested chromosome fusion), NCF:B>A: segments of B sit between two parts of the same copy of A, and the two parts of A are complementary (their spans hardly overlap): B was inserted into A, usually at the centromere. One chromosome is lost.
  • RCT (reciprocal translocation), RCT:A/B: two junctions of A and B, on different chromosomes, at least one end within the chromosome rather than at its end. The number of chromosomes stays.
  • TRA (other translocation), TRA:A-B: an unpaired junction within a chromosome. When both sides are broken inside, the exchange left one more chromosome (its other product split).
  • FIS (fission), FIS:A: a copy of A is split over more chromosomes than its translocations explain. One chromosome is gained.
  • WGD, WGD:x2: overlapping copies of the ancestral chromosomes (the median number over ancestral chromosomes) are whole-genome duplications, not fissions. The chromosome number expected from the events, ancestral chromosomes x copies + FIS - EEJ - NCF (plus one per TRA broken on both sides), is set beside the observed one as a check: a gap means events the segments do not resolve.

Every event is a character, present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.characters.tsv). With a rooted species tree (--tree) the characters are mapped onto it by irreversible (Camin-Sokal) parsimony: an event can arise on several branches but never reverts, so independent whole-genome duplications and parallel fusions stay on their own branches and an ancestor carries only the events all its descendants share (--model dollo: one origin per event, losses elsewhere). The karyotype of every ancestor follows from the events it carries: which fusions it already had, and its chromosome number (ancestral chromosomes x WGD copies + FIS - EEJ - NCF, each event counted once; genomes keep their observed number). Shared EEJs and NCFs are how the ancestral karyotypes of grasses and eudicots were built (bottom-up); the events on the branches are the trajectory to each genome (top-down):

mcscan3 karyotype events eudicot.segments.tsv --tree species.nwk -o eudicot

Writes <prefix>.events.tsv (genome, type, event, chromosomes, detail), <prefix>.genomes.tsv (per genome: chromosomes, copies, counts of each event type, expected chromosomes), <prefix>.characters.tsv and, with --tree, <prefix>.nodes.tsv (per node: events gained on the branch above it, events carried, chromosome number) and the tree figure <prefix>.tree.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SEGMENTS Segments of karyotype map (.segments.tsv).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --tree Rooted species tree: events and ancestral karyotypes on it. --genomes Only these genomes (comma-separated). --end-tol Ancestral positions this close to 0 or 1 are ends. (default: 0.15) --min-genes Smaller segments are ignored (genes). (default: 50) --model irreversible (parallel gains, no reversals) or dollo (one gain). (default: irreversible) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype fusions
docs.text:
Fusion junctions of one genome, and whether other genomes share them.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype fusions [OPTIONS] SEGMENTS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the fusion positions database and fusion detection of WGDI (Wang et al. 2025, Nat Protoc 20:3528). Starts from a genome painted by karyotype map: wherever two segments of different ancestral chromosomes meet on one of its chromosomes, the junction may be a fusion (or a translocation). The junction is described by the genes flanking it (--flank genes on each side, taken from segments of at least --min-genes genes) and saved as a database, <prefix>.junctions.tsv, which later runs read with --junctions.

Each other genome needs only its synteny with the painted genome (--target BED --anchors ANCHORS), not a painting of its own. For every junction, the partners of the left and right flanking genes are found on the target. The junction is

  • shared: on one target chromosome at least --min-hits partners of each side lie within --max-gap genes of each other: the two ancestral chromosomes are joined at the same place;
  • absent: both sides have at least --min-hits partners, never together;
  • unknown: one side has too few partners (lost, or not assembled).

With --tree, every junction is placed on the tree: the most recent common ancestor of the genomes sharing it (with the painted genome), and consistent says whether every genome below that node shares it too (unknown genomes are allowed). A shared junction inherited from a common ancestor is consistent; one found in scattered genomes points to independent breaks at the same place, or to a hidden polyploidy.

Writes <prefix>.junctions.tsv (junction, genome, chromosome, rank, ancestral chromosomes, left and right genes), <prefix>.fusions.tsv (one row per junction and target: status, target chromosome, partners of each side, gap) and <prefix>.<format> (junction x genome matrix).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SEGMENTS Segments of karyotype map (not needed with --junctions).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --genome The painted genome whose junctions are tested. --bed Genes of that genome (BED). --junctions A junctions table of an earlier run instead. --target Genes of another genome (BED); repeat. --anchors Its synteny with the painted genome; one per --target. --tree Rooted species tree: place every junction on it. --flank Genes taken on each side of a junction. (default: 20) --min-genes Smallest segment giving a junction. (default: 10) --min-hits Partners needed on each side. (default: 3) --max-gap Largest distance (genes) between the two sides when shared. (default: 30) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Resolution of raster images. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype genome
docs.text:
The ancestral karyotype written out as a genome.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype genome [OPTIONS] ANCESTOR REF_BED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the ancestral genome files of WGDI (-ak) and AKRUP (-ags). Every ancestral chromosome becomes a pseudo-chromosome holding the reference genes that carry it, in ancestral order (see mcscan3.features.karyotype.core). The protein (and coding) sequences of those genes make the ancestral genome a genome like any other: align it to extant genomes (align, synteny), draw dot plots against it, and use it as the reference of karyotype map, where every chromosome is its own ancestral chromosome:

mcscan3 karyotype genome anc.segments.tsv grape.bed --pep grape.pep --cds grape.cds -o AEK
mcscan3 karyotype map AEK.labels.tsv AEK.bed --target cacao.bed --anchors AEK.cacao.anchors -o AEK.map

--add NAME=BED,ANCHORS (repeatable) enlarges the ancestral gene repertoire: genes of another genome that sit between two consecutive anchors of one of its synteny blocks with the reference, with no partner in the reference, are genes the reference lost. Up to --max-insert such genes per gap are inserted into the ancestral order after the anchor that comes first, in the order of that genome. Genomes are added in the order given; the origin column of the labels table says where each gene came from. Give their proteins and CDS as more --pep / --cds files.

--name prefixes the pseudo-chromosomes (default: none, the ancestral chromosome names) and --rename gives the genes new names <name><chromosome>g<number>, keeping the originals in the labels table. Writes <prefix>.bed (genes spaced --spacing bp apart), <prefix>.lens (chromosome, genes), <prefix>.labels.tsv (gene, ancestral chromosome, reference gene), and <prefix>.pep / <prefix>.cds when the sequences are given.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCESTOR Ancestral karyotype on the reference: segments, WGDI regions or genelabel; chromosomes: the reference chromosomes. REF_BED Genes of the reference genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --pep Proteins of the reference (and of the --add genomes). --cds Coding sequences of the reference (and of the --add genomes). --copy Use only this copy (class) of a polyploid reference. --name Prefix of the pseudo-chromosomes. --rename New gene names g. --spacing Distance between genes in the BED (bp). (default: 10000) --add NAME=BED,ANCHORS: genes of this genome lost in the reference join the ancestral repertoire (repeatable). --max-insert Most genes inserted between two anchors. (default: 3) --min-block Smallest block (anchor pairs) used by --add. (default: 5)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype map
docs.text:
A known ancestral karyotype painted on another genome through synteny blocks.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype map [OPTIONS] ANCESTOR REF_BED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the karyotype mapping of WGDI (Sun et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841) and the event-related blocks of AKRUP (ancestral karyotype reconstruction pipeline, Wang lab). The reference genome carries the ancestral karyotype (see mcscan3.features.karyotype.core); an anchors file between the reference and the target gives the synteny blocks. Each block with at least --min-block anchors votes for the ancestral chromosome most of its reference genes carry:

  • every target gene between the block's first and last anchor gets one vote (the block covers it);
  • every anchor gets two more votes for the ancestral chromosome of its own reference partner.

Each target gene takes the ancestral chromosome with most votes; labels are smoothed along the chromosome (--window genes each side) and runs shorter than --min-run genes join their neighbours, as in ancestral karyotype. A segment's ancestral span comes from the ancestral positions of its anchors' partners (median of the first and of the last five) and its strand from their rank correlation. Segments of one ancestral chromosome holding the same ancestral positions (over half of the shorter one's, in 1% bins) are copies (from whole-genome duplication), numbered 1, 2, ... by size, as the classes of WGDI.

With --ks (the anchor-pair TSV of wgd ksd --anchors) and --ks-range lo,hi, only blocks whose median Ks falls in the range count: in a polyploid, the blocks of one duplication event (wgd peaks gives the range) paint the copies that event made, as the event-related blocks of AKRUP. Several targets are painted in one run:

mcscan3 karyotype map anc.segments.tsv grape.bed --target cacao.bed --anchors grape.cacao.anchors \
    --target peach.bed --anchors grape.peach.anchors -o eudicot

Writes <prefix>.segments.tsv (the ancestral karyotype columns, then ancestral span, strand, copy and anchors; karyotype events reads it), one WGDI-style region file per genome <prefix>.<genome>.regions.txt (chromosome, start, end, colour, class), the colours <prefix>.colors.tsv, and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCESTOR Ancestral karyotype on the reference: segments, WGDI regions or genelabel; chromosomes: the reference chromosomes. REF_BED Genes of the reference genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --target Genes of a genome to paint (BED); repeat. --anchors Anchors of the reference and each target, in order. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --copy Use only this copy (class) of a polyploid reference. --min-block Fewest anchors of a block that votes. (default: 5) --window Smoothing: genes on each side. (default: 5) --min-run Shorter runs join their neighbours (genes). (default: 20) --ks Anchor-pair Ks (TSV of wgd ksd --anchors). --ks-range Only blocks with median Ks in lo,hi (with --ks). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype pindex
docs.text:
Gene retention of every copy along the reference and the polyploidy index.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype pindex [OPTIONS] ALIGNMENT

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the polyploidy index of Wang et al. (2019, Front Genet 10:807) and the retention plots of WGDI. Reads the event-related alignment of karyotype align (<prefix>.alignment.tsv): one row per reference gene, one column per copy that an event left in a genome. Columns of the same genome and event (soybean:1, soybean:2, or maize:rho:1, maize:rho:2) are the copies of one polyploidy: its subgenomes, as seen from the reference.

The copies compared need a fixed identity along the genome. With the BED of a genome (--bed soybean=soybean.bed) its copies are its chromosomes, as in the definition of the index: two chromosomes covering the same reference windows are homoeologous and are compared. Without a BED the copy columns of the alignment are compared; karyotype align fills its columns from the largest block down, so column 1 tends to hold the better-kept copy in every region, which inflates the index. Give the BED files.

  1. windows: each reference chromosome is cut into windows of --window genes (every --step genes; the default step is the window, so windows do not overlap). The retention of a copy in a window is the share of the window's reference genes that have a partner on it (--covered, for copy columns: only genes inside the copy's blocks count);
  2. comparison: for two copies of one polyploidy, a window is skipped when either retention is below --min-retention (the region is missing, not fractionated). Otherwise d = (r1 - r2) / (r1 + r2); the window favours copy 1 when d > --diff, copy 2 when d < ---diff, and neither otherwise. Pairs of chromosomes sharing fewer than --min-windows compared windows are left out;
  3. index: with a windows favouring copy 1 and b copy 2, the index of the pair is |a - b| / (a + b) (copy columns: summed over the reference chromosomes, as a column may follow different subgenomes on different chromosomes), from 0 (gene loss balanced between the copies) to 1 (biased: one copy always kept more genes). The index of a polyploidy sums |a - b| and a + b over all its pairs. --with-ties puts the windows favouring neither into the denominator. Wang et al. read values above about 0.3 as unbalanced fractionation, as after allopolyploidy, and values below as balanced, as after autopolyploidy; there is no sharp boundary;
  4. test: the sign of each window's difference is flipped at random (--permutations times) to give the index expected when neither copy is favoured; the p-value is the share of permutations reaching the observed index (per pair and per polyploidy). A sign test on the windows of a pair says which copy is dominant.

Writes <prefix>.summary.tsv (one row per polyploidy: copies compared, index, p-value), <prefix>.pindex.tsv (one row per pair: windows compared, windows favouring each, index, p-values, mean retention of each copy, dominant copy), <prefix>.windows.tsv (retention of every copy column in every window), <prefix>.chromosome_windows.tsv (the same by chromosome, with BED files) and <prefix>.retention.<format> (retention along the reference chromosomes, one panel per polyploidy).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ALIGNMENT The .alignment.tsv of karyotype align.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed NAME=BED: compare the copies of this genome by chromosome (recommended; repeat). --window Reference genes per window. (default: 100) --step Genes between window starts (0: the window, no overlap). (default: 0) --covered Copy columns: retention among genes inside blocks only. --min-retention Skip windows where a copy keeps less. (default: 0.05) --diff Smallest (r1 - r2) / (r1 + r2) favouring one copy. (default: 0.1) --with-ties Count windows favouring neither in the denominator. --min-windows Fewest compared windows for a pair of chromosomes. (default: 5) --permutations Random sign flips for the p-value (0: none). (default: 1000) --group Only this polyploidy (genome or genome:event); repeat. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Resolution of raster images. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype trajectory
docs.text:
Chromosome evolutionary trajectories from the ancestor to each genome.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype trajectory [OPTIONS] SEGMENTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. karyotype events places every fusion, fission and duplication on a branch of the species tree. Here the karyotype is followed down each path from the root to a genome:

  • the root has one chromosome per ancestral chromosome;
  • on every branch, its events are applied in turn: a fission (FIS:A) splits A off its chromosome (or into two halves), an end-to-end joining (EEJ:A-B) joins the chromosomes of A and B, a nested fusion (NCF:B>A) puts the chromosome of B inside that of A, and a whole-genome duplication (WGD:xk) copies every chromosome k times (last, so that fusions on the same branch are inherited by every copy). Translocations keep the chromosome number and are listed only;
  • the genome at the end of the path is drawn as it is painted (karyotype map), its chromosomes as stacks of ancestral segments.

Each path is one panel: rows are the nodes from the root (top) to the genome (bottom), chromosomes are bars coloured by ancestral chromosome, and ribbons join every chromosome to those of the next row that hold the same ancestral chromosome, so fusions show as ribbons meeting and fissions and duplications as ribbons parting. The events of each branch are written beside its row:

mcscan3 karyotype trajectory eudicot.segments.tsv --tree species.nwk -o eudicot

Writes <prefix>.trajectory.tsv (per path and node: chromosomes as +-joined ancestral pieces, events applied) and the figure <prefix>.trajectory.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SEGMENTS Segments of karyotype map (.segments.tsv).

(default: 0.15) --min-genes Smaller segments are ignored (genes). (default: 50) --model irreversible or dollo (as karyotype events). (default: irreversible) --ncols Panels per row. (default: 3) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype trees
docs.text:
Gene trees of the event-related alignment and which copies are sisters.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype trees [OPTIONS] ALIGNMENT

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the alignment trees of WGDI (Sun et al. 2022). Every row of the alignment of karyotype align is a set of syntenic genes: the reference gene and its partner in each copy column. Rows with at least --min-genes genes become gene trees:

  1. sequences: proteins (--pep, several files; CDS with --cds instead) of the row's genes, named after their columns;
  2. alignment: MAFFT (--threads sets at once);
  3. tree: neighbour joining on corrected distances (Kimura's protein distance; Jukes-Cantor for CDS) computed in MCscan3 over sites without gaps. With --tree-tool fasttree or iqtree (when installed) that program builds the trees instead.

Leaves are named by column (ref, soybean:1 ...), so the trees file (<prefix>.trees.nwk) goes straight to ASTRAL or any summary method. MCscan3 also counts, over all trees, every split of the columns (an unrooted bipartition), <prefix>.splits.tsv: the share of trees in which two copies group together. Copies of one polyploidy that group with different relatives point to an allopolyploidy and tell which progenitor each copy came from; a majority-rule consensus of the splits is written as <prefix>.consensus.nwk.

Writes <prefix>.trees.nwk (one tree per line), <prefix>.trees.tsv (row, reference gene, genes, tree), <prefix>.splits.tsv and <prefix>.consensus.nwk.

docs.text: Argument Description ALIGNMENT The .alignment.tsv of karyotype align.

(default: 4) --threads Gene sets aligned at once. (default: 4) --tree-tool nj (built in), fasttree or iqtree. (default: nj) --max-sets Use only the first N rows (0: all). (default: 0)

docs.title: mcscan3 ks calc
docs.text:
Ks/Ka of sequence pairs (mcscan3 ks calc; legacy compara.ks calc).

Group ks · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks calc [OPTIONS] FILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For consecutive pairs of CDS records (translated first unless a protein file is given):

  1. align the protein pair with ClustalW (default) or MUSCLE;
  2. back-translate the alignment to codons with PAL2NAL;
  3. run PAML yn00 for Yang-Nielsen and Nei-Gojobori Ks/Ka.

Writes name,yn_ks,yn_ka,ng_ks,ng_ka (-o). Needs clustalw2 (or muscle 3.8), pal2nal.pl and yn00 on PATH (or MCSCAN3_<TOOL>_PATH). Intermediate files are kept in <workdir>/syn_analysis as in the original:

mcscan3 ks calc grape.peach.cds.fasta -o grape.peach.ks --workdir=ksw

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FILES [protein FASTA] CDS FASTA with consecutive pairs.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --longest Use the longest ORF (only without a protein file). --msa Protein aligner: clustalw or muscle. (default: clustalw) --workdir Work directory (default: current directory). --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

cd core && mcscan3 ks calc grape.peach.200.cds.fasta -o grape.peach.200.ks --workdir ksw && head -4 grape.peach.200.ks

docs.title: mcscan3 ks gc3
docs.text:
Remove gene pairs with high GC3 from Ks results (mcscan3 ks gc3; legacy compara.ks gc3).

Group ks · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks gc3 [OPTIONS] KSFILE CDSFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
High-GC3 genes give unreliable Ks (the two estimates disagree strongly; Tang et al. 2010 PNAS), which is common in cereals. A pair is dropped when the mean GC content at the third codon position of its two genes is above 0.75. For two genomes, give both CDS files (or one concatenated file):

mcscan3 ks gc3 grape.peach.ks grape.cds peach.cds -o grape.peach.gc3.ks

The output is CSV with \r\n line ends, as the original's csv writer produced. The original crashed on every run (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.7). --plot also writes the GC3 values to <cdsfile>.gc3 and draws their histogram (needs plot histogram).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE Ks file. CDSFILES CDS FASTA file(s): one, or one per genome (at most 2).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --plot Also plot the GC3 histogram (see plot histogram). --outfile, -o Output Ks file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 ks kaks
docs.text:
Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks of gene pairs with MCscan3's own estimators.

Group ks · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks kaks [OPTIONS] PAIRS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, in the spirit of KaKs_Calculator: no external aligner or PAML. Each pair's proteins are aligned and threaded back onto the codons, then Ks and Ka are estimated with one or more methods (--method, comma-separated; see mcscan3.core.kaks):

  • ng86 (Nei & Gojobori 1986) and lpb93 (Li 1993; Pamilo & Bianchi 1993): counting methods, about 0.1 ms per pair after the alignment;
  • gy94: maximum likelihood under the Goldman & Yang (1994) codon model, as pairwise codeml (tens of ms per pair; parallel with --cpus).

Pairs come from a two-column file (gene1<TAB>gene2) or an anchors file; sequences from one or more CDS FASTA files:

mcscan3 ks kaks grape.grape.anchors --cds grape.cds --method lpb93,gy94 --cpus 8 -o grape.kaks.tsv

Writes gene1, gene2, codons, identity and, per method, <method>_ks, <method>_ka and <method>_kaks. Pairs below --min-identity (protein identity over the aligned codons) get empty values: maximum-likelihood Ks of near-random pairs is meaningless.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PAIRS Gene pairs: two columns, or an anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --cds CDS FASTA file(s) with the genes (repeatable). --outfile, -o Output TSV. --method ng86, lpb93, gy94 (comma-separated for several). (default: lpb93) --min-identity Leave pairs below this protein identity empty. (default: 0.0) --cpus Processes (useful for gy94). (default: 1)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks (Goldman-Yang maximum likelihood and Nei-Gojobori) of the syntenic pairs, with MCscan3's own estimators; also written as Ks tables.

cd core && cat grape.cds peach.cds poplar.cds > all.cds  && for p in grape.peach.lifted.1x1 grape.poplar.lifted.1x2 peach.poplar grape.grape; do
   mcscan3 ks kaks $p.anchors --cds all.cds --method gy94,ng86 --cpus $CPU -o ${p%%.lifted*}.kaks.tsv; done  && for p in grape.peach grape.poplar peach.poplar grape.grape; do awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)c[$i]=i; print "name,yn_ks,yn_ka,ng_ks,ng_ka"; next} $c["gy94_ks"]!=""{print $1";"$2","$c["gy94_ks"]","$c["gy94_ka"]","$c["ng86_ks"]","$c["ng86_ka"]}' $p.kaks.tsv > $p.ks; done && wc -l *.ks && head -3 grape.peach.kaks.tsv

run time 10 min 25 s · data real · showcase step ks_kaks

Variables: $CPU threads.

docs.title: mcscan3 ks strata
docs.text:
Evolutionary strata from Ks along a sex or mating-type chromosome.

Group ks · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks strata [OPTIONS] KS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after EASYstrata (Rougemont et al.; github.com/QuentinRougemont/EASYstrata) and the strata of Lahn & Page (1999, Science 286:964). Recombination stopped in steps between the two sex chromosomes (X/Y, Z/W, U/V) or mating-type chromosomes, so their gametologous gene pairs diverge in blocks: pairs in an older stratum have a higher Ks. Laid along the gene order of one chromosome (or of an ancestral genome), Ks forms steps; this command finds them.

  • gene pairs and their Ks from any table with gene1, gene2 and a ks/*_ks column (ks kaks), ordered along --bed (the genes of one haplotype, or of an ancestral genome with --ref-anchors from that genome to the haplotype), restricted to --chrom in the given order (a - suffix reverses a chromosome, e.g. --chrom X-);
  • for 0 to --max-changepoints changepoints, the optimal segmentation into strata, each with its own mean and variance of Ks (older strata vary more; Gaussian likelihood, exact by dynamic programming, at least --min-size pairs per stratum);
  • the number of strata by BIC, with BIC weights for every model (an approximation of the posterior model probabilities that the R package mcp reports through LOO);
  • 95% intervals of every changepoint by a bootstrap of the residuals within strata;
  • adjacent strata compared with a one-sided Mann-Whitney test (older stratum higher Ks).

Writes <prefix>.strata.tsv (pairs with their position and stratum), .strata.segments.tsv, .strata.models.tsv and .strata.<format> (Ks along the order with the strata, and BIC).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KS Ks of gene pairs between the two sex or mating-type chromosomes (TSV).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --bed Genes giving the order: one haplotype, or an ancestral genome. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --chrom Chromosome(s) of --bed to use, in order; NAME- reverses one. Repeatable. --ref-anchors Anchors of the ancestral genome (--bed) against one haplotype. --max-changepoints Most changepoints tried. (default: 8) --min-size Fewest gene pairs in a stratum. (default: 3) --max-ks Drop pairs with a higher Ks (0: keep all). (default: 0.0) --bootstrap Bootstrap replicates for changepoint intervals. (default: 200) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro algs
docs.text:
Ancestral linkage groups from many genomes.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro algs [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Ancestral linkage groups (ALGs) are sets of gene families that stayed together on one chromosome since a distant ancestor, e.g. the 24-29 bilaterian ALGs (Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884) or the 17 ALGs of the metazoan ancestor. Here they are found without a reference. Each pair of families is weighted by the share of the genomes having both in which they sit on one chromosome; the families are then split into groups whose pairs share a chromosome in more than --resolution (default 0.4) of the genomes on average: the Constant Potts Model (Traag et al. 2011, Phys Rev E 84:016114) optimised by Leiden when igraph is installed, else MCL. Pairs below --min-link (default 0.2) are left out of the graph, for speed. Families are used when present in at least --min-genomes genomes (default: half, at least two); groups of fewer than --min-size families are dropped. Fusions in a few lineages do not merge two ALGs (they are on one chromosome in a minority of genomes), and fissions in a few do not split one. With a rooted species tree (--tree), genomes are weighted so that each clade below a node has an equal share: a rearrangement shared by a large, densely sampled clade then counts once against its sister lineage, and the outgroups decide what was ancestral (a tie is not a link).

With --reference, each ALG is named after the chromosome of that genome holding most of its families (ref:chr, letters when several ALGs share one), else ALG01, ALG02, ... by size. ALGs that are already known (e.g. the bilaterian ALGs on amphioxus genes) are given with --known gene<TAB>ALG; families then take the ALG of most of their genes in that table:

mcscan3 macro algs *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa --reference amphioxus
mcscan3 macro algs *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa --known bfl_blg.tsv

Writes <prefix>.algs.tsv (family, ALG) and <prefix>.alg_summary.tsv (per ALG: families and, per genome, the chromosome holding most of them and its share).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --known Known ALGs as geneALG (instead of finding them). --tree Rooted species tree: weight genomes by clade. --reference Name ALGs after this genome's chromosomes. --resolution Least mean co-location within an ALG. (default: 0.4) --min-link Family pairs co-located less are ignored. (default: 0.2) --min-genomes Families in fewer genomes are left out (default: half). --min-size Smallest ALG (families). (default: 10) --seed Random seed (Leiden). (default: 666) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro ancestors
docs.text:
Ancestral karyotypes on a species tree from BUSCO genes, and the rearrangements of every branch

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro ancestors [OPTIONS] TABLES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
(mcscan3 macro ancestors).

New in MCscan3, after syngraph (github.com/A-J-F-Mackintosh/syngraph; bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2023.09.17.558111), reimplemented from its description. Needs only the BUSCO full_table.tsv of each chromosome-level assembly (or a marker<TAB>sequence<TAB>start<TAB>end table of any single-copy markers) and a rooted species tree, for instance the one of mcscan3 phylo busco (--synteny there runs this step directly):

  1. karyotypes: a genome is the partition of its single-copy markers into chromosomes; sequences with fewer than --min-chrom-markers markers (unplaced contigs, which would read as fissions) are left out;
  2. ancestors: the karyotype of each internal node is the median of its children and its outgroup (the sibling lineage): the partition needing the fewest fissions and fusions to reach them. Turning karyotype A into B by fissions and fusions alone takes |A| + |B| - 2c events, where c counts the connected components of the graph joining chromosomes of A and B that share markers. Starting from the common refinement of the inputs (marker sets on one chromosome in every input), merging two groups saves an event for every input in which they are already connected and costs one for every input in which they are not, so groups are merged greedily while the weighted inputs favour it. Marker sets smaller than --min-markers (a single moved BUSCO, often an orthology error) do not vote and join the group most inputs place them with. The tree is solved from the leaves up with the children alone, then again with outgroups until no ancestor changes. The root has no outgroup: ties between its children are broken by its grandchildren (together less than one vote), so a fusion seen in only one of the two lineages is placed in that lineage;
  3. rearrangements of each branch: in each component of the parent-child graph (edges of --min-markers markers or more) with a parental and b child chromosomes, b - 1 fissions and a - 1 fusions; a component of two chromosomes on each side exchanging markers both ways is one reciprocal translocation (--no-translocations counts it as two fissions and two fusions). On branches to extant genomes the markers must also lie in a stretch of --min-markers consecutive markers (one foreign marker allowed), as a moved segment does; scattered moves and moves below --min-markers (orthology errors, mostly) are counted as noise, not events.

Chromosomes of ancestors are named <node>_<i> by size; --reference adds which chromosomes of that genome each one became. Writes <prefix>.rearrangements.tsv (parent, child, event, multiplicity, markers, chromosomes), <prefix>.nodes.tsv (per node: chromosomes, markers, events on the branch above), <prefix>.karyotypes.tsv (every marker on every node), <prefix>.algs.tsv (markers of the ancestral chromosomes of --node, the root by default, as linkage groups for plot busco --algs and the other macro commands), <prefix>.fates.tsv (each linkage group in each genome: intact, fused, split, split and fused, absent), <prefix>.tree.nwk (with node names) and four figures: <prefix>.ancestors (the tree with every ancestral karyotype drawn at its node, events on the branches and the extant chromosomes painted by linkage group), <prefix>.flows (ribbons from parental to child chromosomes on each rearranged branch), <prefix>.fates (fate of every linkage group in every genome beside the tree) and <prefix>.rates (chromosome number along each lineage; rearrangements against branch length):

mcscan3 macro ancestors busco/*/full_table.tsv --tree species.nwk --reference Bmori -o lep

docs.text: Argument Description TABLES BUSCO full_table.tsv files or run folders (or marker tables), as PATH or NAME=PATH.

(default: 5) --min-chrom-markers Sequences with fewer markers (unplaced contigs) are left out. (default: 10) --translocations Call reciprocal translocations (else fissions+fusions). --reference Name chromosomes after this genome's chromosomes. --node Node whose chromosomes are written as linkage groups (root). --format Figure format. (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro fusions
docs.text:
Fusions, fissions and mixing of ancestral linkage groups in each genome.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro fusions [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. With ALGs from macro algs, every chromosome of every genome is tested for the ALGs it carries (one-sided Fisher test of chromosome x ALG gene counts, Benjamini-Hochberg; an ALG is carried with at least --min-genes genes). A chromosome carrying two or more ALGs is a fusion; an ALG carried by two or more chromosomes of a genome is split (fission).

After a fusion, intrachromosomal rearrangements gradually interleave the genes of the fused ALGs. Such fusion-with-mixing cannot be undone and so marks clades (Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884; Schultz et al. 2023, Nature 618:110). Mixing is measured from the order of the ALG genes along the chromosome by the number of runs (blocks of consecutive genes of one ALG): k runs for k unmixed ALGs, about 1 + (n - 1)(1 - sum n_i(n_i - 1) / (n(n - 1))) for a random order. The mixing index scales the observed runs from 0 (unmixed) to 1 (random), and a permutation test (--permutations) gives the chance that a random order has as few runs: below --alpha, the ALGs are still in separate segments (fusion, A+B); otherwise they are mixed (fusion-with-mixing, A x B). Every pair of ALGs on a chromosome is scored the same way.

Each fused pair of ALGs (A+B, any mixing) and each mixed pair (A x B) is then a character present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.characters.tsv, a profile matrix). With a rooted species tree (--tree) the characters are mapped onto it, giving the branch on which each fusion happened: by irreversible (Camin-Sokal) parsimony by default, since fusions, and above all fusions with mixing, are not undone, while the same fusion can arise in parallel in two lineages; --model dollo places each fusion once, at the last common ancestor of the genomes having it:

mcscan3 macro fusions *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --algs metazoa.algs.tsv -o metazoa --tree sp.nwk

Writes <prefix>.chromosomes.tsv (per genome and chromosome: genes, ALGs carried, state, runs, mixing index, p), <prefix>.alg_pairs.tsv (per genome, every pair of ALGs on one chromosome), <prefix>.splits.tsv (ALGs on several chromosomes), <prefix>.characters.tsv and, with --tree, <prefix>.gainloss.tsv / .origins.tsv / .gainloss.nwk.

docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --algs ALGs from macro algs (.algs.tsv). --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --tree Rooted species tree: map fusions onto it. --model irreversible (parallel fusions, no reversals) or dollo (one origin). (default: irreversible) --alpha Significance of carried ALGs and of unmixed order. (default: 0.05) --min-alg-genes Fewest genes of an ALG on a chromosome. (default: 10) --permutations Permutations of the mixing test. (default: 1000) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro plot
docs.text:
Macrosynteny figures.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro plot [OPTIONS] PREFIX BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• oxford: an Oxford dot plot of two genomes, one dot per gene pair of a shared family at the genes' positions (gene ranks) along the concatenated chromosomes, coloured by ALG when ALGs are given. Chromosomes of the second genome are ordered by the chromosome of the first they are most enriched with (macro test), so homologous chromosomes line up on the diagonal; cells of significant chromosome pairs are shaded.
  • painting: every genome as a row of chromosome bars, each gene a thin stripe coloured by its ALG, so fusions (several colours on one bar), fissions (one colour on several bars) and mixing (interleaved stripes) are seen at a glance across many genomes.

docs.title: mcscan3 macro test
docs.text:
Which chromosomes of two genomes descend from the same ancestral chromosome.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro test [OPTIONS] BED_A BED_B

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Between distantly related genomes (hundreds of millions of years), gene order is lost but genes stay on the chromosomes they came from: macrosynteny (Simakov et al. 2020, Nature Ecology & Evolution 4:820; Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884). For every pair of chromosomes, the number of gene families with genes on both is compared with what the chromosome sizes alone would give by the one-sided Fisher exact test, and adjusted for the number of pairs (Benjamini-Hochberg; --adjust bonferroni|holm|none). Families come from an orthogroup table (--families) or from reciprocal best hits in a BLAST table (--hits):

mcscan3 macro test amphioxus.bed scallop.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o amph.scallop

Writes <prefix>.macro.tsv, one row per chromosome pair: shared families, expected, the ratio, p and adjusted q, and whether the pair is significant (q <= --alpha and at least --min-count families); prints the significant pairs. macro plot --kind oxford draws them.

(default: bh) --alpha Largest adjusted p of a significant pair. (default: 0.05) --min-count Fewest shared families of a significant pair. (default: 3) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 micro ancestral
docs.text:
Ancestral microsyntenic blocks at every node of the species tree, and what became of them in each species.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro ancestral [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. micro blocks finds blocks of genes kept together in extant genomes. micro ancestral asks the phylogenetic question instead: which groups of families were neighbours in each ancestor, and did each descendant keep them close, keep them only on the same chromosome, or break them up? The method follows SYNPHONI (Robert et al. 2022, Bioinformatics), reimplemented from its description.

  1. Co-located family pairs. In each genome, the fewest genes between two genes of two families on the same chromosome are counted, up to --window genes. Pairs found in only one genome are dropped.
  2. An ancestral network for each node. Around a node, the species fall into groups: the clade of each child, and the outgroup (every other species). A group has a pair when at least --min-species of its species have it, or all of them if the group is smaller. A pair is ancestral to the node when a child clade and at least one other group have it. A pair on both sides of the node was present in the ancestor, while a pair found in one clade alone may be a rearrangement within that clade. The ancestral distance of a pair is its median distance in the species of those groups.
  3. Ancestral blocks.
    • Edges of the network longer than nmax genes are cut.
    • The connected groups of at least --min-families families that are also cliques of the full network (every pair of their families ancestrally co-located) are the ancestral blocks.
    • nmax is chosen for each node from a curve: the share of families in the largest connected group as the cut-off grows. The curve is sigmoid, and nmax is its elbow just before the steep rise, where separate blocks begin to merge. --nmax overrides it.
  4. Descendants. In every species, each ancestral block is one of:
    • compact: at least --coverage of its families (and at least two) within nmax genes of each other, so microsynteny is kept;
    • dispersed: as many on one chromosome but no longer close, so only macrosynteny is kept;
    • split: its families spread over several chromosomes;
    • lost.

The tree does not need branch lengths, and it may have polytomies. Nodes are named by their label in the Newick file if they have one, otherwise N<i>:<first tip>..<last tip>. --node selects nodes by label, by N<i>, or by two tips (--node human,fly).

With few species on each side of a node (for example a node with two tips), chance neighbours shared by two genomes enter the network. Raise --min-species on large trees; the default of 3 is SYNPHONI's.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
mcscan3 micro ancestral *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --tree species.nwk -o metazoa
mcscan3 micro ancestral *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --tree species.nwk --node Bilateria --node human,fly -o two

pipeline run runs it as the microsynteny step on its orthogroups and species tree.

(2022) Bioinformatics 38:5434-5436), reimplemented from its description: node-specific ancestral family networks from co-location in child clades and the outgroup, distance cut-off at the elbow of the largest-component curve, clique-checked blocks, and each block in every descendant as compact, dispersed, split or lost.

docs.title: mcscan3 micro blocks
docs.text:
Microsynteny blocks shared by many distant genomes.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro blocks [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the multi-species microsynteny of Simakov et al. (2013, Nature 493:526), Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289, metazoan microsynteny) and Robert et al. (2022, BMC Genomics 23:143, syntenic density). Over hundreds of millions of years gene order decays to small groups of genes that stay together in any order: microsynteny. A block is found in four steps, all on integer arrays:

  1. co-location: in each genome, two genes of different families are co-located when at most --max-gap genes lie between them (all genes count, so the gap is in the genome's own units);
  2. conserved pairs: a pair of families co-located in at least --min-genomes genomes;
  3. family groups: the conserved pairs form a graph of families, weighted 0.5 + 0.5 x the share of genomes with the pair (so the blocks of one lineage still count). It is cut into groups of tightly co-located families by the Constant Potts Model (Leiden, --resolution: the least mean weight within a group). Unlike single linkage, this does not chain neighbouring blocks into whole chromosome arms in closely related genomes; in distant genomes the groups are the isolated blocks themselves;
  4. blocks: in each genome, the genes of a group form runs along the chromosome (at most --max-gap genes between neighbours); a run with at least --min-families families is the block in that genome. A family found in fewer than half the genomes having its group is a chance neighbour and is dropped (and the runs found again). Blocks found in at least --min-genomes genomes are kept; their core families are those in at least two genomes;
  5. significance: a block's E-value is the number of blocks as large (core families), as compact (median span) and as widespread (genomes) expected by chance in genomes of random gene order; blocks above --max-evalue are left out. Small loose blocks shared by two genomes arise by chance surprisingly often; micro density checks the rest by shuffling.

Each block is then present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.profile.tsv, the profile format of network), so micro nodes dates it on a species tree, and micro density measures how tightly packed it is:

mcscan3 micro blocks *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (block, genomes, families, core families), <prefix>.members.tsv (block, genome, chromosome, first and last gene rank, genes in the span, block genes, families) and <prefix>.profile.tsv.

(default: 3) --resolution Least mean co-location weight within a family group. (default: 0.5) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 8) --seed Random seed. (default: 666)

docs.title: mcscan3 micro coexpr
docs.text:
Co-expression of the genes of microsynteny blocks.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro coexpr [OPTIONS] MEMBERS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289; reimplemented from the paper and its published code, metazoan_synteny): genes kept together for hundreds of millions of years may be kept together because they are expressed together. For every block of micro blocks in a genome with an expression matrix (tissues, conditions or cell types as columns), MCscan3 measures:

  • co-expression: the mean Pearson correlation of all pairs of block genes over the conditions (averaged through Fisher's z) on log2(CPM + 1), each condition first centred over all genes (--no-center: not), so a tissue where nearly every gene is low (pollen, seed) does not make every set of genes look co-expressed;
  • against three kinds of random blocks with the same number of expressed genes, drawn --draws times each (default 10,000): shuffled (genes drawn from all block genes of the genome, so the gene content is shuffled among blocks), sampled (runs of neighbouring genes anywhere in the genome) and sampled orthologs (runs of neighbouring genes that have a family, so only genes with homologs elsewhere, as block genes are). The empirical P-value of a block is against the sampled runs; Q-values by Benjamini-Hochberg;

  • specificity: tau of each gene (Yanai et al. 2005, Bioinformatics 21:650) averaged over the block, and the condition bias: the condition holding the largest mean share of the block genes' expression, as a fold over an even spread; Random blocks are drawn --draws times for each number of expressed genes and shared by all blocks of that size. Blocks on organelle chromosomes (--skip-chroms: Pt, Mt, chrC, chrM...) are left out, as organelle genes are transcribed together as operons.

  • paralog share: genes of a block whose family has another gene in the same block;

  • gaps: the number of other genes between neighbouring block genes, with a negative binomial fitted by moments:
mcscan3 micro coexpr eudicots.members.tsv --expr ath=ath.counts.tsv --bed ath=ath.bed \
    --families Orthogroups.tsv -o eudicots.coexpr

Gene IDs of the blocks and of the matrix are matched as they are, then without a version suffix (--strip). Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (one line per block and genome), <prefix>.genomes.tsv (observed against random blocks, Mann-Whitney), <prefix>.gaps.tsv and the figures <prefix>.<fmt> (distributions), <prefix>.top.<fmt> (expression of the most co-expressed blocks) and <prefix>.bias.<fmt> (blocks by condition).

(default: []) --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily (homolog runs, paralogs). --by-sample Samples as columns instead of condition means. --min-cpm Genes below this CPM in every condition are left out. docs.title: mcscan3 micro density
docs.text:
Syntenic density of microsynteny blocks, against shuffled genomes.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro density [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the syntenic density of Robert et al. (2022, BMC Genomics 23:143: distinct density regimes and their transitions in early animal genomes). The density of a block in a genome is the share of the genes in its span that belong to it: 1 for a compact block, low when other genes have been inserted between its members. Per genome the command reports the blocks, the genes in them, the share of the genome they cover, and the median density and span.

False blocks. Some blocks arise by chance, more so with many genomes, large gaps and small blocks. Each genome in turn has its gene order shuffled (--shuffles times; the families and the other genomes stay as they are) and the blocks are found again: the blocks still found in the shuffled genome are chance blocks, and their mean over the shuffles, divided by the blocks found in the real genome, estimates the share of false blocks (FDR) at these settings.

Transitions. With --tree, every block is dated (micro nodes) and the density of the blocks arisen at each node is compared with that of the blocks of its parent (Mann-Whitney U, Benjamini-Hochberg): a shift marks a transition between density regimes:

mcscan3 micro density *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --tree species.nwk -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.density.tsv (per genome), <prefix>.members.tsv with each block's density, <prefix>.transitions.tsv with --tree, and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

(default: 2) --min-families Fewest families of a block in a genome. (default: 3) --resolution Least mean co-location weight within a family group. (default: 0.5) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 8) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. docs.title: mcscan3 micro nodes
docs.text:
Microsynteny blocks dated on the species tree.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro nodes [OPTIONS] PROFILE TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Simakov et al. (2013, Nature 493:526) and Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289). The presence of each block of micro blocks in each genome is mapped onto a rooted species tree by Dollo parsimony (a block arises once, at the last common ancestor of the genomes having it, and may be lost): the blocks ancestral at each node (present there), the novel ones (arisen on the branch above it) and the lost ones:

mcscan3 micro nodes metazoa.profile.tsv species.nwk -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.gainloss.tsv (per node: genomes below, novel, lost and ancestral blocks), <prefix>.origins.tsv (per block: node of origin and nodes of loss), <prefix>.gainloss.nwk and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 network build
docs.text:
Build a synteny network from anchors files.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network build [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the synteny network approach of Zhao & Schranz (2017, PNAS; 2019, PNAS), reimplemented from the papers with MCscan3's synteny. Nodes are genes; edges are syntenic anchor pairs from all pairwise (and self) comparisons. The species of each gene comes from the anchors file name, <speciesA>.<speciesB>.anchors: the first column is A, the second is B:

mcscan3 network build *.anchors -o net

Pairs can also come as one table (--table): block, score, gene1, gene2 (or block, gene1, gene2), as written by other synteny-network tools. The species of each gene is then taken from the gene tables in --genes-dir (<species>.bed, BED or the MCScanX layout chr, gene, start, end`; a `<species>__` prefix on gene names is dropped, and `<species><gene><species> is also recognised):

mcscan3 network build --table blocks.tsv.gz --genes-dir genomes/ -o net

Writes <prefix>.edges.tsv (species1, gene1, species2, gene2, source, where the source is the anchors file and block) and prints the numbers of species, nodes and edges.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILES Anchors files named ..anchors.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --table Pairs as one table: block, [score,] gene1, gene2. --genes-dir Gene tables .bed for --table. --compact Write the compact store .net.npz (about 2 bytes per edge) instead of .edges.tsv.

docs.title: mcscan3 network cluster
docs.text:
Cluster a synteny network.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network cluster [OPTIONS] EDGES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the synteny-network work of Zhao & Schranz (2017, 2019). The network from network build is split into clusters of genes that are syntenic with one another, each usually one ancestral syntenic locus. Five methods are available:

  • mcl, Markov clustering (van Dongen 2000; default; --inflation), run on blocks of the matrix in parallel threads (--cpus), or on a GPU with --device auto|cuda|mps: connected components are batched into dense matrix products on the device (PyTorch or CuPy; see mcscan3.core.gpu), for networks of many species;
  • leiden, the Leiden algorithm (Traag, Waltman & van Eck 2019, Scientific Reports 9:5233; --seed), which guarantees connected communities, unlike Louvain. By default it optimises the Constant Potts Model (--objective cpm): a cluster must be denser inside than --resolution (default 0.1), which finds small loci however large the network is. Modularity (--objective modularity, resolution 1) cannot see communities below a size that grows with the network (Fortunato & Barthélemy 2007, PNAS 104:36) and merges loci. Needs the optional igraph package (pip install mcscan3[network]);
  • infomap, communities that compress a random walk best (Rosvall & Bergstrom 2008, PNAS 105:1118; --trials), as used by the original synteny-network work; igraph;
  • louvain, modularity communities (Blondel et al. 2008; networkx, --seed);
  • components, connected components, which merges clusters joined by any edge.

mcl, leiden and infomap give similar locus-level clusters (network compare measures how similar):

mcscan3 network cluster net.edges.tsv -o net

Writes <prefix>.clusters.tsv (cluster, size, species, members, where members are species|gene, comma-separated), largest cluster first.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description EDGES Edge list from network build.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --method mcl, leiden, infomap, louvain or components. (default: mcl) --inflation MCL inflation. (default: 2.0) --objective Leiden: cpm (Constant Potts Model) or modularity. (default: cpm) --resolution Leiden resolution, larger: smaller clusters (default: 0.1 cpm, 1 modularity). --trials Infomap trials. (default: 10) --seed Random seed (leiden, infomap, louvain). (default: 666) --min-size Smallest cluster written. (default: 2) --cpus Threads for MCL, 0 = all. (default: 0) --device MCL on cpu, or a GPU: auto, cuda, mps, cupy. (default: cpu)

docs.title: mcscan3 network compare
docs.text:
How similar two clusterings of a synteny network are.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network compare [OPTIONS] FIRST SECOND

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Compares two network cluster results (e.g. MCL and Leiden, or two inflation values) on the genes that both cluster:

  • the adjusted Rand index (Hubert & Arabie 1985, J Classif 2:193): agreement on which pairs of genes are together, 1 for identical clusterings and about 0 for unrelated ones;
  • the normalised mutual information (arithmetic normalisation; Strehl & Ghosh 2002, JMLR 3:583; Danon et al. 2005);
  • clusters of the first that the second splits, and clusters of the second that merge clusters of the first:
mcscan3 network compare mcl.clusters.tsv leiden.clusters.tsv

Prints the comparison; --out writes, per cluster of the first, where its genes went.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FIRST Clusters from network cluster. SECOND Other clusters of the same network.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --out Write where the genes of each first cluster went.

docs.title: mcscan3 network gainloss
docs.text:
Where syntenic loci arose and were lost on the species tree.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network gainloss [OPTIONS] PROFILE_FILE SPECIES_TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each synteny cluster (a syntenic locus, network profile) is mapped onto a rooted species tree by Dollo parsimony (Farris 1977, Syst Zool 26:77): a locus arises once, on the branch above the last common ancestor of the species that have it, and is lost on as few branches as possible below it. A locus found in only some lineages is either young (a gain: a lineage- specific transposition or new gene arrangement) or old and lost; the synteny-based phylogenomics of Zhao et al. (2021, Nature Communications 12:3498) reads such presence/absence characters for the history of genome structure:

mcscan3 network gainloss net.profile.tsv species.nwk -o net

Writes <prefix>.gainloss.tsv (per branch, named by its node: leaves below, loci gained on it, loci lost on it, loci present at its end), <prefix>.origins.tsv (per cluster: the node where it arose and the nodes where it was lost) and <prefix>.gainloss.nwk (the tree with the node names used). Internal nodes without a name in the tree are named N1, N2, ... from the root. Species of the profile missing from the tree are an error; tree tips missing from the profile have no loci.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PROFILE_FILE Profile matrix from network profile. SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick file or text).

docs.title: mcscan3 network groups
docs.text:
Synteny clusters specific to a group of species, and the sub-network of a gene family

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network groups [OPTIONS] PROFILE_FILE GROUPS_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
(mcscan3 network groups).

New in MCscan3, after the group-specific clusters of syntenet (Almeida-Silva et al. 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btac806) and the family sub-networks of SynNet (Zhao & Schranz 2019, PNAS).

groups: the profile of network profile (clusters x species) and a table of species and their group (family, order, ecotype; species<TAB>group). A cluster is specific to a group when every species holding it belongs to that group and at least --min-percent of the group's species hold it. MCscan3 adds a test: for every cluster and group, Fisher's exact test of the presence in the group's species against the other species, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, finds the clusters enriched in a group even when an outsider or two hold them too (--fdr). Writes <prefix>.groups.tsv (cluster, group, species of the group holding it, percent, species outside holding it, p, FDR, specific, enriched) and <prefix>.groups.summary.tsv (per group: species, specific clusters, enriched clusters).

The sub-network of a gene family is network extract (mcscan3.features.network.extract).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PROFILE_FILE Profile matrix from network profile. GROUPS_FILE speciesgroup table.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --min-percent Specific: share of the group's species holding it. (default: 50.0) --fdr Enriched: largest FDR of Fisher's exact test. (default: 0.05)

docs.title: mcscan3 network plot
docs.text:
Figures of a synteny network.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network plot [OPTIONS] PREFIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the figures of the synteny-network papers (Zhao & Schranz 2017, 2019) and Tree2GD. --kind selects one or more (comma-separated, or all):

  • heatmap: species x species synteny similarity (Jaccard of their syntenic clusters), ordered by the species tree. The lower triangle is the raw similarity; the upper triangle is phylogeny-corrected: the similarity each pair would have at the average tree distance (its residual from an exponential decay with tree distance, fitted to all pairs, added to the decay at the mean distance). Both halves are Jaccard similarities on one colour scale; pairs darker above than below kept more synteny than their divergence predicts;
  • profile: the phylogenomic profile in the layout of the synteny-network papers: species as rows (species tree on the left, a clade strip), the largest --max-clusters clusters as columns ordered by average-linkage clustering of their presence (dendrogram on top), presence dark (--profile-style binary) or shaded by copy number (copies). Shared and lineage-specific synteny show as blocks. Clades come from --clades (speciesclade) or are cut from the tree (best with a balanced, trusted tree);
  • graph: the species network, edges weighted by shared clusters (the strongest --top share of the pairs);
  • cluster: the gene network of one cluster (--cluster), force-directed, nodes coloured by clade.

    • The species tree (--tree) orders the figures; without it, the network tree (network tree) is used. Distances are patristic when the tree has branch lengths, else in nodes:

    mcscan3 network plot net --tree species.nwk --kind all -o net

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PREFIX Prefix of the network files (.profile.tsv, .clusters.tsv, ...).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --tree Species tree (Newick) (default: .tree.nwk). --kind heatmap, profile, graph, cluster (comma-separated) or all. (default: all) --cluster Cluster for --kind cluster (default: the largest). --max-clusters Profile: largest clusters shown. (default: 2000) --top Graph: share of the strongest species pairs drawn. (default: 0.3) --profile-style Profile: binary (presence) or copies. (default: binary) --clades speciesclade colours (default: cut from the tree). --edges Edge list for --kind cluster (default: .edges.tsv). --outfile, -o Output prefix (default: the network prefix). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

Phylogenomic profiles of synteny clusters.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the synteny-network work of Zhao & Schranz (2019, PNAS). For each cluster from network cluster, counts its genes in each species. Clusters present in only some lineages are the shared or lost syntenic loci that phylogenomic synteny profiling uses:

Prints the numbers of clusters shared by all species and private to each.

docs.title: mcscan3 network run
docs.text:
A synteny network project that grows genome by genome.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network run [OPTIONS] GENOMES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the network building and genome adding of SynNet (Zhao & Schranz 2017, PNAS 114:E2203; 2019, PNAS 116:2165) and syntenet (Almeida-Silva et al. 2023). A project is a folder: give it a folder of genomes (<name>.bed with <name>.pep, as prep genome writes them) and run it again whenever genomes are added; only the new pairs are compared:

mcscan3 network run genomes/ -o brassicaceae.net --cpus 16
cp new/*.bed new/*.pep genomes/
mcscan3 network run genomes/ -o brassicaceae.net --cpus 16      # only the new pairs run

For every pair of genomes (and every genome with itself, unless --no-self) the proteins are compared with DIAMOND in both directions (--hits best hits per protein and genome) and the syntenic blocks found with MCscan3's synteny scan (--min-size anchors, --dist genes). The project then builds the network, clusters it, writes the species profiles, a species tree from them and the statistics.

The project stays small whatever the number of genomes:

  • the hits of a pair are deleted as soon as its blocks are found (--keep-hits keeps them);
  • the blocks of each pair are kept gzipped, anchors/<a>.<b>.anchors.gz: the network can be rebuilt from them at any time, with other settings, without aligning again;
  • the network is the compact store net.net.npz (about 2 bytes per edge);
  • the DIAMOND databases are deleted at the end;
  • network.json records the genomes (paths and checksums of their files), the settings and the pairs done, so an interrupted run resumes where it stopped, a genome whose files changed is compared again, and a run with other settings refuses to mix results (--redo starts over).

Writes, in the project folder: network.json, anchors/, net.net.npz, net.clusters.tsv, net.profile.tsv, net.tree.nwk (with three genomes or more), net.stats.tsv and the figures of network plot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Folder of genomes: .bed with .pep (prepared).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Project folder (created, or grown when it exists). --cpus Threads for DIAMOND, 0 = all. (default: 0) --hits Best hits per protein and genome. (default: 5) --evalue DIAMOND e-value cutoff. (default: 1e-05) --sensitivity DIAMOND mode: fast, sensitive, more-sensitive... --min-size Fewest anchors in a block. (default: 5) --dist Largest gap between anchors of a block (genes). (default: 20) --no-self Do not compare each genome with itself. --method Clustering: mcl, leiden, infomap, louvain or components. (default: mcl) --outgroup Root the profile tree on this genome. --groups speciesgroup table: clusters specific to a group. --drop-missing Drop genomes no longer in the folder. --keep-hits Keep the DIAMOND hits (large). --redo Compare every pair again. --only-build Rebuild and analyse the network; compare nothing. --format Image format. (default: pdf)

docs.title: mcscan3 network stats
docs.text:
Statistics of synteny clusters and the links between them.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network stats [OPTIONS] EDGES CLUSTERS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For each cluster from network cluster (a syntenic locus), with the network from network build:

  • size, species, copies: genes, species, the most genes of one species and the species with two or more (retained duplicates, e.g. after a whole-genome duplication);
  • density: edges inside the cluster over all possible (1 for a locus syntenic in every pair);
  • leaving: the share of its genes' edges that go to other clusters (low: a well-separated locus);
  • class, pan-synteny classes after pan-genome practice (e.g. Kaas et al. 2012, BMC Genomics 13:577): core (every species), softcore (at least --softcore, default 95%, of them), shell, cloud (under --cloud, default 15%) and private (one species).

Clusters joined by many edges are listed as links (<prefix>.links.tsv): syntenic loci that are adjacent or were duplicated together, the trace of segmental duplications, translocations and fusions in the network. The summary gives the modularity of the clustering (Newman & Girvan 2004, Phys Rev E 69:026113; higher: the clusters explain the network better) and the share of edges inside clusters:

mcscan3 network stats net.edges.tsv net.clusters.tsv -o net

Writes <prefix>.cluster_stats.tsv and <prefix>.links.tsv; prints the summary.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description EDGES Edge list from network build. CLUSTERS Clusters from network cluster.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --softcore Share of species of a softcore cluster. (default: 0.95) --cloud Clusters in fewer species than this share are cloud. (default: 0.15) --min-links Fewest edges between two clusters listed as a link. (default: 3)

docs.title: mcscan3 network tree
docs.text:
Species tree from synteny-cluster profiles.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network tree [OPTIONS] PROFILE_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the phylogenomic synteny profiling of Zhao & Schranz (2019, PNAS). Species are compared by which synteny clusters they share: the Jaccard distance between their presence/absence profiles (--distance jaccard) or the fraction of differing clusters (hamming). A tree is built by neighbour joining (--method nj) or UPGMA:

mcscan3 network tree net.profile.tsv -o net --outgroup rice

Writes <prefix>.tree.nwk and <prefix>.distances.tsv. --outgroup roots the tree. For a maximum-likelihood tree, give the PHYLIP matrix of network profile --phylip to RAxML or IQ-TREE.

docs.title: Arguments

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --distance jaccard or hamming. (default: jaccard) --method nj or upgma. (default: nj) --outgroup Root the tree on this species.

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog enrich
docs.text:
Add genes that OMG missed to its families (mcscan3 ortholog enrich; legacy compara.catalog enrich).

docs.title: Synopsis

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For each OMG family (genes<TAB>taxa from ortholog omg-parse) that lacks some of the ntaxa taxa, candidates are the other members of the first gene's group (groups file, one comma-separated group per line) from the missing taxa. docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog hogs
docs.text:
Hierarchical orthologous groups at every node of the species tree.

Group ortholog · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog hogs [OPTIONS] SPECIES_TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the bottom-up HOG inference of OMA and FastOMA (Altenhoff AM et al. 2013, PLoS One 8:e53786; Majidian S et al. 2025, Nat Methods 22:269), with synteny as extra evidence. A HOG at a node is the set of genes descending from one ancestral gene of that node. Within each gene family (--families; without it, the connected groups of the hits), HOGs are built from the leaves to the root:

  1. at a species, every gene is a HOG;
  2. at a node, every HOG of each child is linked to its best match among the HOGs of each other child (the highest bit score between their genes; matches within --ratio of the best count too). Bit scores of gene pairs in a synteny block (--anchors) are raised by --synteny-bonus (x 1.5 by default), so the positional copy wins among close paralogs. A syntenic pair whose two genes both lie in clearly stronger blocks (median bit score) of the same two genomes is set aside: after a duplication and differential loss, the weaker block pairs paralogs (pseudo-orthologs), the stronger one is where the orthologs were;
  3. links are taken from the strongest down and join HOGs into the node's HOGs, except that two HOGs of the same child are joined only when they are at least as similar to each other as the link (they are paralogs from a duplication after the node, in-paralogs); otherwise they come from a duplication before the node and stay in different HOGs;
  4. a HOG left alone is kept at the node only when its genes match genes outside the node (the gene was there and was lost in the other children); otherwise it arose in the child's lineage.

A node's HOGs are its ancestral genes. Two genes of two species are orthologs when they are in the same HOG at the species' last common ancestor; a HOG that holds two HOGs of one child marks a duplication on the branch to that child:

mcscan3 ortholog hogs species.nwk --bed-dir data --hits *.last --anchors *.anchors \
    --families Orthogroups.tsv -o eudicots

Writes <prefix>.hogs.tsv (node, HOG, parent HOG, species, genes), <prefix>.genes.tsv (the HOG of every gene at every node above it), <prefix>.orthoxml (OrthoXML 0.4, with ortholog and paralog groups) and <prefix>.summary.tsv (per node: HOGs, duplications, gains).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick); leaves are .bed names.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --hits Homology hits (BLAST tabular / LAST m8), all species pairs. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed-dir Directory of the .bed files. (default: .) --anchors Synteny anchors files: links in blocks weigh more. --families Gene families to split (default: from the hits). --synteny-bonus Score factor of links inside synteny blocks. (default: 1.5) --ratio Least score, relative to a gene's best, of a kept link. (default: 0.9) --max-family Largest family split (larger ones are skipped). (default: 3000) --format Image format of the tree figure. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Hierarchical orthologous groups at every node of the eudicot tree, guided by synteny.

mkdir -p hogs && H=() && A=() && for a in amborella grape ath poplar peach soybean; do for b in amborella grape ath poplar peach soybean; do [ -e $R/synteny/$a.$b.last ] && H+=(--hits $R/synteny/$a.$b.last);  [ $a != $b ] && [ -e $R/synteny/$a.$b.lifted.anchors ] && A+=(--anchors $R/synteny/$a.$b.lifted.anchors); done; done;  mcscan3 ortholog hogs $R/ancestral/species.nwk --bed-dir $R/data "${H[@]}" "${A[@]}" --families $R/orthology/orthofinder/Results_mcscan3/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv -o hogs/eudicots

run time 1 min 34 s · data real · showcase step ortholog_hogs

Variables: $R the eudicot pipeline run (six genomes).
