docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog qc
docs.text:
Quality of orthogroups, genomes and annotations.

Group ortholog · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog qc [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the orthogroup and genome checks of cogeqc (Almeida-Silva F & Van de Peer Y, Bioconductor), reimplemented with its own scores. Reads orthogroups from:

  • an OrthoFinder results folder (Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv, unassigned genes, duplications per species tree node, the rooted species tree), or Orthogroups.tsv / N0.tsv alone;
  • MCscan3 HOGs (ortholog hogs: <prefix>.genes.tsv; every gene in its topmost HOG, or the HOGs at --node);
  • a long table (group, species, gene) or one group per line (genes, with --pep/--bed for their species).

and reports, for every species: genes, genes in orthogroups, unassigned genes, orthogroups with the species, species-specific orthogroups and their genes, single- and multi-copy orthogroups, duplications (OrthoFinder); orthogroups shared by every pair of species; orthogroup sizes and copy numbers. With domains (--domains, any of the formats of mcscan3.core.domains, or --pfam Pfam-A.hmm to search the proteomes) every orthogroup gets:

  • homogeneity H: the mean Sørensen-Dice similarity 2|A∩B|/(|A|+|B|) of the domain sets of all pairs of its annotated genes (genes without domains are left out; up to --max-size genes, sampled beyond). H is also given within each species, and for orthogroups of the same sizes with the domain sets shuffled among genes (what chance gives);
  • dispersal D: for each domain, (groups holding it − 1) / (genes with it − 1), 0 when all its genes are in one orthogroup and 1 when every gene is alone; D of an orthogroup is the mean over its domains. Unassigned genes count as groups of one, so domains split by under-clustering raise D;
  • score H − D: high for orthogroups that are both internally consistent and not split.

With --busco (BUSCO or phylo busco runs) and --genome (assemblies) the genome table adds completeness, assembly length, N50/L50 of scaffolds and contigs, GC and gaps. --compare measures agreement with a second grouping (orthogroups kept exactly, split, merged; best Jaccard; adjusted Rand index):

mcscan3 ortholog qc --orthofinder Results_Oct26 --domains pfam.domtbl --busco ath=busco_ath -o qc

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --orthofinder OrthoFinder results folder (or Orthogroups.tsv). --groups Orthogroups: MCscan3 HOG genes.tsv, a group/species/gene table or a group list. --node Node of the HOGs to use (default: the root). --pep Proteome NAME=FASTA (gene species, protein stats; repeatable). (default: []) --bed Annotation NAME=BED (gene species and counts; repeatable). (default: []) --domains Domains: gene/domain table, HMMER domtblout, pfam_scan or InterProScan (repeatable). (default: []) --pfam Pfam-A.hmm: search the --pep proteomes with hmmsearch. --evalue Largest domain E-value kept. (default: 1e-05) --max-size Annotated genes per orthogroup scored (sampled beyond). (default: 200) --busco BUSCO run NAME=DIR or a phylo busco status table (repeatable). (default: []) --genome Assembly NAME=FASTA for N50 and the like (repeatable). (default: []) --compare A second grouping to compare with (any --groups format). --compare-node Node of HOGs given to --compare. --tree Species tree (Newick) for the figures. --cpus Threads for hmmsearch. (default: 4) --seed Seed for sampling and shuffling. (default: 1) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog run
docs.text:
The one-command MCscan pipeline (mcscan3 ortholog run; legacy compara.catalog ortholog).

Group ortholog · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog run [OPTIONS] SPECIES_A SPECIES_B

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For species a and b (files a.bed, a.cds / a.pep, b.bed, ...):

mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --cpus=8
  1. align a against b (LAST by default; --align-soft blast, diamond or mmseqs) -> a.b.last
  2. filter blastfilter -> a.b.last.filtered
  3. synteny scan with liftover from a.b.last -> a.b.anchors, a.b.lifted.anchors
  4. optionally quota align --quota on the lifted anchors
  5. dot plot a.b.pdf (unless --no-dotplot)

--full instead builds 1:1 blocks (quota 1:1), lifts them over, stacks them with synteny mcscan both ways and recruits reciprocal best hits: a.b.ortholog and b.a.ortholog. Steps whose outputs are newer than their inputs are skipped, as in the original.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_A Species a (a.bed + a.cds/a.pep). SPECIES_B Species b.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --dbtype nucl (.cds) or prot (.pep). (default: nucl) --full Full 1x1 mode, including blocks and RBH. --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within distance. (default: 10) --cscore C-score cutoff. (default: 0.7) --dist Extent of flanking regions to search. (default: 20) -n, --min-size Minimum number of anchors in a cluster. (default: 4) --quota Quota align parameter, e.g. 1:2. --exclude Remove anchors from a previous run. --self-remove Self comparison: drop hits above this identity. (default: 98) --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing. --liftover-dist Liftover distance (default: --dist // 2). --cpus Number of CPUs, 0 = all. (default: 0) --skipempty Dot plot: skip seqids without matches. --nochpf Dot plot: do not change the contig names. --nostdpf Dot plot: do not standardise contig names. --genomenames Dot plot axis names, e.g. "A_B". --grid-color Dot plot grid colour index (0-8; the original's --theme). --notex Dot plot: do not use TeX. --no-dotplot Do not make the dot plot. --ignore-zero-anchor Continue when no anchor is found. --align-soft last, blast, diamond (proteins) or mmseqs. (default: last) --out-format Also write the lifted anchors as mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv.

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog soi
docs.text:
Keep orthologous synteny using the Orthology Index.

Group ortholog · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog soi [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a reimplementation of the Orthology Index method (SOI; Zhang et al. 2025, Nucleic Acids Research) from its description. A syntenic block's Orthology Index (OI) is the fraction of its anchor pairs that an independent orthology inference also calls orthologs. Blocks from speciation (orthologous synteny) have a high OI. Blocks from older duplications (out-paralogous synteny) have a low one. Blocks with OI >= --cutoff (default 0.6) are kept:

mcscan3 ortholog soi grape.peach.anchors --orthologs grape_peach.orthologs.tsv

Orthologs come from one of:

  • --orthologs: a file of ortholog pairs (two columns), or an OrthoFinder Orthologues directory (Orthologues_<A>/<A>__v__<B>.tsv, all pairs within each row);
  • --blast: reciprocal best hits of the BLAST file (a quick stand-in when no orthology inference is available).

Writes <anchors prefix>.soi.anchors (the kept blocks) and <anchors prefix>.oi (one line per block: id, anchors, ortholog anchors, OI, kept), and prints a summary to stderr.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file of two genomes.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --orthologs Ortholog pairs (2 columns) or an OrthoFinder Orthologues directory. --blast Use reciprocal best hits of this BLAST file as orthologs. --cutoff Keep blocks with an Orthology Index at least this. (default: 0.6) --strip-names Match genes without transcript suffixes (.1, .t01). --outfile, -o Kept blocks (default: .soi.anchors). --score The same blocks before lifting (..anchors): the OI is read on them.

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog tandem
docs.text:
Tandem gene clusters (mcscan3 ortholog tandem; legacy compara.catalog tandem).

Group ortholog · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog tandem [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE CDS_FILE BED_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
From a self BLAST (comment-free table), genes within --tandem-nmax genes of each other that align over at least --percent-overlap % of the shorter gene (e-value <= --evalue) are grouped. With --not-self the BLAST is between two gene sets and neighbouring homologs of similar length are grouped; --genefamily groups all homologs. Writes one comma-separated family per line; a summary goes to stderr:

mcscan3 ortholog tandem grape.grape.last.filtered grape.cds grape.bed -o grape.tandem

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE Self BLAST without comment lines (e.g. a.a.last.filtered). CDS_FILE CDS (or protein) FASTA, for gene lengths. BED_FILE BED of the genome.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within distance. (default: 3) --percent-overlap Tandem genes have >= x% aligned sequence. (default: 50) --evalue E-value cutoff. (default: 0.01) --not-self The BLAST is not a self comparison. --strip-gene-name Isoform separator; None to disable. (default: .) --genefamily Compile gene families by similarity. --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 pad cluster
docs.text:
Segment chromosomes and cluster the segments (mcscan3 pad cluster; legacy compara.pad cluster).

Group pad · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pad cluster [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Method of Tang et al. (2010) PNAS: chromosomes are cut at synteny block boundaries (blocks with at least --minsize anchors) into segments (<prefix>.pad.bed); the -log(P) of hit enrichment between every pair of segments is written to <q>.<s>.logmp.txt and clustered with CLUSTER 3.0 (Pearson correlation, average linkage) into .cdt/.gtr/.atr files.

Needs the CLUSTER 3.0 command-line program (--path or MCSCAN3_CLUSTER_PATH); note that Graphviz ships an unrelated program also called cluster.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE Filtered BLAST file. ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED. --sbed Subject BED. --minsize Only segment using blocks >= this size. (default: 10) --path Directory containing the CLUSTER 3.0 cluster program.

docs.title: mcscan3 pan cnv
docs.text:
Local presence/absence and copy-number variation along a reference genome.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan cnv [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. The pan-genes of pan genes are placed along a reference genome and read in sliding windows of --window pan-genes (step --step). Each pan-gene is pav when it is missing from at least one genome and cnv when it is present in every genome with different copy numbers. For each window: the share of pav and cnv pan-genes, and every genome's mean copy number. Hotspots are windows with more variable pan-genes than expected: the variable flags are shuffled along the genome --permutations times, and the empirical P of a window is the share of shuffles whose most variable window anywhere in the genome is at least as variable (the genome-wide maximum corrects for the number of windows):

mcscan3 pan cnv A B C D --ref A -o pan

Writes <prefix>.cnv_windows.tsv (one line per window), <prefix>.cnv_pangenes.tsv (copy numbers per pan-gene) and <prefix>.cnv.png (tracks along the reference chromosomes and a genome-by-window heatmap of copy number relative to the reference).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome: windows are read along it. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the .. anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix (e.g. lifted.anchors). (default: anchors) --window Pan-genes per window. (default: 50) --step Pan-genes between window starts. (default: 25) --permutations Shuffles for the hotspot test (0: none). (default: 1000) --alpha Hotspot P cutoff. (default: 0.05) --labels Display names of the genomes, comma-separated. --chrom-names Display names of the reference chromosomes: genome, chromosome, name per line. --plot Figure of tracks and heatmap. --format Figure format (png, pdf, svg). (default: png)

docs.title: mcscan3 pan genes
docs.text:
Synteny-constrained pan-gene sets across genomes.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan genes [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the idea of GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife), reimplemented from the paper with MCscan3's own synteny. Each pairwise anchors file (<a>.<b>.anchors, e.g. from ortholog run) links syntenic homologs. The connected groups of genes across all genomes are the pan-genes. Each pan-gene is placed on the reference genome by the position of its reference gene. A pan-gene without a reference gene takes the position of the nearest pan-gene (within --window genes, on the same genome) that has one:

mcscan3 pan genes grape peach poplar --ref grape -o pan

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed). Anchors files are looked up in --anchors-dir for every pair, in either order (<a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>). Writes <prefix>.pangenes.tsv: one line per pan-gene in reference order, with its reference position, category and genes per genome (comma-separated, . if absent). Categories are core (in all genomes), shell (in several) and private (in one). Prints counts per category and genome.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome for positions. --prefix, -o Output prefix (.pangenes.tsv). --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the .. anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix (e.g. lifted.anchors). (default: anchors) --window Genes searched for a placed neighbour. (default: 20)

docs.title: mcscan3 pan graph
docs.text:
Graph pan-genome of assemblies.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan graph [OPTIONS] ASSEMBLIES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The graph is built and genotyped by established tools, and MCscan3 turns their output into tables, variants, association markers and figures:

  1. graph: minigraph (Li H, Feng X & Chu C 2020, Genome Biol 21:265) builds a structural-variant graph with the reference as backbone (minigraph -cxggs). Contigs are renamed after PanSN (sample#1#contig) first, so that contigs of the same name in several assemblies stay apart. A graph made elsewhere can be given instead (--gfa): an rGFA of minigraph is genotyped as below; a GFA with paths (PGGB, Minigraph-Cactus) is analysed from its paths;
  2. genotypes: every assembly is aligned back to the graph and its allele in every bubble is read (minigraph -cxasm --call); the reference allele follows the backbone. Bubbles are typed by their alleles (insertion, deletion, inversion, complex);
  3. paths: each assembly is written as a walk through the graph (the backbone with its own alleles in the bubbles, broken where it has no call or changes contig), so the graph can be read by odgi, panacus, vg or Bandage (<prefix>.paths.gfa);
  4. pan-genome: every segment is core (in all genomes), softcore (--softcore), shell or private; growth curves are the exact expected pan-genome and core sizes for every number of genomes (hypergeometric expectation over all genome orders, as computed by panacus, github.com/marschall-lab/panacus). With panacus installed its own histgrowth table is written too; with odgi installed, its 1D visualisation of the paths (Guarracino A et al. 2022, Bioinformatics 38:3319);
  5. variants and markers: bubbles as a multi-sample VCF (AT gives the allele traversals); --plink writes one presence marker per non-reference allele for association studies;
  6. diversity: variable sequence per reference window; windows far above or below the genome-wide level are flagged.

Writes <prefix>.gfa (when built), <prefix>.paths.gfa, <prefix>.graph.bubbles.tsv, .graph.nodes.tsv, .graph.growth.tsv, .graph.windows.tsv, .graph.vcf, .graph.json, the figure and, with --plink, .graph.bed/.bim/.fam.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ASSEMBLIES Assemblies to add and genotype (FASTA, gzip ok).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ref Reference assembly: the backbone of a new graph. --gfa Existing graph: an rGFA (minigraph) or a GFA with paths (PGGB, Cactus). --names Comma-separated genome names (default: file names). --ref-name Name of the reference genome (default: file name). --min-size Smallest variant added to a new graph (bp). (default: 50) --minigraph-args Extra minigraph options for building, quoted. --softcore Share of genomes for softcore segments. (default: 0.9) --window Reference window for diversity (bp). (default: 100000) --region Region chrom:start-end: subgraph, sequences, tube map (repeatable). (default: []) --gff Reference GFF3: presence of every gene in every genome. --min-cover Share of a gene's bases for presence. (default: 0.8) --plink PLINK markers of the bubble alleles. --pan-reference Linear pan-reference FASTA (reference + other segments). --max-allele Longer alleles are symbolic in the VCF (bp). (default: 10000) --path Folder of minigraph. --cpus Threads. (default: 4) --keep Keep the renamed assemblies. --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 pan haplotype
docs.text:
Haplotypes of regions across genomes, and their association with traits.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan haplotype [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For each region (pan region), every genome is described by the local copy number of the region's pan-genes (0, 1, 2, 3 or more), optionally the presence of the structural variants of sv merge inside the region (the region's genome must be the SV reference), and the orientation of the region (gene order against the region's genome). Genomes are clustered by the share of features that differ (average linkage); clusters closer than --max-dist form one haplotype, and genomes carrying the region inverted form a haplotype of their own:

mcscan3 pan haplotype g1 g2 g3 g4 g5 --regions qtl.txt -o qtl --phenotypes traits.tsv

With a phenotype table (genome column, then one column per trait; numbers or categories), each trait is tested against the haplotypes (Kruskal-Wallis for numbers, chi-square for categories) and against the presence or absence of each variable pan-gene (Mann-Whitney U, Benjamini-Hochberg across the pan-genes of a region). Writes <prefix>.haplotypes.tsv, <prefix>.haplotype_assoc.tsv, <prefix>.pav_assoc.tsv and a figure per region (<prefix>.<region>.haplotypes.png: dendrogram, copy-number matrix, haplotypes and traits).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --regions Regions file: genome chrom start end [name [colour]] per line (QTL, loci). --region One region: genome:chrom:start-end. --phenotypes Trait table: genome column, then one column per trait (tab separated). --pansv Pan-SVs of sv merge (.pansv.tsv) on the region's genome as reference. --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the .. anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix (e.g. lifted.anchors). (default: anchors) --min-block Blocks with fewer anchors do not trace the region. (default: 5) --flank Genes added either side of every syntenic interval. (default: 0) --max-dist Genomes closer than this share of differing features share a haplotype. (default: 0.2) --labels Display names of the genomes, comma-separated. --plot Figure per region. --format Figure format (png, pdf, svg). (default: png)

docs.title: mcscan3 pan region
docs.text:
Presence/absence and copy number of the pan-genes of a region.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan region [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. A region (a QTL interval, a locus) on one genome is traced through the anchors into every other genome (as in plot riparian --highlight). The pan-genes (pan genes) with a gene inside the region on any genome are its pan-genes; they are ordered along the genome of the region (pan-genes missing there are placed next to their neighbours). For every genome, each pan-gene has a number of copies inside the syntenic region (its local copy number) and possibly copies elsewhere in the genome (moved or dispersed):

mcscan3 pan region grape peach poplar ath --regions qtl.txt -o qtl
mcscan3 pan region grape peach poplar ath --region grape:chr1:5000000-7000000 -o locus

The regions file has genome chrom start end [name [colour]] per line. Each pan-gene and genome gets a state: absent (no copy in the genome), elsewhere (copies only outside the syntenic region), single, tandem (several local copies within --tandem-gap genes) or multi (several local copies further apart). A pan-gene is variable when its local copy number differs between genomes. Writes <prefix>.region.tsv (pan-genes by genomes), <prefix>.region_summary.tsv (per region and genome) and a heatmap per region (<prefix>.<region>.png).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --regions Regions file: genome chrom start end [name [colour]] per line (QTL, loci). --region One region: genome:chrom:start-end. --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the .. anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix (e.g. lifted.anchors). (default: anchors) --min-block Blocks with fewer anchors do not trace the region. (default: 5) --flank Genes added either side of every syntenic interval. (default: 0) --tandem-gap Local copies this close (in genes) are tandem. (default: 3) --labels Display names of the genomes, comma-separated. --plot Heatmap per region. --format Figure format (png, pdf, svg). (default: png)

docs.title: mcscan3 pan run
docs.text:
Pan-genome of many genomes, gene-based and sequence-based.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan run [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Two views of the same question (what every genome shares, what only some carry, and whether sampling more genomes keeps adding new content):

  • gene-based: pan-genes are the syntenic homologs linked across genomes (pan genes). Missing pairwise synteny is computed first (ortholog run on proteins or CDS). Genes found in no anchor are pan-genes of one genome;
  • sequence-based: each assembly is sketched by FracMinHash (k-mers kept with a hash below 2**64 / scaled, Irber et al. 2022), so no annotation or reference is needed. Each kept k-mer stands for scaled bp of distinct sequence.

Both give a presence/absence matrix, from which MCscan3 reports:

  • classes: core (in every genome), softcore (at least --softcore of them), shell (two or more) and cloud (one genome), in total and per genome;
  • accumulation curves: pan-genome and core genome size as genomes are added, over --permutations random orders (all orders when there are fewer);
  • Heaps' law: the new content added by the k-th genome fitted as kappa * k**-alpha; alpha < 1 means an open pan-genome that keeps growing, alpha > 1 a closed one (Tettelin et al. 2008, Curr Opin Microbiol 11:472);
  • similarity: shared content of every pair of genomes (Jaccard), and for sequences the containment both ways and the Mash identity estimate (Ondov et al. 2016, Genome Biol 17:132):
mcscan3 pan run dmel dsim dyak dpse --bed-dir insects --fasta dmel=dmel.fa ... -o flies

Writes <prefix>.<mode>.{pav,classes,frequency,curve,similarity}.tsv for gene and seq, <prefix>.gene.pangenes.tsv (the genes of each pan-gene), <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.json, the sketches (<prefix>.sketches/, reused) and four figures: <prefix>.curves, <prefix>.composition, <prefix>.similarity and <prefix>.pav.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names for the gene-based pan-genome (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --mode gene, sequence or both. (default: both) --fasta Assembly for the sequence-based pan-genome, NAME=FILE (repeatable; .gz read). (default: []) --ref Reference genome for pan-gene order (default: first). --bed-dir Directory of .bed and .pep (or .cds). (default: .) --anchors-dir Anchors files (default: --bed-dir). --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: lifted.anchors) --align Compute missing pairwise synteny. --dbtype prot (.pep) or nucl (.cds) for missing synteny. (default: prot) --align-soft last, diamond, mmseqs or blast. (default: last) --k k-mer size of the sketches (at most 31). (default: 21) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (bp per sketch hash). (default: 1000) --min-length Leave out sequences shorter than this (bp). (default: 0) --softcore Share of genomes for the softcore class. (default: 0.9) --permutations Random genome orders for the curves. (default: 100) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --cpus Processes for sketching and alignment. (default: 1) --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo build
docs.text:
NJ and ML trees from CDS (mcscan3 phylo build; legacy apps.phylo build).

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo build [OPTIONS] FILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Steps, all with external programs:

  1. translate the CDS (unless a protein file is given) and align the proteins with MUSCLE (default) or ClustalW (--msa);
  2. back-translate to a codon alignment with PAL2NAL;
  3. remove poorly aligned blocks with Gblocks (--nogblocks to skip; then --synonymous or --fourfold keep only those sites);
  4. a bootstrapped neighbour-joining tree with EMBOSS PHYLIP (fseqboot, fdnadist, fneighbor, fconsense, ffitch; --noneighbor to skip);
  5. a maximum-likelihood tree with RAxML or PhyML (--ml=raxml|phyml).

Files go to <outdir>/alignment and <outdir>/tree (<cds prefix>.NJ.unrooted.dnd, <cds prefix>.ML.unrooted.dnd):

mcscan3 phylo build family0.cds --ml=phyml

--outgroup=<file> roots the trees on the first outgroup name (prefix) found; --SH=<tree> runs RAxML's SH test against a reference tree; --treefix (with --stree, --smap) runs TreeFix on the RAxML tree. Rooting and the NJ tree need the phylo extra (ete4).

Differences from the original (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.11): it crashed on Python 3 when reading Gblocks output, and did not find the -gb.fa file that current Gblocks builds write.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FILES [prot.fasta] cds.fasta

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --longest Use the longest ORF (no protein file, e.g. ESTs). --nogblocks Do not edit the alignment with Gblocks. --synonymous Keep synonymous sites only (with --nogblocks). --fourfold Keep fourfold degenerate sites (with --nogblocks). --msa Protein aligner: clustalw or muscle. (default: muscle) --noneighbor Do not build the NJ tree. --ml ML tree program: raxml or phyml. --outgroup File with outgroup names, in order of preference. --SH, --sh Reference Newick tree for the SH test. --shout SH output file name. (default: SH_out.txt) --treefix Rearrange the ML tree with TreeFix. --stree Species Newick tree (TreeFix). --smap gene_name_patternspecies_name file (TreeFix). --outdir Output directory. (default: .)

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo busco
docs.text:
Phylogenomics from single-copy BUSCO genes.

Group phylo · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo busco [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the BUSCO_phylogenomics workflow (McGowan J & Fitzpatrick DA; reimplemented from its description) and BUSCO itself (Manni M et al. 2021, Mol Biol Evol 38:4647), made faster:

  1. markers: annotated proteomes (--pep NAME=FILE) are searched directly with the lineage's profile HMMs in one hmmsearch per genome (seconds instead of a BUSCO run); a protein is a match above the lineage's score cutoff (and counts only for the BUSCO it matches best), complete when its HMM coverage reaches the expected length minus two standard deviations, else fragmented; one complete match is single, more scoring at least 85% of the best are duplicated (weaker ones are paralogs, not copies). Finished BUSCO runs (--busco NAME=DIR) are read instead when given;
  2. loci: single-copy BUSCOs present in at least --occupancy of the genomes;
  3. alignment of each locus in parallel (FAMSA, MAFFT or MUSCLE; cached), trimming of gappy columns (--max-gap) natively, and loci shorter than --min-length dropped;
  4. supermatrix with a partition file (RAxML-NG and NEXUS formats), and trees: a concatenated maximum-likelihood tree (IQ-TREE's fast search with SH-aLRT support by default; --partitioned for a model per locus, --bootstrap for ultrafast bootstrap; or FastTree), gene trees (FastTree or IQ-TREE, in parallel) and their coalescent summary (ASTRAL);
  5. gene concordance factors of every branch, natively (Minh et al. 2020, Mol Biol Evol 37:2727), and the Robinson-Foulds distance between the concatenated and coalescent trees:
mcscan3 phylo busco --pep scer=scer.pep --pep dmel=dmel.pep ... --manifest manifest.tsv \
    --outgroup ath -o tree/euk

--lineage is a BUSCO dataset name (diptera_odb10; downloaded once into --lineage-dir) or folder (hmms/, scores_cutoff and, for OrthoDB 10, lengths_cutoff). With auto (the default) the species of the genomes are looked up in NCBI Taxonomy and the most specific lineage holding them all is chosen (--odb sets the dataset version). Species come from --species NAME=SPECIES (a name or taxid), from fetch manifests (--manifest), or from genome names that are species names (Saccharomyces_cerevisiae). Writes <prefix>.status.tsv (status of every BUSCO in every genome), <prefix>.summary.tsv (BUSCO scores), <prefix>.loci.tsv, <prefix>.supermatrix.faa, <prefix>.partitions.{txt,nex}, <prefix>.concat.nwk, <prefix>.genetrees.nwk, <prefix>.astral.nwk, <prefix>.species.nwk (rooted, with gCF), <prefix>.concordance.tsv and the figures <prefix>.tree, <prefix>.matrix and <prefix>.compare. Intermediate files go to <prefix>.work/.

With --synteny the same BUSCOs serve as syntenic markers: their positions (from genome-mode BUSCO runs, or from --bed NAME=genes.bed for proteomes) give each genome's karyotype, and the species tree just built is used to reconstruct the ancestral karyotypes and the fissions, fusions and translocations of every branch (as mcscan3 macro ancestors), written as <prefix>.synteny.*.

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo date
docs.text:
Divergence times on a species tree, with the checks that show how far to trust each age.

Group phylo · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo date [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. phylo date turns a species tree into a time tree. The tree and the loci come from one of three places:

  • --from-busco PREFIX: a phylo busco run. Its species tree (ASTRAL, else the concatenated tree), its trimmed single-copy alignments and its gene trees are reused.
  • --from-orthofinder DIR: an OrthoFinder results folder. The rooted species tree is dated, and the single-copy orthogroups are aligned and trimmed here.
  • --alignments: any set of aligned loci, with --tree. To date the topology of a synteny network tree (network tree), give --from-network PREFIX. Its branch lengths measure synteny, not substitutions, so only the topology is used, and the loci supply the sequence data.

The tree must be rooted (or rooted here with --outgroup) and fully resolved.

docs.title: Calibrations
docs.text:
Calibrations come from two places, and the two are combined.

MCscan3's calibration library (--library, on by default) stores node ages for the main clades with fossil records or well-supported secondary ages: vertebrates, eudicots, Vitaceae, filamentous ascomycetes, dinoflagellates, Haemosporida and the apicomplexan-dinoflagellate split. Each comes with its source and a confidence level. Each node is defined by two NCBI Taxonomy taxa (crown mammals are the most recent common ancestor of Monotremata and Theria). A library age is applied only when the tree has tips on both sides, so it always lands on the node it was meant for.

  • Tip lineages. The NCBI lineage of every tip is looked up from --species TIP=SPECIES, a fetch manifest (--manifest), or the tip name itself (plasmodium_falciparum_3d7 is looked up as Plasmodium falciparum 3d7, then Plasmodium falciparum, then Plasmodium). The lineages are saved as OUT.taxonomy.tsv. --taxonomy FILE gives them directly, with no lookup.
  • Confidence. --library-confidence (low, medium or high; default medium) sets the least confidence used. Rows marked low are secondary ages or fossils whose placement is debated, and they need --library-confidence low.
  • Checking the library. The library is at src/mcscan3/features/phylo/calibrations.tsv. Check every row you rely on against its source before publication.

Your own table (--calibrations) is tab-separated, with ages in million years before present:

scheme   name           taxa                                   min    max    source
*        root           root                                   650    1100   apicomplexan-dinoflagellate split, Strassert et al. 2021
fossil   Dinophyceae    taxon:Gonyaulacales|Suessiales         240           Middle Triassic dinoflagellate cysts
fossil   Haemosporida   taxon:Haemosporida                     100           Paleohaemoproteus in Burmese amber
host     Mammal-Plasmodium  ~^plasmodium_(vivax|knowlesi|cynomolgi|berghei)  64  120  host co-divergence
  • taxa names the node in one of four ways:
    • taxon:A|B is the most recent common ancestor of the tips in NCBI taxa A and B.
    • taxon:A is the crown of taxon A. It is used only if A is monophyletic in the tree; otherwise it is skipped and the reason is logged, because an age placed on a polyphyletic group would date the wrong node.
    • Two or more tip names give their most recent common ancestor. root is the root.
    • A regular expression after ~ selects tips by name.
  • Minimum and maximum. A minimum without a maximum is a fossil-style lower bound, a truncated Cauchy with a long tail toward older ages. A maximum alone is an upper bound. Both together are soft bounds, with 2.5% of the probability outside each end.
  • Schemes. Rows with the same scheme are analysed together, and rows of scheme * belong to every scheme. Put independent lines of evidence in separate schemes (fossils, secondary ages from a larger dated tree, host co-divergence, mutation rates). Agreement between schemes is the strongest evidence that an age is right. The library's schemes are fossil and secondary.
  • Your rows win. A row of yours replaces a library row of the same name, and on a node that both calibrate, your row is used.
  • The root needs a maximum in every scheme. It can come from a library node that spans the whole tree, a root row, or --root-max.

OUT.calibrations.tsv lists every calibration considered: where it came from, the node and its number of tips, its bounds, and whether it was used, replaced or skipped, with the reason.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Clock-like loci.
    • Each locus is scored by how well its gene tree agrees with the species tree, then by the spread of its root-to-tip distances.
    • The best --loci loci are kept.
    • They are grouped by rate into --rate-partitions partitions.
  2. MCMCTree, with the approximate likelihood (gradient and Hessian of the branch lengths under LG+G4 by codeml).
    • The other nodes get a birth-death prior.
    • The rate prior is centred on the substitution rate that the tree and the root age imply.
    • Each clock model in --clock is run: independent (lognormal rates) and autocorrelated (geometric Brownian rates).
    • Each analysis runs as --chains independent chains with different seeds.
    • The same analysis is also run without the data, which gives the effective prior of every node: the joint effect of all calibrations and the tree prior, which can differ markedly from the bounds as written.
  3. LSD2 (least-squares dating, through IQ-TREE) on the same loci and topology, as a second, independent method. --method lsd2 uses it alone, which takes seconds.
  4. Cross-validation. Each calibration in turn is left out, and its node is estimated from the others. A calibration that the others cannot predict conflicts with them and is reported.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
Every node gets a verdict:

Verdict Meaning robust the chains agree and the age holds across schemes and clock models not converged effective sample size below 200, R-hat above 1.05, or chain means more than 5% apart scheme-sensitive calibration schemes disagree by more than 1.5-fold clock-sensitive the clock models disagree by more than 1.25-fold prior-driven the 95% posterior interval is more than 90% as wide as the prior's, so the sequences add little and the age is set by the calibrations

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# from a BUSCO phylogeny, with the library alone (species from the fetch manifest)
mcscan3 phylo busco -o vert --pep ... --outgroup chicken
mcscan3 phylo date -o vert.date --from-busco vert --manifest genomes/manifest.tsv --cpus 16

# the library plus your own calibrations and schemes, both clocks
mcscan3 phylo date -o apic.date -c calibrations.tsv --library-confidence low --from-busco apic --cpus 16

# OrthoFinder species tree and single-copy orthogroups
mcscan3 phylo date -o of.date -c cal.tsv --from-orthofinder OrthoFinder/Results_Nov24 --cpus 16

# the topology of a synteny network tree, with BUSCO loci for the rates
mcscan3 phylo date -o net.date -c cal.tsv --from-network net --alignments apic.work --outgroup perkinsus_marinus

# a quick look with LSD2 only
mcscan3 phylo date -o quick -c cal.tsv --from-busco apic --method lsd2

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: File Content OUT.dates.tsv every node under every scheme and clock: mean age, 95% HPD, prior interval, ESS, R-hat, LSD2 age, verdict OUT.<scheme>.<clock>.nwk dated tree (branch lengths in Myr; node labels mean[low-high]) OUT.crossval.tsv each calibration left out: its bounds, the age predicted by the others, and whether they agree OUT.calibrations.tsv every calibration considered (library and yours): node, tips, bounds, used, replaced or skipped, and why OUT.taxonomy.tsv the NCBI lineage of every tip (reusable with --taxonomy) OUT.loci.tsv the loci used: rank, taxa, sites, concordance, root-to-tip CV, rate, partition OUT.chronogram.pdf the time tree with HPD bars coloured by verdict, calibrated nodes and geological eras OUT.sensitivity.pdf ages of the calibrated and deepest nodes under every scheme, clock and LSD2 OUT.json settings and verdict counts OUT.work/ MCMCTree, codeml and LSD2 runs (in.BV, mcmc.txt of every chain); finished runs are reused

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Run length. The default (20,000 burn-in, 20,000 samples every 20 iterations) is enough for trees of a few hundred tips with the approximate likelihood. If a node is not converged, raise --nsample and --sampfreq.
  • Mitochondrial loci. Mitochondrial genes saturate at deep divergences and underestimate old ages, so date with nuclear loci where they exist.
  • Requirements. PAML (mcmctree, codeml) for MCMCTree and IQ-TREE 2 or 3 for LSD2. The LG matrix is bundled.

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo draw [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
--input is one Newick file or a directory holding only tree files. Each tree is drawn as it is rooted (use plot tree for rerooting and more annotations); node support above --scutoff is shown in red. --combine=RxC puts R x C trees on one page (trees<N>.<format>); otherwise each tree goes to <tree prefix>.<format> in --outdir:

mcscan3 phylo draw --input=tree/family0.ML.unrooted.dnd --format=png

--sh gives a file of tree_file<TAB>SH p-value lines (as written by phylo build --SH). --trunc-name shortens names (headN, oheadN, tailN, otailN). Needs the phylo extra.

The original crashed on Python 3 (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.12). Its --barcode and --leafcolorfile options had no effect and are accepted but ignored.

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo families
docs.text:
Gene family expansion and contraction on a dated species tree.

Group phylo · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo families [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. The number of genes of each family in each species is modelled as a birth-death process along the branches of an ultrametric tree. In this process each gene duplicates or is lost at rate λ per million years. This is the model of CAFE, reimplemented in MCscan3 with no external program.

  • Counts. They come from OrthoFinder's Orthogroups.tsv (gene lists), Orthogroups.GeneCount.tsv, MCscan3's own orthogroups (pipeline run writes them in the same format), or a CAFE table (Desc, Family ID, one column per species).
  • The tree. It must be dated and ultrametric, such as a tree from phylo date. Its tips must be the species of the count table, or the species given with --species, which prunes the tree to that clade. --make-ultrametric gives an undated tree a relative time scale by mean path lengths. Rates are then per unit of relative time.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
• Rates. One λ is shared by all families. With k > 1 gamma categories, λ varies among families.
  • The root. The number of genes at the root follows a uniform or a Poisson prior.
  • Exact transitions. Transition probabilities are CAFE's closed formula, computed as convolutions of positive terms so that even the smallest probabilities are accurate to full precision. A spectral decomposition of the generator, the usual shortcut, loses every digit below about 1e-16 and makes the likelihood of families with large changes noisy.
  • Conditioning. The likelihood is conditioned on a family being seen in at least --min-species species, which is how orthogroups are defined.
  • Model choice. Every k from 1 to --max-k is fitted under each root prior in --root. The model with the lowest AIC is used, as in the EXCON pipeline.
  • Large families. Families whose counts differ by more than --max-differential between species would dominate the fit. λ is estimated without them, and they are then tested with it, as in the CAFE5 tutorial.

docs.title: Which families changed, and where
docs.text:
• Family p-values. For each family, --simulations families are simulated from its most likely root size. The p-value is the share of simulations at most as likely as the observed counts. Families with p < --pvalue changed faster than λ allows.
  • Ancestral counts are reconstructed by joint maximum likelihood.
  • Branch tests. On every branch of a significant family, the probability of a change at least as large as the reconstructed one is computed. Changes with probability below --pvalue are the significant expansions and contractions of that branch.

docs.title: Checks that are new in MCscan3
docs.text:
• Annotation gaps. For each species, OUT.species_check.tsv gives the share of conserved families (present in at least 80% of the other species) in which it has no gene. A badly annotated genome stands out here before its missing genes are mistaken for contractions.
  • How families grew. With --dup, which takes the <prefix>.genes tables of dup classify for any species, the genes of significantly expanded families are counted by duplication mode (WGD, tandem, proximal, transposed, dispersed) and compared with all genes of the species. This shows whether expansions came from tandem arrays, whole-genome duplication or dispersed copies.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# OrthoFinder orthogroups on a tree dated with phylo date
mcscan3 phylo date -o dated --from-orthofinder Results_run1 --cpus 16
mcscan3 phylo families -o fam -c Results_run1/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv -t dated.fossil.independent.nwk

# one clade only, with duplication modes
mcscan3 phylo families -o vitis -c Orthogroups.tsv -t dated.nwk --species vv,vr,va,vc --dup dup/vv.genes --dup dup/vr.genes

# an undated tree (relative time)
mcscan3 phylo families -o fam -c Orthogroups.tsv -t SpeciesTree_rooted.txt --make-ultrametric

pipeline run runs this step (families) on its orthogroups and species tree, using the duplication modes from its dup step.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
File Content OUT.models.tsv every model fitted: k, root prior, λ, gamma shape, root mean, lnL, AIC, the one chosen OUT.families.tsv each family: p-value, significant, root size, counts, and the branches where it changed significantly (branch(+n)) OUT.branches.tsv each branch: families expanded and contracted, genes gained and lost, significant expansions and contractions OUT.ancestral.tsv the reconstructed number of genes of every family at every node OUT.species_check.tsv missing conserved families per species, and a flag for possible annotation gaps OUT.dup_modes.tsv with --dup: genes of significantly expanded families by duplication mode, and the enrichment over all genes OUT.changed_genes.tsv genes of the significant changes on every branch, as gene sets (set<TAB>gene; go enrich --sets) OUT.excluded.tsv families left out, and why OUT.tree.nwk, OUT.branch_pvalues.tsv the tree with nodes named as in the tables, and the branch p-values of significant families OUT.summary.pdf the dated tree with the significant and all expansions and contractions of each branch OUT.top_families.pdf the most significant families, each on its own tree with the counts at every node OUT.highlights.pdf, .tsv families picked out with the reason: largest burst and loss, clade expansions, complete losses, the most volatile OUT.go.tsv, OUT.go.pdf with --obo and --annotations: GO terms enriched among the families expanded and contracted on every branch

More figures, and one family with its gene tree and domains: mcscan3 plot families and plot family.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --counts, -c Orthogroups.tsv, Orthogroups.GeneCount.tsv or a CAFE count table. --tree, -t Dated (ultrametric) species tree, e.g. from phylo date. --make-ultrametric Undated tree: relative time by mean path lengths. --species Analyse only these species (tree pruned to them). (default: []) --max-k Fit 1..k gamma rate categories; the best by AIC is used. (default: 3) --root Root-size priors to compare. (default: ['uniform', 'poisson']) --min-species Families in fewer species are left out. (default: 2) --max-differential Families whose counts differ more are tested, not fitted. (default: 50) --error Counting error fitted with the rates: none, global (one rate) or species (one each). (default: none) --obo Gene Ontology (go-basic.obo): GO enrichment per branch. --annotations GO annotations of the genes (eggNOG-mapper, GAF, GPAD, gene2go, InterProScan). (default: []) --outlier-p Refit the rate without families this far outside the model (0: no refit). (default: 0.001) --pvalue Significance of families and branches. (default: 0.05) --simulations Simulations per root size for family p-values. (default: 1000) --dup dup classify gene tables (.genes), any species. (default: []) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --format Figure format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Gene family expansion and contraction on the eudicot tree (approximate TimeTree ages), with GO terms enriched among the families that changed on each branch (A. thaliana annotations).

mkdir -p families && echo '(amborella:180,(grape:117,(ath:108,(poplar:103,(peach:100,soybean:100):3):5):9):63);' \

 --obo $IN/go-basic.obo --annotations go/tair.gaf.gz -o families/fam && head -4 families/fam.branches.tsv

run time 10 min 22 s · data real · showcase step phylo_families

docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). Birth-death model of gene counts after CAFE (Hahn MW, et al. (2005) Genome Res 15:1153-1160; Mendes FK, et al. (2020) Bioinformatics 36:5516-5518), reimplemented: transition probabilities of the closed formula as convolutions of positive terms (exact at any rate), discrete-gamma rate categories, uniform or Poisson root, conditioning on observation, maximum likelihood with exact gradients (quasi-Newton), refit without outlier families, optional counting error per genome, model choice by AIC as in the EXCON pipeline (github.com/Eco-Flow/excon), family p-values by simulation under the fitted model, joint ancestral counts (Pupko T, et al. (2000) Mol Biol Evol 17:890-896); expansions split by duplication mode from dup classify.

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo prepare
docs.text:
Per-family CDS files from MCscan output (mcscan3 phylo prepare; legacy apps.phylo prepare).

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo prepare [OPTIONS] MCSCANFILE CDSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each row of an MCscan table (synteny mcscan output: one column per genome, . for none, comma-separated tandem genes) with more than three genes becomes <outdir>/<first gene>.cds, ready for phylo build:

mcscan3 phylo prepare families.mcscan all.cds --outdir=sequences

--addtandem=<tandem file> first replaces anchors by their tandem clusters (the file must cover all genomes) and merges rows that overlap within 10 rows. --writecolors writes leafcolors.txt (gene, R,G,B of its column) for phylo draw.

Differences from the original (docs/DEVIATIONS.md): it crashed on Python 3 (A.10), and wrote each family in hash-seed-dependent order; MCscan3 writes genes in column order.

docs.text: Argument Description MCSCANFILE MCscan table (synteny mcscan output). CDSFILE CDS FASTA of all genomes.

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 pipeline inputs
docs.text:
Find and prepare the genomes of a project directory (mcscan3 pipeline inputs; first step of pipeline run).

Group pipeline · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pipeline inputs [OPTIONS] DIRECTORY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each species is the file-name prefix before the first dot (grape.gff3.gz, grape.dna.fa.gz, grape.cds, ...). FASTA files are classified by name (cds, pep/protein/prot/faa, dna/genome/genomic/fna) and otherwise by content: protein, short nucleotide records (CDS), or long nucleotide records (genome). A species can be given as any of:

  • gff + genome: the longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced from the genome and translated (prep genome);
  • gff + cds [+ pep]: the longest transcript per gene from the GFF (the attribute that matches the FASTA names is found automatically), with the CDS and protein subset to it;
  • bed + cds [+ pep], or bed + pep: already processed. Names are checked and the protein is translated from the CDS when missing. The .bed may also be an MCScanX gene table (chr, gene, start, end); it is converted to BED.

--samples (TSV: species, gff, genome, bed, cds, pep; empty cells allowed) overrides the detection. Prepared files are <outdir>/<species>.bed, .cds (if any) and .pep, with clean IDs (transcript: and similar prefixes removed) and one record per BED gene.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description DIRECTORY Directory with genome files (gff, genome, bed, cds, pep).

docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Also prepare the files into this directory. --samples Sample sheet to use instead of detection.

docs.title: mcscan3 pipeline run
docs.text:
Everything from a directory of genomes, in one command.

Group pipeline · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pipeline run [OPTIONS] DIRECTORY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Point it at a directory of raw or processed genome files (see pipeline inputs) and it runs, resuming where it stopped:

  1. inputs: one clean <species>.bed/.cds/.pep per species;
  2. orthology: OrthoFinder (orthogroups, orthologues, rooted species tree) when installed, else MCscan3's own orthogroups (DIAMOND + MCL, reciprocal best hits);
  3. synteny: ortholog run for every pair of species (and each species against itself), with dot plots. --search chooses the homology search: LAST per pair (default), BLASTP, one search of all proteomes with MMseqs2 or DIAMOND, or orthofinder, which reuses OrthoFinder's own all-against-all DIAMOND search (align orthofinder) so nothing is searched twice;
  4. orthologous synteny: every pairwise block is scored by its Orthology Index against the orthologues (ortholog soi), so blocks from older duplications are set aside;
  5. pan-genes: the new part. Pan-genes are linked only by anchors that are orthologous synteny and fall in the same orthogroup, so they hold syntenic orthologues and not out-paralogues. Each pan-gene is then completed with the other members of its orthogroups (up to 40 genes), marked separately (like GENESPACE's non-syntenic orthologues), and placed on the reference. A riparian plot follows;
  6. network: a synteny network of all pairwise (and self) anchors, its clusters, profiles and a synteny-based species tree, to set against the orthology species tree;
  7. ancestral genomes on the species tree (CARs at every node), with each genome painted by the root's CARs;
  8. duplications: duplicate-gene classes per species (an outgroup gives transposed copies);
  9. gene families (phylo families): expansions and contractions of the orthogroups on the species tree under a birth-death model, with the duplication modes (step 8) behind the significant expansions and a check for genomes with annotation gaps. An undated species tree is given a relative time scale (date it with phylo date for rates per million years);
  10. ancestral microsynteny (micro ancestral): the groups of families that were neighbours at every node of the species tree, and whether each species kept them compact, dispersed on their chromosome, split or lost;
  11. WGD (--ks, slower): anchor-pair Ks (yn00), block medians and mixture models per species;
  12. Gene Ontology (--go-obo and --go-annotations): enrichment of every gene set the run produced, per species: duplication classes, pan-gene categories, orthogroup classes (core, single-copy, accessory, species-specific, expanded, contracted), synteny-network clusters, and genes syntenic or not with the reference (go enrich on go sets);
  13. report: report.html, everything on one page.

Example:

mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --ref grape --cpus 8 --ks
mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --orthofinder yes --search orthofinder --cpus 16

Output directory: samples.tsv (what was found), data/ (prepared files), orthology/ (OrthoFinder results or MCscan3's own), synteny/ (ortholog run per pair; with --synteny-format also synteny/formats/: the blocks as MCScanX, WGDI, i-ADHoRe, BEDPE, ... files), soi/ (Orthology Index per block and *.soi.anchors), pan/ (pangenes.tsv, riparian.png), network/ (net.*), ancestral/ (CARs per node, anc.summary.tsv, paintings), dup/, families/ (families.*: models, families, branches, ancestral counts, tree figure), microsynteny/ (ancestral.*: blocks per node and their fate in each species), wgd/ (with --ks) and report.html. Steps that fail are listed in the report's notes and the others still run. OrthoFinder with only three species cannot root its species tree reliably: give --tree when the rooting matters (ancestral genomes).

The genomes can also be downloaded first: --fetch takes accessions or species from NCBI, Ensembl, the Genome Warehouse, CNGB or URLs (as fetch genome; repeatable) and --taxon the best annotated genome of each species of a taxon (as fetch taxon; --taxon-max, --taxon-per-genus, --taxon-level). They go to <outdir>/genomes together with the files of the directory, if one is given, so your own genomes can be compared with public ones. The NCBI taxonomy tree of the species is compared with the gene-based species trees (a taxonomy group missing from a tree counts as a conflict; unresolved taxonomy does not), and is used for ancestral genomes when it is fully resolved and OrthoFinder gave no tree:

mcscan3 pipeline run -o grasses --taxon Poaceae --taxon-max 8 --cpus 16 --ks
mcscan3 pipeline run my_genomes -o run --fetch GCF_000001735.4 --fetch ensembl:vitis_vinifera

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description DIRECTORY Directory with genome files (see pipeline inputs); optional with --fetch or --taxon.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Output directory (re-running resumes). --samples Sample sheet to use instead of detection. --ref Reference genome for pan-gene positions (default: first). --cpus CPUs for aligners and Ks. (default: 1) --orthofinder auto, yes or no. (default: auto) --tree Rooted species tree (Newick) (default: OrthoFinder's). --soi-cutoff Orthology Index of orthologous blocks. (default: 0.6) --ks Also anchor/block Ks and WGD mixtures per species (slower). --search Homology search: last (alias pairwise; LAST per pair, CDS), blast (BLASTP per pair), one search of all proteomes with mmseqs or diamond, or orthofinder (reuse OrthoFinder's DIAMOND hits). (default: pairwise) --gpu With --search mmseqs: MMseqs2-GPU (NVIDIA GPU). --jobs Genome pairs processed at once (synteny step); at most --cpus. (default: 1) --steps Comma-separated steps to (re)run (default: all). Steps: orthology, synteny, formats, soi, pan, network, ancestral, dup, families, microsynteny, wgd, wgd-consensus, go, report. --go-obo Gene Ontology (OBO): enables the GO enrichment step. --go-annotations GO annotations: FILE for every species, or SPECIES=FILE (repeatable). (default: []) --go-strip Regular expression removed from annotated gene ids. --synteny-format Also write every pair's synteny blocks as: anchors, mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv (comma-separated) in synteny/formats/. --fetch Genome to download first: accession, ncbi:/ensembl:SPECIES, GWH, CNGB, URL (repeatable). (default: []) --taxon Download the best annotated genome of each species of a taxon. --taxon-max --taxon: at most this many genomes (0: all). (default: 10) --taxon-per-genus --taxon: genomes per genus (0: any). (default: 1) --taxon-level --taxon: least assembly level. (default: chromosome) --taxon-source --taxon: databases (ncbi, ensembl). (default: ncbi,ensembl)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot busco
docs.text:
Synteny of BUSCO genes across genomes.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot busco [OPTIONS] TABLES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after BUSCO-based chromosome synteny plots (ChromSyn, github.com/slimsuite/chromsyn; Oxford dot plots of BUSCO genes). Needs only the full_table.tsv of a BUSCO (or compleasm) run per assembly (or a marker<TAB>sequence<TAB>start<TAB>end table), so genomes without annotation can be compared:

  1. markers: complete single-copy BUSCOs with their positions; a BUSCO single-copy in two genomes is an anchor between them;
  2. blocks: along the first genome of each adjacent pair, runs of anchors on the same pair of chromosomes whose order in the second genome keeps one direction (one out-of-place anchor is allowed, --min-busco anchors per block) are syntenic blocks, inverted when the order falls;
  3. layout: chromosomes of each genome are ordered and oriented after the genome above it (by their main partner and the median position on it), so that rearrangements stand out;
  4. figures: chromosome painting (every BUSCO coloured by its reference chromosome, or by its ancestral linkage group with --algs, for instance from macro ancestors) with blocks as ribbons between adjacent genomes, and Oxford dot plots of every genome against the reference.

Writes <prefix>.busco.anchors.tsv, <prefix>.busco.blocks.tsv, <prefix>.busco.summary.tsv and the figures <prefix>.busco.<format> and <prefix>.busco.dotplots.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TABLES BUSCO full_table.tsv files or run folders, the reference first.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --names Comma-separated genome names (default: file names). --lengths NAME=FILE chromosome lengths (.fai), repeatable. (default: []) --min-busco Fewest BUSCOs in a syntenic block. (default: 3) --ribbons Draw blocks between adjacent genomes. --algs BUSCOlinkage group table (macro ancestors): colour by ancestral chromosome. --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot chromosome
docs.text:
Paint features onto chromosomes (mcscan3 plot chromosome; legacy graphics.chromosome).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot chromosome [OPTIONS] BEDFILE MAPPINGFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Features in a BED file are painted onto vertical chromosome glyphs, coloured by class. The optional id_mappings file maps feature ids to classes (id<TAB>class[<TAB>color]); without it each feature id is its own class. A feature named centromere marks a centromere. Chromosome lengths come from --sizes (else the last feature end):

mcscan3 plot chromosome peach.bed peach.idmap --sizes=peach.sizes --seed=666

Class colours are random unless given in the mapping file (--seed for reproducible colours). --gauge draws a Mb ruler; --imagemap also writes an HTML image map (<prefix>.map) of --winsize windows; --mergedist merges nearby regions of the same class.

docs.title: mcscan3 plot circos
docs.text:
Circular synteny plot of several genomes.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot circos [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the circular genome plots of Circos (Krzywinski et al. 2009, Genome Research). The chromosomes of every genome sit on one circle, each genome on its own arc (equal arcs by default, or arcs in proportion to genome size with --scale bp). An outer track shows gene density along the chromosomes; inside, every syntenic block between two genomes is a ribbon through the centre, coloured by the chromosome of the reference genome it touches, or traced to it through the other blocks:

mcscan3 plot circos dmel dyak dpse agam --ref dmel --suffix lifted.anchors -o insects.circos.pdf

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed); anchors files between pairs of genomes are looked up as <a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>. --pairs ref (default) draws the blocks of the reference with each other genome, --pairs ring those of neighbouring genomes around the circle and --pairs all every pair with an anchors file.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, clockwise from the top (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome: ribbons are coloured by its chromosomes. --outfile, -o Output figure (PDF, PNG or SVG). (default: circos.pdf) --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --pairs Blocks drawn: ref (reference with each genome), ring or all. (default: ref) --scale fit (equal arc per genome) or bp (arcs by genome size). (default: fit) --labels Display names, comma-separated. --min-block Do not draw blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 10) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --no-density Leave out the gene density track. --size Figure width in inches. (default: 8.0) --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --title Figure title.

docs.title: mcscan3 plot dot3d
docs.text:
Three-genome dot plot in 3D.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot dot3d [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. A gene of the reference genome A that is syntenic to a gene of B and to a gene of C is one point (A, B, C) in a cube whose axes are the three genomes, laid out chromosome after chromosome in base pairs. Colinear blocks shared by the three genomes become lines in space; a whole-genome duplication in one genome doubles the lines along its axis.

The three walls of the cube carry the pairwise dot plots: the floor A x B, the back wall A x C and the side wall B x C (from <B>.<C>.anchors when given, otherwise the projection of the three-way points). Points are coloured by the reference chromosome:

mcscan3 plot dot3d dmel dyak dpse --suffix lifted.anchors -o flies.dot3d.pdf --html flies.html

--html also writes a self-contained interactive page (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, hover for gene names, click a chromosome in the legend to hide it). Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed); anchors files are looked up as <a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Three genome names, the reference first (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output figure (PDF, PNG or SVG). (default: dot3d.pdf) --html Also write an interactive HTML page (rotate, zoom, hover). --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --labels Display names of the three genomes, comma-separated. --views Viewing angles elevation,azimuth; several separated by ';' (one panel each). (default: 22,-58) --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --max-copies Syntenic copies per reference gene and genome. (default: 2) --reorder Order and flip chromosomes of the other genomes after the reference. --title Figure title.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text: Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

docs.title: Example 1

docs.title: mcscan3 plot dotplot
docs.text:
Dot plot of anchors or Ks values (mcscan3 plot dotplot; legacy graphics.dotplot).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot dotplot [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each anchor pair is a dot at (rank of the query gene, rank of the subject gene); chromosome boundaries are drawn as grid lines:

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed -o grape.peach.pdf

A third column (e.g. Ks) colours the dots when --cmaptext is given (values outside --vmin..--vmax are dropped); a .ks file is converted to anchors first. Blocks can be coloured by class (--colormap: block_id<TAB>class, 1-based ids) or by orientation (--colororientation). --synteny boxes the blocks found by a quick synteny scan. At most --nmax dots are drawn (a random subset). --grid-color is the Set1 colour index of the grid lines (the original's --theme).

--qorder and --sorder choose, order and flip the chromosomes of either axis by hand, and zoom on parts of them: a comma-separated list of chromosomes, a trailing - drawing one reversed, and chrom:start-end (10M, 250k allowed) keeping only that range. Reversed chromosomes carry a minus after their name. A fusion or fission is checked by zooming on the chromosomes involved:

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors --qorder 5,2-,9 --sorder 1:10M-25M,4 -o zoom.pdf

Without them the subject chromosomes are ordered and flipped along the query (--order auto).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file (or .ks file) of gene pairs.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --synteny Run a fast synteny scan and box the blocks. --cmaptext Colour dots by the 3rd column; label of the colour bar. --vmin Minimum value in the colour map. (default: 0) --vmax Maximum value in the colour map. (default: 2) --nmax Maximum number of dots (random subset) (default: 10000; all with --theme mcscan3). --minfont Do not draw labels smaller than this. (default: 4) --colormap block_idclass file: colour blocks by class. --colororientation Colour blocks by orientation. --nosort Do not sort the seqids along the axes. --nosep Do not draw chromosome grid lines. --title Title of the dot plot. --skipempty Skip seqids without matches. --nochpf Do not change the contig names. --nostdpf Do not standardise contig names. --genomenames Axis names as qname_sname, e.g. "Vitis vinifera_Oryza sativa". --grid-color Set1 colour index (0-8) of the grid lines. (default: 2) --outfile, -o Output image (default: .); a .html name makes an interactive dot plot (zoom, pan, genes on hover). --order Subject chromosomes: name, or auto (follow the query, flip reversed ones) [default: auto with --theme mcscan3]. --oi ortholog soi .oi table: grey out low Orthology Index blocks. --oi-cutoff Orthology Index of orthologous blocks. (default: 0.6) --qorder Query chromosomes to show, in this order: 5,2-,9:10M-25M (- reverses, :start-end zooms). --sorder Subject chromosomes to show, in this order (as --qorder); overrides --order auto. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 9x9) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 90) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: dark) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map [default: copper (mcscan3), copper (classic)]. --notex Do not use LaTeX (MCscan3 uses LaTeX only when installed). --chinese Render Chinese labels (implies --notex). --seed Random seed when assigning colours. --theme mcscan3 (default; or set MCSCAN3_THEME) or classic (the original look).

docs.title: mcscan3 plot families
docs.text:
Gene family evolution on the species tree.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot families [OPTIONS] RESULTS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Reads the results of phylo families (an output prefix) or a CAFE5 output folder (Base_* or Gamma_* files), and draws:

  • a summary tree (<out>.summary): every branch coloured by its net number of significant changes, with the significant expansions (+) and contractions (-) above it and all changes below it; bars beside the tips repeat the significant changes of each species;
  • a grid of families (<out>.top_families): the most significant families, each on its own small tree, with the gene count at every node, branches coloured by expansion or contraction, thicker as the change grows, and marked by the branch p-value (*** p <= 0.001, ** <= 0.01, * <= 0.05); one figure for any number of families instead of a file per family;
  • one family in detail (plot family): the species tree with a circle at every node sized by the gene count, next to the family's gene tree (from --gene-tree, OrthoFinder's resolved gene trees, or grouped by species without one), its genes coloured by species, with the domain architecture of every protein (--domains: Pfam, HMMER or InterProScan) drawn along its length;
  • Gene Ontology enrichment at every branch (--obo and --annotations): the families significantly expanded, and those contracted, on each branch, against all analysed families. A family carries a term when at least --go-min-share (half) of its annotated genes do, so large families do not collect terms from a few genes; writes <out>.go.tsv and a dot grid of terms by branch (<out>.go), branches in tree order.
mcscan3 plot families fam -o fig                         # phylo families -o fam
mcscan3 plot families cafe_results/ -o fig --format svg  # a CAFE5 folder
mcscan3 plot families fam -o fig --obo go-basic.obo --annotations ath.gaf --annotations osa.gaf
mcscan3 plot family fam OG0000123 -o og123 --gene-tree OG0000123_tree.txt --domains pfam.domtbl

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description RESULTS phylo families output prefix, or a CAFE5 output folder.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --top Families in the grid of the most significant. (default: 24) --family Draw these families in the grid instead (repeatable). (default: []) --columns Panels per row of the grids. (default: 4) --no-highlights Skip the figure of highlighted families. --alpha Significance of families and branches. (default: 0.05) --obo Gene Ontology (go-basic.obo): GO enrichment per branch. --annotations GO annotations (eggNOG-mapper, GAF, GPAD, gene2go, InterProScan, table). (default: []) --orthogroups Orthogroups.tsv: the genes of each family (needed for GO with CAFE5 results). --go-min-share Share of a family's annotated genes a term needs. (default: 0.5) --expansion-color Colour of expansions. (default: #D55E00) --contraction-color Colour of contractions. (default: #0072B2) --cladogram Ignore branch lengths (tips aligned). --font-scale Scale all text. (default: 1.0) --width Figure width in inches (0: automatic). (default: 0.0) --height Figure height in inches (0: automatic). (default: 0.0) --highlight Shade a clade or species: 'colour:sp1+sp2' (their last common ancestor; repeatable). (default: []) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot family
docs.text:
One gene family in detail.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot family [OPTIONS] RESULTS NAME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Draws one family of phylo families (an output prefix) or CAFE5 (an output folder) in three aligned panels:

  • the species tree with a circle at every node sized by the family's gene count there, branches coloured by expansion or contraction (pale when not significant), thicker as the change grows, and stars for the branch p-value (*** p <= 0.001, ** <= 0.01, * <= 0.05);
  • the family's gene tree: --gene-tree, or the resolved gene tree of an OrthoFinder run (--orthofinder), with each gene coloured by its species; without a tree the genes are grouped by species, in the order of the species tree;
  • the domain architecture of every protein (--domains: HMMER --domtblout, pfam_scan.pl or InterProScan), drawn along its length (--proteins gives the lengths), in a colour key of its own.

Colours, cladogram layout, text size, figure size and shaded clades (--highlight) are options, as in plot families.

mcscan3 plot family fam OG0000123 -o og123 --orthogroups Orthogroups.tsv \
    --orthofinder OrthoFinder/Results_x --domains pfam.domtbl --proteins proteins.faa
mcscan3 plot family cafe_results/ OG0000123 -o og123 --orthogroups Orthogroups.tsv --gene-tree og123.nwk

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description RESULTS phylo families output prefix, or a CAFE5 output folder. NAME The family (orthogroup) to draw.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --orthogroups Orthogroups.tsv: the family's genes. --gene-tree The family's gene tree (Newick). --orthofinder OrthoFinder results folder: its resolved gene tree of the family. --domains Protein domains: HMMER --domtblout, pfam_scan.pl or InterProScan TSV (repeatable). (default: []) --proteins Protein FASTA (protein lengths for the domain track). (default: []) --alpha Significance of families and branches. (default: 0.05) --expansion-color Colour of expansions. (default: #D55E00) --contraction-color Colour of contractions. (default: #0072B2) --cladogram Ignore branch lengths (tips aligned). --font-scale Scale all text. (default: 1.0) --width Figure width in inches (0: automatic). (default: 0.0) --height Figure height in inches (0: automatic). (default: 0.0) --highlight Shade a clade or species: 'colour:sp1+sp2' (their last common ancestor; repeatable). (default: []) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot histogram
docs.text:
Histogram of numbers (mcscan3 plot histogram; legacy graphics.histogram).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot histogram [OPTIONS] NUMBERFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Input files hold one number per line (--col picks another whitespace-separated column, --skip skips header lines). Only values within --vmin..--vmax are counted; summary statistics go to stderr:

mcscan3 plot histogram ks.values --vmax=3               # ks.values.pdf
mcscan3 plot histogram ks.values --vmax=3 --ascii       # text histogram on stderr
mcscan3 plot histogram a.txt b.txt --tags=A,B --facet   # a_b.pdf, one panel per file

--base=2|10 bins by powers of the base (log axis). --quick plots a file of value<TAB>count pairs as bars with the counts written above them.

The original drew figures with R/ggplot2; MCscan3 draws the same kind of figure with matplotlib (no R needed), so figures differ in look but not in content. The text mode is unchanged.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description NUMBERFILES Files with one number per line.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --skip Skip the first several lines. (default: 0) --col Use the n-th column (0-based). (default: 0) --vmin Minimum value, inclusive. (default: 0) --vmax Maximum value, inclusive (default: data maximum). --bins Number of bins. (default: 20) --xlabel Label on the X-axis. (default: value) --title Title (default: first file name). --tags Comma-separated names of the input files. --ascii Print a text histogram (stderr) instead of a figure. --base Logarithmic bins with base 2 or 10; 0 to disable. (default: 0) --facet One panel per input file. --fill Bar colour. (default: white) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --quick Input is value<TAB>count (already binned). --noprintstats With --quick: no statistics on the plot. --plain Text mode: print the title and no rich markup (fix).
