docs.title: mcscan3 plot karyotype
docs.text:
Macrosynteny between genomes drawn as chromosome tracks (mcscan3 plot karyotype; legacy graphics.karyotype).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot karyotype [OPTIONS] SEQIDSFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
seqids lists the chromosomes of each track, one track per line (comma-separated; a trailing - draws a chromosome reversed; # starts a comment). The layout file describes each track, then the edges (syntenic wedges from .simple block files):

# y, xstart, xend, rotation, color, label, va, bed[, label_va]
.6, .1, .4, 0, m, Grape, top, grape.bed, center
.4, .3, .6, 60, k, Athaliana, top, athaliana.bed, center
# edges
e, 0, 1, athaliana.grape.4x1.simple[, samearc]

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout -o karyotype.pdf

Chromosome lengths are in genes (--basepair: base pairs). Track colours are random when not given (--seed). --shadestyle curve or line, --chrstyle auto, rect or roundrect, --keep-chrlabels keeps full names in the circles, --nocircles drops them.

With --genomes the horizontal tracks share one scale and are centred, so chromosome lengths compare between genomes (--to-scale, the default there; --fill stretches every track to the width of the layout).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SEQIDSFILE Chromosomes of each track, one track per line, comma-separated (not with --genomes). LAYOUTFILE Track layout, then e, i, j, blocks.simple edge lines (not with --genomes).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output image. (default: karyotype.pdf) --basepair Use base-pair positions instead of gene ranks. --keep-chrlabels Keep full chromosome labels. --nocircles Do not draw chromosome circles. --shadestyle Wedges: curve or line. (default: curve) --chrstyle Chromosomes: auto, rect or roundrect. (default: auto) --genomes Genomes top to bottom, comma-separated: layout made automatically. --bed-dir With --genomes: directory of .bed. (default: .) --anchors-dir With --genomes: directory of . anchors. (default: .) --anchors-suffix With --genomes: anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --min-frac With --genomes: drop chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction. (default: 0.005) --auto-order Order and flip chromosomes to follow the track above (default: on with --genomes). --color-by Ribbon colours: none, chr (first track's chromosome), car (--cars) or labels (--labels) [default: chr with --theme mcscan3, else none]. --cars CARs TSV from ancestral genomes (for --color-by car). --families Gene families used for the CARs (for --color-by car). --labels genelabel table (for --color-by labels). --to-scale Tracks share one length scale, centred (default with --genomes); --fill: every track full width. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 8x7) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... docs.title: mcscan3 plot ks
docs.text:
Ks distribution figures (mcscan3 plot ks, mcscan3 ks multireport, ks report --pdf).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot ks [OPTIONS] KSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The distribution of Nei-Gojobori Ks values (within --vmin..--vmax) is drawn as the percentage of gene pairs per bin, as a line with markers (--fill: a filled area; --kde: a smoothed curve):

mcscan3 plot ks grape.peach.ks                  # Ks_plot.pdf
mcscan3 ks multireport ks.layout -o Ks_plot.png # several Ks files in one figure

--fit adds a log-normal mixture of --components peaks fitted to log(Ks), with the peak positions labelled. The original shelled out to an external gmm-bic program for the fit; MCscan3 fits the mixture itself (expectation-maximisation), so no extra program is needed.

The multireport layout file lists Ks file, ncomponents, label, color, marker per line (# lines are comments); a missing colour or marker is assigned at random (--seed). If the layout file does not exist, a template listing the *.ks files below the current directory is written first.

docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE Ks file.

(default: 0.0) --vmax Maximum value, inclusive. (default: 3.0) --bins Number of histogram bins. (default: 60) --fit Add a fitted log-normal mixture (peaks labelled). --kde Smooth the distribution (Gaussian KDE). --legendp Legend position (matplotlib loc). docs.title: mcscan3 plot locus
docs.text:
Microsynteny of one locus across genomes, in several styles.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot locus [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Give a gene (--gene) or region (--region chr:start-end) of the reference genome (the first one named) and the anchors between the reference and every other genome; the syntenic regions are found automatically (the largest runs of anchor partners, up to --copies per genome, for duplicated genomes; --copies scer=2 for one genome) and drawn in one of four styles:

ribbons gene arrows on one track per region, homologous genes joined by ribbons between neighbouring tracks; arrows tracks aligned on the focal gene (base pairs from it, regions flipped so that it points the same way), homologs in one colour per reference gene; matrix one row per region and one column per reference gene: kept in the same orientation, inverted or missing (compact for many genomes); dots a local dot plot per region (reference genes against the region's genes).

Several styles at once (--style ribbons,matrix or all) write one figure each:

mcscan3 plot locus dmel dsim dyak dpse agam --gene rna-NM_079260.3 --suffix lifted.anchors \
    --style all -o adh

Colours (--color-by): homolog (one colour per reference gene, default), strand or focal (only the focal gene and its homologs). --layout middle puts the reference in the middle of the ribbons tracks (the two copies of a duplicated genome on either side), --scale bp draws ribbons tracks to scale (default: genes evenly spaced), --highlight marks more genes, --gene-labels names the reference genes.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, the reference first (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --gene Focal gene of the reference: ID or symbol (with --names). --region Or a region of the reference, chr:start-end. --outfile, -o Output prefix: .

docs.title: mcscan3 plot microsynteny
docs.text:
Local synteny of gene-level tracks (mcscan3 plot microsynteny; legacy graphics.synteny).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot microsynteny [OPTIONS] BLOCKSFILE BEDFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Draws the regions of an MCscan blocks file (one column per track, from synteny mcscan) as gene tracks, with wedges between syntenic genes:

mcscan3 plot microsynteny micro.blocks all.bed micro.layout

The layout file has one line per track, x, y, rotation, ha, va, color[, ratio[, label[, fontsize]]] (a leading * hides the track), then e, i, j[, color[, samearc]] lines for the wedges between tracks i and j. ha is left, right, leftalign, rightalign, center or empty; va is top, bottom, center or empty. Saved as <blocks prefix>.<format>.

Options: --switch renames seqids (two columns); --tree draws trees below the tracks; --extra adds features (BED, e.g. repeats); --genelabels/--genelabelsize label genes; --glyphstyle box or arrow; --glyphcolor orientation or orthogroup; --scalebar.

Everything can be styled from the command line, without editing the layout file:

  • --gene-colors FILE: gene<TAB>colour[<TAB>label]; those genes are drawn in their colour on top of the others, the links that touch them take the same colour, and the labels make a legend;
  • --highlight g1,g2 with --highlight-color: a quick way to colour a few genes;
  • --forward-color/--reverse-color: strand colours; --link-color/--link-alpha: the colour and transparency of every other link (the layout's per-edge colour is the default);
  • --track-labels "Grape,Peach,Poplar": track names in layout order; --label-color, --gene-label-color: text colours;
  • --align left|center|right: line the tracks up on their left ends, centres or right ends; --align-gene GENE: shift every track so that this gene and its syntenic partners sit on one vertical line;
  • --theme classic keeps the legacy look (100Kb, bp ranges); the default theme shows ranges in Mb with "(−)" for a reversed segment and the scale bar in kb.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLOCKSFILE MCscan blocks file (one column per track). BEDFILE BED of all genes in the blocks. LAYOUTFILE Layout: one line per track, then e, i, j wedge lines.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --switch Rename seqids with this two-column file. --tree Trees to display below the tracks. --extra Extra features (BED), e.g. repeats. --genelabels Label only these genes (comma-separated). --genelabelsize Gene label font size (0: no labels). (default: 0) --genelabelrotation Gene label angle (anti-clockwise). (default: 25) --scalebar Add a scale bar. --vpad Gap between a track's name and its coordinates (axes units). (default: 0.015) --glyphstyle Gene glyphs: box or arrow. (default: box) --glyphcolor Colour genes by orientation or orthogroup. (default: orientation) --shadestyle Wedges: curve or line. (default: curve) --outputprefix Prefix of the output file. --noprune Keep extra features under 0.1% of the region. --gene-colors genecolour[label] file: genes and their links in that colour. --highlight Genes to colour (comma-separated). --highlight-color Colour of --highlight genes. (default: #d62728) --forward-color Colour of + strand genes. --reverse-color Colour of - strand genes. --link-color Colour of the links (default: layout's). --link-alpha Link opacity, 0-1. (default: 1.0) --track-labels Track names in layout order (comma-separated). --label-color Colour of the track names. --gene-label-color Colour of gene labels. (default: lightslategray) --align Line tracks up on their left, center or right ends. (default: center) --align-gene Put this gene and its partners on one vertical. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 8x7) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: darkgrid) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map [default: viridis (mcscan3), jet (classic)]. --notex Do not use LaTeX (MCscan3 uses LaTeX only when installed). --chinese Render Chinese labels (implies --notex). --seed Random seed when assigning colours. --theme mcscan3 (default; or set MCSCAN3_THEME) or classic (the original look).

docs.title: mcscan3 plot painting
docs.text:
Chromosomes of one genome painted by the syntenic chromosomes of another.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot painting [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. The bar plot of MCScanX (bar_plotter) drawn as a karyotype in the style of karyoploteR: every chromosome of the target genome is a horizontal ideogram to base-pair scale, and each colinear block paints the span it covers with the colour of the source chromosome it comes from. Two copies after a whole-genome duplication show as the same colour on two target chromosomes; a fusion as two colours on one:

mcscan3 plot painting grape.poplar.anchors --qbed grape.bed --sbed poplar.bed -o poplar.painting.pdf

The target is the second genome of the anchors (--target q: the first). Blocks with fewer than --min-block anchors are skipped; target chromosomes holding fewer than --min-frac of its genes (small scaffolds) are left out. A block is drawn as one band over its span; where blocks overlap, the larger one is drawn on top.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --outfile, -o Output figure. (default: painting.pdf) --target Genome painted: s (second, default) or q (first). (default: s) --min-block Skip blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 5) --min-frac Drop target chromosomes with fewer genes than this. (default: 0.005) --names Display names of the two genomes, comma-separated. --figsize Width x height in inches (default: by chromosomes). --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot phylo
docs.text:
Tree figures.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot phylo [OPTIONS] TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: publication tree figures without a separate tree package (the features people reach for ete3 or iTOL for), in the MCscan3 house style:

  • rectangular (phylogram or --cladogram) or --layout circular trees, rooted on --outgroup or at the midpoint (--midpoint), ladderized;
  • support values from the node labels (--min-support: only those below), or pies of the share (--pies: node labels such as gCF 95/62 give the second number);
  • clades shaded and labelled (--highlight "NAME1,NAME2=label": the smallest clade holding the names) and tips coloured by group (--groups FILE: tipgroup);
  • a table aligned to the tips (--data FILE, tip in the first column): numeric columns drawn as a heatmap (--data-style heatmap) or stacked bars (stacked);
  • a tanglegram against a second tree (--tangle OTHER.nwk), with the Robinson-Foulds distance:
    • mcscan3 plot phylo species.nwk --outgroup scer --highlight "dmel,agam=Diptera" --data busco.tsv -o tree

docs.text: Argument Description TREE Newick tree.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --outgroup Outgroup tip(s) to root on (repeatable). (default: []) --midpoint Root at the midpoint. --layout rect or circular. (default: rect) --cladogram Ignore branch lengths. --min-support Show support values only below this. --pies Pies from node labels (last number, e.g. gCF of 95/62). --highlight Shade a clade: 'TIP1,TIP2=label' (repeatable). (default: []) --groups tipgroup: tip label colours. --data Table aligned to the tips (tip in the first column). --data-style heatmap or stacked. (default: heatmap) --tangle Second tree: draw a tanglegram. --italic Italic tip labels (species names). --title Figure title. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot ribbon
docs.text:
Shared identity between aligned chromosomes as ribbons (mcscan3 plot ribbon; legacy graphics.ribbon).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot ribbon [OPTIONS] BLOCKSFILE BEDFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each track is a chromosome range; ribbons join the aligned intervals of a blocks file (one column per track; the intervals are BED features):

mcscan3 plot ribbon alignment.blocks alignment.bed ribbon.layout --reorient=F,R

The layout has one line per track, then e, i, j edge lines:

# x, y, rotation, ha, va, color, ratio, label, chrmName, rStart, rEnd, chrmMax
0.5, 0.6, 0, top, center, g, 1, Spp 1 Chrm 8, Chromosome_08, 2000000, 2108098, 2108098

--reorient flips tracks (F/R per track). --paintbystrand colours ribbons by relative orientation (--strandcolors), --paintbyscore sets their transparency from the BED score (0-100; --scalealpha rescales 50-100 to 0.1-0.9). --annotations and --extra-annotations draw feature tracks above and below each chromosome (BED columns 7-9: colour, offset and height multipliers); --annotation-boxes frames regions. Saved as <blocks prefix>.<format> (or --outfile).

The original crashed without --reorient, with --annotations, --scalebar or --tree, and with 11-column layout lines (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.13, A.22).

docs.title: Arguments

docs.title: mcscan3 plot riparian
docs.text:
Riparian (braid) plot of synteny across several genomes.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot riparian [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the riparian plots of GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife). Each genome is a row of chromosomes, with lengths in genes (--basepair: base pairs). Syntenic blocks between neighbouring rows are drawn as braids, coloured by the reference chromosome they descend from. The colours spread from the reference row to the others through the blocks:

mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape -o riparian.pdf

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed). Anchors files between neighbouring genomes are looked up as in pan genes (<a>.<b>.anchors or <b>.<a>.anchors). Braids that cannot be traced to a reference chromosome are grey. Small scaffolds (--min-frac) are left out and the other genomes' chromosomes are ordered and flipped to follow their neighbour (--no-reorder keeps the natural order).

Regions such as QTL intervals are traced through the anchors into every genome and drawn in their own colours over grey synteny (--highlight, a file of genome chrom start end [name [colour]]`), or drawn alone with their syntenic regions and a flank of genes (`--region):

mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape --highlight qtl.txt -o qtl.pdf
mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape --region grape:chr1:5000000-7000000

Both write <figure>.regions.tsv: the coordinates of each region in each genome, one line per syntenic interval (several for duplicated regions).

All rows share one scale (base pairs or genes), so chromosome lengths compare across genomes, and each row is centred (--fill stretches every row to the full width instead). Three options give a macrosynteny view or a fixed layout:

  • --merge-gap N joins blocks of the same chromosome pair that are fewer than N genes apart on both genomes, so a chromosome pair is one wide braid rather than many thin ones;
  • --chrom-order GENOME=SPEC fixes the chromosomes of one row and their direction (5,2-,9: chromosome 5, then 2 reversed, then 9; repeatable). Other rows still follow their neighbours;
  • --no-reorder keeps the natural order of every row.

Reversed chromosomes are marked with a minus after their name:

mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape --merge-gap 25 --chrom-order poplar=1,2-,3 -o r.pdf

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, top to bottom (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome: braids are coloured by its chromosomes. --outfile, -o Output figure. (default: riparian.pdf) --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --basepair Chromosome lengths in base pairs, not genes. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 10x6) --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --reorder Order and flip chromosomes after the neighbouring genome. --min-block Do not draw blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 10) --labels Display names, comma-separated (... for italics). --title Figure title. --highlight Regions file (genome chrom start end [name [colour]]): QTL or loci traced into every genome. --region Draw only this region and its syntenic regions: genome:chrom:start-end. --flank Genes either side of the region (--region). (default: 20) --chrom-names Display names of chromosomes: genome, chromosome, name per line. --to-scale Rows share one length scale, centred; --fill: every row full width. --merge-gap Join blocks of the same chromosome pair closer than this many genes (macrosynteny). (default: 0) --chrom-order GENOME=5,2-,9: chromosomes of a row by hand (- reverses; repeatable). --chromosomes-only Draw only sequences named as nuclear chromosomes (.chroms.tsv).

docs.title: mcscan3 plot tree
docs.text:
Plot a Newick tree (mcscan3 plot tree; legacy graphics.tree).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot tree [OPTIONS] NEWICK

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The tree is rerooted at the midpoint (or --outgroup; --noreroot keeps the given root) and drawn with leaf names, node support and a scale bar, to <tree prefix>.<format>:

mcscan3 plot tree tree.nwk --outgroup=rice

Annotations: --leafinfo (CSV name,color,new_name) recolours or renames leaves; --groups names the leaf colour groups to the right of the tree; --wgdinfo (CSV node,divergence,name,color,style) marks whole-genome duplications; --geoscale draws a geological time scale (branch lengths in 100 million years; 95% HPD intervals in the Newick are drawn as bars); --gffdir draws each gene's exon structure (<gene>.gff) and --sizes its protein length. Needs the phylo extra (ete4).

docs.text: Argument Description NEWICK Newick tree file (or demo).

docs.title: Options

(default: 0.2) --gffdir Directory of .gff files: draw exon structures. --sizes FASTA or sizes file: show protein lengths. --sh, --SH SH test p-value to print. --leafcolor Font colour of the leaves. (default: k) --leaffont Font size of the leaves. (default: 12) --leafinfo CSV of leaves: name,color,new_name. --scutoff Show node support above this value (0-100). (default: 0) --no-support Do not print node support values. --no-internal Do not label internal nodes. --dashedoutgroup Dash the edges between outgroup and ingroup. --geoscale Draw a geological time scale. --wgdinfo CSV of WGD events: node,divergence,name,color,style. --groups Names of the leaf colour groups, top to bottom, comma-separated. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. docs.text:
Reformat FASTA and clean up sequence IDs (mcscan3 prep fasta-format; legacy formats.fasta format).

Group prep · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep fasta-format [OPTIONS] INFASTA OUTFASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Used in the MCscan tutorial to normalise CDS/protein files before alignment:

mcscan3 prep fasta-format grape.cds.fa.gz grape.cds

Records are re-written with Biopython (60 columns per line). The ID is the first word of the header unless changed by the options; the rest of the header is kept unless --nodesc.

docs.title: Options

(default: 0) --pad0 Zero-pad sequential IDs to this width. (default: 0) --gb For GenBank IDs, keep the accession. --sep Split the header by this string ... --index ... and use the i-th field as ID. (default: 0) --noversion Remove the trailing .version. --prefix Prepend to IDs. --suffix Append to IDs. --template template=a dir=x library=m -> m-a/x. --switch Two-column file mapping old to new IDs. --annotation Two-column file with descriptions. --ids Write the ID conversion table here. --upper Upper-case sequences. --nodesc Drop the description after the ID. --minlength Minimum sequence length to keep. docs.title: mcscan3 prep genome
docs.text:
Longest-isoform BED, CDS and protein from a genome GFF3 + FASTA.

Group prep · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep genome [OPTIONS] GFF FASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One step from a raw genome annotation to the MCscan inputs: for every gene, the transcript with the longest coding sequence is kept (ties: the first listed); its CDS is spliced from the genome (reverse-complemented on the minus strand, honouring the phase of the first CDS part) and translated. Writes <prefix>.bed, <prefix>.cds and <prefix>.pep, and <prefix>.chroms.tsv (chromosome names of the FASTA descriptions or GFF regions, used to label figures):

mcscan3 prep genome grape.gff3.gz grape.dna.fa.gz --prefix grape

IDs are cleaned: prefixes such as transcript: or gene: (Ensembl) are removed. --name gene names each record by its gene instead of its transcript. Transcripts without a CDS (non-coding) are skipped, as are genes whose CDS is shorter than --min-length codons. The GFF and FASTA may be gzip-compressed.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Genome annotation (GFF3, may be .gz). FASTA Genome sequence (FASTA, may be .gz).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -p, -o Output prefix: .bed, .cds, .pep. --name Name records by transcript or gene. (default: transcript) --min-length Skip genes with a CDS shorter than this (codons). (default: 0) --table Genetic code (NCBI translation table). (default: 1) --types GFF feature types of transcripts. (default: mRNA,transcript) --chrom-names Name chromosomes as in the FASTA descriptions (NC_001133.9 -> chrI). --symbols Also write .names.tsv: gene symbols of the GFF, for figures.

docs.text: Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

docs.title: mcscan3 prep gff2bed
docs.text:
Convert GFF features to BED (mcscan3 prep gff2bed; legacy formats.gff bed).

Group prep · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep gff2bed [OPTIONS] GFF_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Typical MCscan preparation keeps one transcript per gene:

mcscan3 prep gff2bed --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only grape.gff3.gz -o grape.bed

primary_only keeps the first transcript listed for each gene (original behaviour). longest (MCscan3 addition) instead keeps the transcript with the longest total CDS length (the transcript span if it has no CDS); ties keep the first listed.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF_FILE GFF3/GFF2 file (may be .gz).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --type Feature types, comma-separated; all for all. (default: gene) --key Attribute used as the BED name. (default: ID) --accn Use this fixed name in column 4. --source Only these GFF sources (comma-separated). --span Use the feature span as the score. --score-attrib Attribute used as the score. --append-source Prefix the name with the GFF source. --append-ftype Prefix the name with the feature type. --append-attrib Append this attribute to the name. --nosort Keep GFF order instead of sorting. --primary-only Keep the first transcript per gene. --longest Keep the transcript with the longest CDS per gene. --parent-key Attribute grouping transcripts into genes. (default: Parent) --human-chr Only 1-22,X,Y,MT; add chr prefix. --ensembl-cds Name CDS as transcript_name.exon_number. --outfile, -o Output file (default: stdout). (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 promoter compare
docs.text:
Promoter divergence of gene pairs and motif enrichment (mcscan3 promoter compare, promoter enrich).

Group promoter · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 promoter compare [OPTIONS] SITES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Binding sites from promoter scan are compared between the genes of pairs that MCscan3 finds: syntenic orthologs and duplicates (anchors), duplicates by mode (dup classify .pairs), homoeologs (subgenome homoeologs sets) or any two-column table:

  1. divergence: for every pair, the motif content of the two promoters (--level family or motif) as Jaccard similarity, and positional conservation (sites of the same family within --window bp of the same position relative to the transcription start, both directions);
  2. against chance: each category (one per --pairs file) against random pairs of scanned genes (--permutations): mean similarity, empirical p-value and effect size. Duplicates whose promoters are no more alike than random genes have diverged in regulation;
  3. with age: with --ks (gene1, gene2 and a Ks column), Spearman correlation of promoter similarity with Ks per category: promoters of older duplicates are expected to have drifted;
  4. asymmetry: per family, pairs where only the first or only the second gene keeps a site, tested against 1:1 (two-sided binomial, Benjamini-Hochberg). With pairs ordered by subgenome (homoeolog sets list subgenomes in order) this is biased retention of cis-elements.

promoter enrich tests every family for promoters of a gene set carrying it more (or less) often than the other scanned promoters (Fisher's exact test, BH) — e.g. retained duplicates, genes of a QTL or a co-expression module.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SITES Sites of promoter scan (.tfbs.tsv).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --pairs Pairs FILE[:CATEGORY]: anchors, .pairs or homoeolog sets (repeatable). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --promoters Scanned promoters (.promoters.fa); default: next to the sites. --level Compare TF families or single motifs. (default: family) --window Distance for a positionally conserved site (bp). (default: 50) --ks Ks table (gene1, gene2, a column ending in ks). --max-q Only sites with q-values up to this. (default: 1.0) --permutations Random pairs for the null. (default: 1000) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 promoter enrich
docs.text:
Motif families enriched or depleted in the promoters of gene sets.

Group promoter · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 promoter enrich [OPTIONS] SITES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. From the sites of promoter scan, every TF family (or motif, --level) is tested for being carried by the promoters of a gene set more or less often than by the other scanned promoters (--background narrows them): Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and a log2 odds ratio (0.5 added to every cell). Gene sets can be any list: retained duplicates, genes of a QTL, a co-expression module, the genes of one subgenome.

Writes <prefix>.enrich.tsv and the figure.

(default: family) --max-q Only sites with q-values up to this. (default: 1.0) --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 promoter scan
docs.text:
Promoters and their transcription factor binding sites.

Group promoter · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 promoter scan [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, for plants and any other species with a motif library:

  1. promoters: from an annotation and its genome, the window --upstream bp before to --downstream bp after the transcription start of each gene (its longest transcript), on the gene's strand; the upstream part stops at the nearest other gene unless --no-clip (so a promoter never reaches into a neighbour). A FASTA of promoters can be given instead;
  2. motifs: a library in MEME, JASPAR, TRANSFAC or HOMER format, or jaspar:<taxon> (see promoter.motifs); --families maps motifs to TF families;
  3. scan (--engine): fimo (MEME suite; Grant CE, Bailey TL & Noble WS 2011, Bioinformatics 27:1017), native (log-odds scores and exact p-values against the base composition of the promoters, both strands; on a CUDA GPU through CuPy when installed), plantpan (a local PlantPAN 5 stand-alone image run with Docker, with its own plant motif library; plantpan.itps.ncku.edu.tw, github.com/wenchilab/plantpan5-standalone), or auto (FIMO when installed, else native). Matches at --pvalue or lower are kept with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values over every position scanned.

Positions are relative to the transcription start (negative upstream). Writes <prefix>.promoters.fa, <prefix>.tfbs.tsv (one row per site), <prefix>.tfbs.genes.tsv (sites per gene and family), <prefix>.tfbs.json and the figure.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --gff Annotation (GFF3/GTF) for the promoters. --genome Genome FASTA of the annotation. --fasta Promoter sequences instead of --gff/--genome. --motifs, -m Motif file (MEME, JASPAR, TRANSFAC, HOMER) or jaspar:. --families TSV motif -> TF family. --engine auto, fimo, native or plantpan (Docker image). (default: auto) --upstream Bases before the transcription start. (default: 1000) --downstream Bases after the transcription start. (default: 200) --clip Stop the promoter at the nearest other gene. --level Name promoters by gene or by transcript. (default: gene) --name Attribute used as the name. (default: ID) --pvalue Largest p-value of a site. (default: 0.0001) --plantpan-image PlantPAN 5 stand-alone Docker image. (default: plantpan5-offline:1.1) --path Folder of fimo. --cpus Processes for the native scanner. (default: 4) --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 quota align
docs.text:
Quota alignment (mcscan3 quota align; legacy compara.quota).

Group quota · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 quota align [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Selects the set of synteny blocks with the largest total score such that every gene of genome X is covered by at most a blocks and every gene of genome Y by at most b blocks (--quota=a:b), by 0/1 integer programming (Tang et al., BMC Bioinformatics 2011). Blocks may overlap by up to --Nm genes. Writes the selected block ids to <anchors prefix>.<a>x<b> and, with --screen, the selected blocks to <anchors prefix>.<a>x<b>.anchors:

mcscan3 quota align grape.poplar.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=poplar.bed --quota=1:2 --screen

For a 1:2 pattern (one grape region, two poplar regions after the Salicoid WGD) use 1:2.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --quota Blocks per gene allowed in genome X:genome Y, e.g. 1:2. (default: 1:1) --nm Tolerated overlap between two blocks (genes). (default: 10) --self Self comparison (screening paralogous blocks). --verbose Show verbose solver output. --screen Also write the screened anchors file. --solver MIP solver: ortools (default), highs, scip, glpk. (default: ortools)

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold contacts
docs.text:
Hi-C contacts between and within contigs.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold contacts [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Read pairs come from a 4DN .pairs file (plain or gzip), from SAM/BAM (one line per pair is used: the first read, with its mate's position; samtools reads BAM), or straight from Hi-C reads, mapped here with bwa mem -5SP (the Hi-C mode of BWA, Li H 2013, arXiv:1303.3997). Pairs with a mapping quality below --min-mapq are dropped. Positions are binned (--resolution, 1 kb by default) and identical bin pairs counted, so a dataset of a hundred million pairs becomes a sparse matrix of a few million cells, kept as .npz.

The matrix gives every later step its numbers: links between contigs (for grouping), their positions (for ordering and orientation), contacts within contigs (for the distance-decay law and for finding misjoins), and the contact map figures. Restriction sites per contig (--enzyme, e.g. GATC for MboI/DpnII, AAGCTT for HindIII, GATC,GANTC for Arima) normalise link counts (cf. Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833):

mcscan3 scaffold contacts contigs.fa --pairs hic.pairs.gz -o asm
mcscan3 scaffold contacts contigs.fa --reads hic_R1.fq.gz --reads hic_R2.fq.gz --enzyme GATC -o asm

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA) the Hi-C reads were mapped to.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs, gzip ok). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM, e.g. bwa mem -5SP). --reads Hi-C reads (R1 and R2), mapped here with bwa. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --resolution Bin size (bp). (default: 1000) --enzyme Restriction motif(s), e.g. GATC or GATC,GANTC. --min-mapq Least mapping quality of both reads (SAM/BAM). (default: 1) --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold hic
docs.text:
Hi-C scaffolding of contigs into chromosomes, haplotype- and allele-aware.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold hic [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3; the steps follow ALLHiC (Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833: prune allelic links, partition, rescue, optimise, build), with ideas of HapHiC (Zeng X et al. 2024, Nat Plants), YaHS (Zhou C et al. 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btac808) and 3D-DNA (Dudchenko O et al. 2017, Science 356:92), reimplemented:

  1. break (--break): within every contig, the contacts spanning each position at short range are counted; where they fall below break_ratio of the contig's median (away from the ends), the contig is a misjoin and is cut there.
  2. prune: links between allelic contigs (alleles.py) are removed, and of the links from a contig to several alleles of one region only the strongest is kept (the others come from reads mapped to the wrong allele).
  3. partition: contigs of at least min_length are clustered by average link density (links per restriction site, or per kb, of both) into groups clusters (chromosomes x ploidy for haplotype-resolved assemblies), never joining clusters that share allelic sequence (cannot-link); then every contig is moved to the group it links to most densely, as long as that adds no allele to the group, until nothing moves. With a reference (place), contigs first go to their reference chromosome and each chromosome is split into ploidy haplotypes the same way.
  4. rescue: shorter and unassigned contigs join the group they link to most densely, when that group clearly beats the next (rescue_ratio) and holds none of their alleles.
  5. order and orient: contact probability falls with distance as d^-a, so the layout that maximises the likelihood of the links minimises the sum of log distances of all links. The links of every contig pair are compressed, per relative orientation, into a few weighted distance quantiles, so a layout is scored in microseconds. A greedy join of contig ends (strongest close links first) gives the start; a local search over flips, moves and segment reversals (batched evaluation of all candidates of a contig) improves it to a local optimum. With a reference, its order is the start.

Outputs <prefix>.agp and <prefix>.fa (scaffolds, 100 N gaps), <prefix>.groups.tsv (contig pieces with group, order, orientation) and statistics on stderr:

mcscan3 scaffold hic contigs.fa --pairs hic.pairs.gz --groups 40 --alleles auto -o asm
mcscan3 scaffold hic contigs.fa --bam hic.bam --ref mono.fa --ploidy 8 -o sugarcane

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --contacts Contacts of scaffold contacts (.npz). --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs, gzip ok). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM). --reads Hi-C reads (R1 and R2), mapped here with bwa. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --groups Number of groups: chromosomes x ploidy (without --ref). --ref Reference: contigs grouped by its chromosomes, Hi-C splits haplotypes. --ploidy Haplotypes per chromosome (with --ref, and to name homologs). (default: 1) --alleles Allele table: auto (self-alignment when --ploidy > 1), none, or a file. (default: auto) --break Cut misjoined contigs where Hi-C contacts drop. --min-length Contigs shorter than this are only rescued. (default: 20000) --resolution Bin size (bp) when reading pairs. (default: 1000) --enzyme Restriction motif(s) for normalisation. --min-mapq Least mapping quality (SAM/BAM). (default: 1) --gap Ns between joined pieces. (default: 100) --threads Threads (default: all). --plot Draw the contact map of the result.

New in MCscan3. The contacts of scaffold contacts (in contig coordinates) are lifted through an AGP (scaffold hic/ref/map output, or any AGP of the contigs) onto scaffold coordinates and binned into a square map, whole genome or selected scaffolds, drawn on a log scale with scaffold borders. A correct assembly shows strong squares along the diagonal (chromosomes) with contacts fading away from it; misjoins, inversions and wrongly placed contigs show as off-diagonal blocks and bow ties:

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold map
docs.text:
Scaffolding with genetic maps.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold map [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Chromonomer (Catchen J et al. 2020, G3 10:4115: markers anchor, split and order scaffolds) and ALLMAPS (Tang H et al. 2015, Genome Biol 16:3: several maps at once, scaffold order and orientation maximising the markers in map order), reimplemented:

  1. markers: per map a table of contig, position (bp), linkage group and cM (tab or comma separated, header optional); each map has a weight (--map maps/f2.tsv:2). Linkage-group names of later maps are matched to those of the first (most markers x weight) by the contigs they share, and their direction turned to agree with it.
  2. split: along every contig, markers fall into runs of one linkage group; where two runs of at least min_markers markers of different groups meet, the contig is cut between them (where at least min_maps maps agree).
  3. assign and order: every piece goes to the group with most (weighted) markers; within a group, pieces start in the order of their weighted median map position and are oriented by the trend of cM along them.
  4. optimise: a local search over flips, moves and segment reversals maximises the sum over maps (times weight) of the longest run of markers in map order (increasing or decreasing), the ALLMAPS objective, so a few misplaced markers do not move a piece.

Writes AGP and FASTA, <prefix>.markers.tsv (every marker with its scaffold position) and a summary per group (markers placed, Spearman rho of physical vs genetic position per map):

mcscan3 scaffold map contigs.fa --map f2.tsv --map ril.tsv:2 -o asm

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --map Markers: contig, position, linkage group, cM; path:weight; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --min-markers Markers of a linkage group needed on each side of a cut. (default: 3) --min-maps Maps that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --format Image format of the marker plot. (default: png)

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold ref
docs.text:
Reference-guided correction and scaffolding of contigs.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold ref [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the approach of RagTag (Alonge M et al. 2022, Genome Biol 23:258: correct, then order and orient by alignment to a related genome, then merge solutions), reimplemented with these differences:

  • evidence from several references at once: every reference adds weighted adjacencies between contig ends to one scaffold graph (in a single step), and the scaffolds are its best paths (strongest adjacencies first, no cycles), so references that disagree are outvoted rather than run one after another; other evidence (Hi-C join scores) enters the same graph;
  • correction by colinear chains: alignments of a contig are chained (same chromosome and strand, colinear within max_gap); a contig is cut between two chains of at least min_chain bp that go to different chromosomes or far-apart places, at the middle of the unaligned stretch between them, and only where at least min_refs references agree (so a rearrangement of one reference does not break a correct contig);
  • haplotigs: contigs whose reference span lies inside a longer contig's span are allelic copies and are left unplaced (--keep-contained places them as alternate scaffolds);
  • gaps are the reference distance between neighbours (100 N when unknown or overlapping).

Alignment by minimap2 (Li H 2018, Bioinformatics 34:3094):

mcscan3 scaffold ref contigs.fa --ref close.fa --ref other.fa:0.5 -o asm --correct

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference FASTA, optionally path:weight; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --correct Cut misjoins supported by the alignments. --min-refs References that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --preset minimap2 preset: asm5, asm10 or asm20. (default: asm10) --keep-contained Place haplotigs inside other contigs too. --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold review
docs.text:
Interactive Hi-C contact map for reviewing and curating an assembly.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold review [OPTIONS] CONTACTS_ AGP

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: one self-contained HTML page (contacts embedded as binary arrays, map drawn on a <canvas>; no server, no install). The .assembly layout format follows Dudchenko O et al. 2018, bioRxiv 254797 (see also Durand NC et al. 2016, Cell Syst 3:99):

  • the contact map of the scaffolds, with scaffold (blue) and contig piece (green) outlines; scroll to zoom, drag to pan, hover for positions and counts, a slider for the colour range;
  • curation: click a piece to select it (shift-click for a range), then invert (I), move (M, then click where it goes), cut (C, then click where to cut), mark as debris (D), split/join scaffolds at a piece boundary (B, then click), undo (Z); every edit redraws the map from the new layout at once;
  • export of the curated assembly as AGP and as an .assembly layout; scaffold apply turns either back into AGP and FASTA. .assembly layouts from other Hi-C review tools load here too:
mcscan3 scaffold review asm.contacts.npz asm.agp -o asm.review.html
mcscan3 scaffold apply contigs.fa asm.review.assembly -o asm.curated

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTACTS_ Contacts of scaffold contacts (.npz). AGP AGP of the assembly (or an .assembly layout).

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold run
docs.text:
Scaffolding with all evidence at once: references, genetic maps and Hi-C.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold run [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each kind of evidence proposes cuts (misjoins) and adjacencies between contig ends:

  • references: collinear-chain misjoins and neighbours along every reference chromosome (scaffold ref);
  • genetic maps: linkage-group switches and neighbours in the map order (scaffold map); joins to pieces the maps cannot orient count half;
  • Hi-C: contact-drop misjoins (scaffold hic) and, for every contig end, its best partner by close contacts when the choice is mutual, weighted by how clearly it beats the second best.

All cuts are made (nearby cuts of different sources merged), all adjacencies go into one scaffold graph with their weights (--ref x.fa:w, --map m.tsv:w, --hic-weight), and the scaffolds are its best paths (strongest first, no cycles). Adjacencies proposed but not used with at least half the weight of the chosen join are reported as conflicts, with their sources:

mcscan3 scaffold run contigs.fa --ref close.fa --map f2.tsv --pairs hic.pairs.gz -o asm

Writes AGP, FASTA, <prefix>.joins.tsv (every join and the sources supporting it) and <prefix>.conflicts.tsv.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference FASTA, optionally path:weight; repeat. --map Genetic map markers, optionally path:weight; repeat. --contacts Hi-C contacts (.npz). --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM). --hic-weight Weight of Hi-C joins. (default: 1.0) --groups Chromosomes, for the Hi-C layout (default: from --ref or --map). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --correct Cut misjoins. --min-refs References that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --preset minimap2 preset. (default: asm10) --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 sex coverage
docs.text:
Read depth of males against females along a reference, without alignment.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex coverage [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the coverage scans of findZX (Sigeman H et al. 2022, BMC Genomics 23:328; github.com/hsigeman/findZX) and SexFindR, computed from k-mers instead of alignments. Where the Y has lost its genes or diverged beyond recognition, the X is single-copy in males: males have half the female depth (log2 M:F = -1). Sequence of the Y present in a male reference has depth in males and none in females. ZW systems show the mirror image.

  • the sampled k-mers that occur once in the reference are looked up in every sample's k-mer counts (the same counts as sex kmers); counts are divided by the sample's genome-wide median, so samples of any depth compare;
  • per window: the median normalised depth of every sample, the mean over males and over females, and log2_mf = log2((males + 0.05) / (females + 0.05)); windows with fewer than --min-kmers unique k-mers are left out.

Writes <prefix>.coverage.windows.tsv (log2 M:F, male and female depth per window).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --samples, -s Samples: nameM --reference, -r Reference FASTA. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --window, -w Window size (bp). (default: 100000) --k k-mer length. (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash; 1 keeps all). (default: 10) --min-kmers Fewest unique reference k-mers in a window. (default: 20) --min-len Leave out reference sequences shorter than this (bp). (default: 0) --cache Directory keeping each sample's k-mer counts between runs. --cpus Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 sex haplotypes
docs.text:
Sex chromosomes from the two haplotypes of one individual.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex haplotypes [OPTIONS] HAP1 HAP2

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after SCINKD (github.com/DrPintoThe2nd/SCINKD): in a haplotype-resolved assembly of the heterogametic sex (an XY male or a ZW female), the X and Y (Z and W) differ along the non-recombining region, while autosome haplotypes differ only at heterozygous sites. The share of k-mers of one haplotype missing from the other therefore rises along the sex-determining region.

  • sampled k-mers (one in --scaled) of hap1 that are absent from hap2 are counted per window of hap1 (per 1,000 sampled k-mers); swap the haplotypes for hap2 coordinates;
  • every chromosome gets its mean density and its longest run of windows above the genome-wide 95th percentile; the chromosome with the highest robust z-score is the candidate sex chromosome.

Writes <prefix>.haplotypes.windows.tsv (hap1 coordinates) and <prefix>.haplotypes.chroms.tsv.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description HAP1 Haplotype 1 of the heterogametic sex (FASTA). HAP2 Haplotype 2 (FASTA).

docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --window, -w Window size (bp). (default: 100000) --k k-mer length. (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash; 1 keeps all). (default: 10) --min-len Leave out sequences of hap1 shorter than this (bp). (default: 1000000) --cpus Threads (default: all).

docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). Density of haplotype-specific k-mers per window, robust z per chromosome, longest high run; after SCINKD (github.com/DrPintoThe2nd/SCINKD).

docs.title: mcscan3 sex kmers
docs.text:
Sex-specific k-mers from reads of males and females.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex kmers [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the sex-specific k-mer scans of SDRscan (github.com/hafizmtalha/SDRscan), CBS-tools (github.com/HudsonAlpha/CBS-tools), SexFindR (Grayson P et al. 2022, bioRxiv 2022.02.21.481346) and Akagi T et al. 2014 (Science 346:646, persimmon). A Y (or W) chromosome carries sequence that the X (or Z) lacks or that has diverged from it, so in an XY species some k-mers are found in every male and in no female; in a ZW species, in every female and no male.

  • each read set (--samples: name<TAB>M|F<TAB>reads[,reads]) is reduced to its sampled k-mers (FracMinHash, one in --scaled) with counts; k-mers seen fewer than --min-count times are read errors;
  • male-specific k-mers: present in at least --frac of the males and in no female (female- specific the other way round). The heterogametic sex has many more specific k-mers; the ratio gives the system (XY, ZW, or undetermined below --min-ratio);
  • on a reference (--reference), the density of specific k-mers per window (per 1,000 sampled k-mers) locates Y- or W-derived sequence; specific k-mers absent from the reference are counted as unplaced (a reference from the homogametic sex has no Y or W);
  • --reads-out: the reads of the first sample of the heterogametic sex that hold at least two specific k-mers, for assembling the sex-specific sequence.

Writes <prefix>.kmers.windows.tsv (density per window), <prefix>.kmers.json (counts, system).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --samples, -s Samples: nameM --prefix, -o Output prefix. --reference, -r Reference FASTA for the density per window. --window, -w Window size (bp). (default: 100000) --k k-mer length. (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash; 1 keeps all). (default: 10) --min-count Times a k-mer is seen in a sample to count as present. (default: 2) --frac Share of the sex a specific k-mer must be found in. (default: 0.8) --min-ratio Excess of one sex's specific k-mers to call XY or ZW. (default: 3.0) --reads-out Write reads with specific k-mers (FASTA) for assembly. --min-len Leave out reference sequences shorter than this (bp). (default: 0) --cache Directory keeping each sample's k-mer counts between runs. --cpus Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 sex rad
docs.text:
Sex-linked markers from RAD-seq (or any reduced-representation) reads, with no reference.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex rad [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after RADSex (Feron R et al. 2021, Mol Ecol Resour 21:1715). Reads of a RAD library start at a restriction site, so identical read starts from many individuals are one locus.

  • every read is cut to its first --length bases (default: the shortest read, at most 100); reads with N are dropped. A marker is one such sequence; an individual has it when it was read at least --min-depth times;
  • for every marker, the number of males and of females that have it; the table of markers by (males, females) is the RADSex distribution (<prefix>.rad.distribution.tsv);
  • each marker is tested for association with sex (two-sided Fisher's exact test on presence in males and females), corrected by Bonferroni over the markers present in at least --min-individuals; (--correction bh for Benjamini-Hochberg). With few individuals no marker can pass (6 males and 6 females give at best P = 0.002 before correction), so markers present in at least --frac of one sex and in none of the other are counted too;
  • markers significant (or, without any, specific) and present mostly in males point to XY, mostly in females to ZW; <prefix>.rad.markers.fa holds the significant markers (to place on a genome, e.g. with BLAST or wga), <prefix>.rad.tsv their counts and P values.

docs.text: Argument Description

(default: 0) --min-depth Reads of a marker for an individual to have it. (default: 1) --min-individuals Individuals with a marker to test it. (default: 2) --alpha Significance after correction. (default: 0.05) --correction bonferroni or bh. (default: bonferroni) --frac Share of a sex for a marker to be specific to it. (default: 0.8) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 sex run
docs.text:
Sex chromosomes and the sex-determining region from every line of evidence at hand.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex run [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each line of evidence has its own command; sex run takes whatever data there is and combines it on one set of reference windows:

============== ============================================== =========================================== evidence data signal of sex linkage in a window ============== ============================================== =========================================== kmers whole-genome reads of males and females density of k-mers specific to one sex coverage the same reads and a reference male:female depth away from 1 (log2 M:F) vcf genotypes of sexed individuals sites fitting XY/ZW inheritance; F_ST, het. haplotypes a phased assembly of the heterogametic sex k-mers of one haplotype missing in the other rad RAD-seq reads (no reference needed) sex-associated markers (reported on their own) ============== ============================================== ===========================================

System. Each evidence calls XY, ZW or undetermined (more male- than female-specific k-mers, heterozygous males, males at half depth: XY; the mirror image: ZW). The run takes the majority of the calls that are not undetermined; --system overrides it.

Combined score. Each signal is oriented for the system (k-mers specific to the heterogametic sex; |log2 M:F|; sex-linked sites of the system's type, F_ST between the sexes and |log2| heterozygosity of the heterogametic sex over the homogametic: an excess where the Y has diverged, a deficit where it was lost) and turned into a robust z-score over all windows (median and MAD). The combined score of a window is the mean z of the evidence available there.

Regions. Windows with a combined score of at least --min-score are joined into regions (gaps of up to --max-gap windows bridged, at least --min-windows windows kept); every region lists the evidence above --min-score in it. The chromosome holding the most region length is the candidate sex chromosome. Feed the region to ks strata (with X-Y gene pairs) for its strata.

Writes <prefix>.windows.tsv (every signal, z-scores and the combined score per window), <prefix>.regions.tsv, <prefix>.json, <prefix>.<format> (one track per evidence along the genome, regions shaded) and the outputs of each evidence (<prefix>.vcf.sites.tsv, <prefix>.rad.*, ...).

docs.text: Argument Description

(default: 100000) --k k-mer length. (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash; 1 keeps all). (default: 10) --min-count Times a k-mer is seen in a sample to count as present. (default: 2) --frac Share of the sex a specific k-mer must be found in. (default: 0.8) --min-score Combined robust z-score of a window in a region. (default: 3.0) --max-gap Windows below the score bridged inside a region. (default: 1) --min-windows Fewest windows above the score in a region. (default: 2) --min-len Leave out reference sequences shorter than this (bp). (default: 0) --cache Directory keeping each sample's k-mer counts between runs. --cpus Threads (default: all). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 sex simulate
docs.text:
A population with sex chromosomes of known structure, for testing the sex commands.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex simulate [OPTIONS] OUTDIR

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Chromosomes of random sequence carry SNPs at population frequencies drawn from a Beta(0.5, 0.5); the first chromosome is the sex chromosome. Inside its sex-determining region the Y (or W) is a single non-recombining haplotype with fixed differences from the X: an old stratum (divergence --old), a young stratum (--young), a stretch the Y lost (males hemizygous) and a Y-specific insertion absent from the X. For each individual it writes

  • whole-genome reads (FASTQ, --coverage over both haplotypes, --error per base);
  • RAD-seq reads: 80 bp from restriction sites (every ~2 kb on average) of both haplotypes;
  • one VCF of every individual's genotypes at SNPs and at the X-Y differences;
  • the two haplotypes of the first individual of the heterogametic sex (hap1: X or Z; hap2: Y or W);
  • the reference (the ancestral sequence: what an assembly of the homogametic sex looks like);
  • samples.tsv and rad_samples.tsv for sex run, and truth.json.

(default: 5) --length Chromosome length (bp). (default: 200000) --coverage Whole-genome read depth per individual. (default: 8.0) --old X-Y divergence of the old stratum. (default: 0.08) --young X-Y divergence of the young stratum. (default: 0.015) --seed Random seed. (default: 1)

docs.title: mcscan3 sex vcf
docs.text:
Sex-linked sites from genotypes of sexed individuals.

Group sex · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sex vcf [OPTIONS] VCF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after SDpop (Käfer J et al. 2021, Genetics 218:iyab053; gitlab.in2p3.fr/ sex-det-family/sdpop) and the heterozygosity and F_ST scans of findZX and SexFindR. Individuals are sampled from a population and sexed (--samples: name<TAB>M|F); the VCF holds their genotypes (biallelic SNPs; any caller, RAD-seq or whole-genome).

Inheritance models, fitted to the genotype counts of females and males at every site, with a genotyping error rate --error (a wrong call goes to either other genotype):

  • autosomal: both sexes in Hardy-Weinberg proportions with one allele frequency;
  • XY: females X/X in Hardy-Weinberg with the X frequency; males X/Y with the Y fixed for one allele (it does not recombine), so males are heterozygous where X and Y differ;
  • X-hemizygous: the Y lost the gene; males show one allele (called homozygous);
  • ZW and Z-hemizygous: the same with the sexes swapped.

Allele frequencies are fitted by maximum likelihood (a grid), models compared by BIC, and the BIC weights give each site's probability of sex linkage. A site is sex-linked when that probability is at least --min-prob and it is informative (at least one heterozygote, and at least --min-called called individuals of each sex).

Windows (of --window bp, or the reference windows in sex run): sites, sex-linked sites by model, observed heterozygosity of each sex, and Hudson's F_ST between the sexes. The system is called from the excess of XY over ZW sites (or the reverse).

Writes <prefix>.vcf.sites.tsv (sex-linked sites with their model and probability), <prefix>.vcf.windows.tsv and <prefix>.vcf.json.

docs.text: Argument Description VCF VCF (or .vcf.gz) of the sexed individuals.

(default: 0.01) --min-prob Probability of sex linkage to call a site. (default: 0.95) --min-called Fewest called individuals of each sex at a site. (default: 3)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome assign
docs.text:
Assign the chromosomes of a polyploid to subgenomes by homology to progenitors.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome assign [OPTIONS] POLY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. In an allopolyploid each subgenome descends from a different parent, so its genes are closest to the genes of that parent's living relative (the progenitor-like diploid). Given anchors between the polyploid and each progenitor-like genome (e.g. ortholog run):

  1. gene votes: every polyploid gene with a syntenic partner votes for the progenitor whose partner is closest: the highest anchor score (third column of the anchors, a BLAST score), or the lowest Ks when --ks NAME=FILE gives the pairs' Ks (wgd ksd TSV, gene1, gene2, ks columns). Votes closer than --margin (relative score difference) abstain;
  2. segments: votes are smoothed along each chromosome (sliding majority, --smooth genes each side) and runs shorter than --min-run genes are merged, as in ancestral karyotype;
  3. chromosomes: each chromosome gets the subgenome of most of its genes, with the share as a confidence (homoeologous exchanges show as mixed chromosomes):
mcscan3 subgenome assign bnapus --bed-dir data --progenitor brapa=bnapus.brapa.anchors \
    --progenitor bole=bnapus.bole.anchors -o bnapus

Writes <prefix>.genes.tsv (gene, chromosome, vote, scores), <prefix>.segments.tsv, <prefix>.chromosomes.tsv (chromosome, subgenome, share, votes per progenitor) and the figure <prefix>.<format>: the polyploid's chromosomes coloured by subgenome.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description POLY Polyploid genome name (.bed in --bed-dir).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --progenitor NAME=ANCHORS: anchors between the polyploid and a progenitor-like genome. --bed-dir Directory of .bed. (default: .) --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ks NAME=FILE: Ks of the pairs (wgd ksd TSV) instead of scores. --margin Votes with a smaller relative score gap abstain. (default: 0.02) --smooth Sliding-majority window (genes each side). (default: 15) --min-run Shortest segment (genes; at least 1% of a chromosome). (default: 40) --min-frac Leave out sequences with fewer genes than this fraction (0: keep all scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome circos
docs.text:
Circular summary of phased subgenomes.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome circos [OPTIONS] PREFIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Reads the outputs of subgenome phase under one prefix and draws, for any number of subgenomes, every line of evidence on one circle. The chromosomes sit on the circle grouped by subgenome and, inside a subgenome, by homoeologous set, so the copies of one ancestral chromosome sit at the same place in each group. Rings, numbered from the outside in (each drawn only when its input exists):

  1. consensus: each chromosome painted window by window with its consensus subgenome, so homoeologous exchanges show as a patch of another colour (black triangle outside);
  2. lines of evidence: one thin ring per line (k-mers, homology, Ks, fractionation, ...), the subgenome each line calls in every window (<prefix>.consensus.windows.tsv);
  3. k-mer enrichment: windows significantly enriched for the k-mers specific to one subgenome (binomial test of subgenome kmer), in that subgenome's colour;
  4. specific k-mers, one ring per subgenome: each window's density of its specific k-mers over the genome-wide mean, as a share of the same for all subgenomes;
  5. specific LTR retrotransposons: their density per window, stacked by subgenome (<prefix>.repeats.elements.tsv);
  6. all LTR retrotransposons: their density per window;
  7. genes: gene density per window (--bed);
  8. retention: gene retention of each phased unit (<prefix>.retention.units.tsv);
  9. inside, links: syntenic blocks between chromosomes of different subgenomes coloured by their median Ks (--anchors, --ks), or, without them, a ribbon between the units of every homoeologous set.

Chromosome names come from --names (sequence and name; chr1 is shown as 1) or from <bed>.chroms.tsv, written by pipeline inputs; otherwise long accessions are shortened. Under the circle, the key, the insertion ages of the subgenome-specific LTR retrotransposons and the bootstrap support of each chromosome's k-mer assignment:

mcscan3 subgenome circos phase/poly --bed poly.bed --anchors poly.poly.anchors --ks poly.poly.ks.tsv

docs.text: Argument Description PREFIX Prefix of the subgenome phase outputs (.consensus.tsv, ...).

(default: 10) --max-chroms Largest sequences to draw. (default: 60) --names Chromosome names: sequence and name per line (default: .chroms.tsv). --key Key and insets below the circle or right of it (landscape). (default: below) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome consensus
docs.text:
Subgenomes called from several independent lines of evidence.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome consensus [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each way of telling subgenomes apart can fail on its own: repeat k-mers fade in old polyploids, progenitor homology needs living relatives of both parents, Ks to the progenitors blurs when they were close, and biased fractionation exists only when one subgenome dominates. MCscan3 asks every available line of evidence and reports where they agree:

  • k-mers (--kmer, subgenome kmer): the subgenome of each chromosome or segment from its repeat k-mers, weighted by its bootstrap support; windows (<prefix>.kmer.windows.tsv next to it) paint the chromosomes;
  • homology (--assign NAME=GENES, subgenome assign): the progenitor-like genome closest to most genes of a unit (by anchor score), weighted by the share of genes that agree;
  • Ks (--assign NAME=GENES of subgenome assign --ks): the same with the lowest Ks;
  • fractionation (--homoeologs, subgenome homoeologs): the least and more fractionated member of each homoeologous set (LF, MF1...), weighted by how much their retention differs.

Every line of evidence uses its own labels (SG1, a progenitor name, LF). They are matched to one set of names (progenitor names when homology is given, else k-mer subgenomes) by the optimal matching of their co-occurrence over the units. Each unit then gets the label with the most weighted votes, under the constraint that the members of a homoeologous set go to different subgenomes, and a status: agree (all lines), majority, conflict (no majority) or single (one line). Windows along the chromosomes are painted the same way from k-mer windows and gene votes; runs of windows against their unit's subgenome, supported by two lines of evidence, are reported as homoeologous exchanges.

(default: 1000000) --min-genes Fewest gene votes for a unit or window. (default: 5) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome fractionation
docs.text:
Biased fractionation of a polyploid against an unduplicated relative.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome fractionation [OPTIONS] ANCHORS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the analyses of Thomas et al. (2006), Schnable et al. (2011, PNAS, maize) and Cheng et al. (2012, PLoS ONE, Brassica rapa). After a polyploidy, duplicated genes are lost (fractionated). When one parental subgenome keeps more genes than the other, fractionation is biased: a sign of allopolyploidy and of subgenome dominance.

Input: anchors between a reference genome that did not share the polyploidy (ref) and the polyploid (poly), e.g. from ortholog run --quota 1:2 for a tetraploid. Each block of the polyploid covers an interval of the reference:

  1. retention of a block: the share of reference genes in its interval that have a partner in the block (the genes kept by that copy);
  2. ranks: at every reference gene, the covering blocks (at most --copies) are ranked by retention: LF (least fractionated), MF1, MF2...;
  3. windows: the retention of each rank along every reference chromosome (--window reference genes, centred on each gene with any copy);
  4. bias test: ranking by retention alone makes LF look better than MF even without bias. The null keeps every reference gene's number of kept copies but shuffles which copies keep them (--permutations), and re-ranks. The p-value is the share of shuffles whose LF - MF1 retention difference is at least the observed one:
mcscan3 subgenome fractionation ath.brapa.anchors --ref-bed ath.bed --poly-bed brapa.bed --copies 3 -o brapa

Writes <prefix>.genes.tsv (reference gene, then the polyploid gene or . for each rank), <prefix>.blocks.tsv (block, polyploid and reference intervals, retention, majority rank), <prefix>.windows.tsv and the figure <prefix>.<format>; prints the summary.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORS Anchors between the reference and the polyploid.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref-bed BED of the unduplicated reference. --poly-bed BED of the polyploid. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --copies Copies expected per reference region (2 tetraploid, 3 hexaploid). (default: 2) --window Window (reference genes) of the retention curves. (default: 100) --permutations Shuffles for the bias test (0: no test). (default: 200) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome homoeologs
docs.text:
Homoeologous chromosome sets and segments of a polyploid.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome homoeologs [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Phasing by differential k-mers needs the sets of homoeologous chromosomes, one from each subgenome; SubPhaser (Jia KH et al. 2022, New Phytol 235:801) asks the user to write them. MCscan3 finds them from synteny, in one of two ways:

  • self (--self ANCHORS, a polyploid against itself): chromosomes are linked by their syntenic gene pairs; each chromosome's homoeologs are its --copies - 1 partners with the most pairs, kept when the choice is mutual and, with --ks, when the pairs' median Ks is within --ks-max (pairs of an older duplication have larger Ks). Linked chromosomes form a set. This suits recent polyploids whose chromosomes kept their identity (wheat, cotton, Brassica napus);
  • reference (--ref ANCHORS --ref-bed, an unduplicated relative against the polyploid, e.g. ortholog run --quota 1:2): every stretch of a reference chromosome covered by exactly --copies polyploid blocks gives a set of --copies segments (chrom:start-end). This suits old polyploids whose subgenomes are mixed along the chromosomes (maize, soybean), where whole chromosomes cannot be phased. Each segment is ranked by its gene retention against the reference (LF, least fractionated, then MF1...), as in subgenome fractionation.

With --ks (gene1, gene2, ks table of the same pairs), the median Ks of every set is reported; between homoeologs it dates the divergence of the progenitors.

Writes <prefix>.sets.txt (one set per line, for subgenome kmer --sets) and <prefix>.homoeologs.tsv (set, unit, chromosome, start, end, genes, retention, rank, Ks).

(default: 2) --ks Ks of the anchor pairs (gene1, gene2, ks columns). --ks-max Largest median Ks of homoeologs (--self; 0: automatic). (default: 0.0) --min-genes Fewest gene pairs linking homoeologs. docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome kmer
docs.text:
Subgenomes of a polyploid from differential k-mers.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome kmer [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, a clean-room implementation of phasing by differential repeat k-mers as described for SubPhaser (Jia KH et al. 2022, New Phytol 235:801): while the progenitors of an allopolyploid were apart, each gained its own bursts of transposable elements, so some repeat k-mers are far more common on the chromosomes from one progenitor. Homoeologous chromosomes share their genes but not these k-mers, so the k-mers that differ inside every set of homoeologs separate the subgenomes.

  1. counting: canonical k-mers (--k, default 15) of every chromosome, in parallel, in chunks; counts are per Mb of ACGT sequence so that chromosome size does not matter;
  2. differential k-mers: k-mers seen at least --min-count times in the genome whose normalised count on one chromosome of a homoeologous set is at least --fold times that on every other chromosome of the set, in at least --min-sets of the sets;
  3. clustering: chromosomes are clustered on the standardised counts of these k-mers by k-means (as many clusters as subgenomes) constrained by the homoeologous sets: the members of a set go to different subgenomes (optimal assignment per set), which the unconstrained clustering of SubPhaser does not enforce; both are reported. --bootstrap resamples the k-mers to give each chromosome a support;
  4. subgenome-specific k-mers: differential k-mers higher on the chromosomes of one subgenome (--fold and a Welch t-test on log counts, Benjamini-Hochberg q below --alpha) and top on that subgenome's member in at least --min-sets of the sets;
  5. painting: windows (--window bp) along every sequence are assigned to the subgenome whose specific k-mers they are enriched for (binomial test against the genome-wide shares); windows that disagree with their chromosome mark candidate homoeologous exchanges.

The homoeologous sets come from --sets (one set per line, chromosome names separated by spaces or tabs, as written by subgenome homoeologs).

docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA of the polyploid (plain or gzipped).

(default: 15) --min-count Fewest occurrences of a k-mer in the genome. (default: 200) --fold Least fold difference inside a homoeologous set. (default: 2.0) --min-sets Share of the sets in which a k-mer must differ. (default: 1.0) --subgenomes Number of subgenomes (0: the largest set). (default: 0) --bootstrap Resamplings of the k-mers for support (0: none). (default: 200) --window Window for painting the chromosomes (bp). (default: 1000000) --alpha False discovery rate of specific k-mers and windows. (default: 0.05) --cpus Parallel processes. (default: 4) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)
